features.title: Lock Merged to Pentatonic
features.summary: Restrict merged notes to Mosaic’s scale-specific five-note selection. Default: On.
features.prose:
Lock merged to pent. is On by default. A merge mode combines the notes of several patterns; this option restricts the result to Mosaic's five-note selection for the selected scale. Example in C major with pattern 1 on degrees I, III, V, VII and pattern 2 on III, V, VII, I: Average merge gives degrees II, IV, VI, IV. With Off you hear 62, 65, 69, 65 (D F A F). With On, F is not in the major selection and snaps to the nearer E, so you hear 62, 64, 69, 64.

The selections use one-based degrees of each named seven-note scale:
- Major and Harmonic Major: 1/2/3/5/6.
- Minor, Harmonic Minor and Melodic Minor: 1/3/4/5/7.
- Dorian: 1/2/4/5/7.
- Phrygian: 1/3/4/6/7.
- Lydian: 2/3/5/6/7.
- Mixolydian: 1/2/4/5/6.
- Locrian: 2/3/4/6/7.

Apply the named scale's alterations to these degrees. The selection does not always retain the tonic or avoid semitones.

Merged values remain seven-note scale degrees, not five-note indices. Their scale pitches snap to the nearest selected pitch across repeated octaves. An exact tie selects the lower pitch. Snapping can cross an octave boundary.

For example, Lydian C snaps to the B below it. Melodic Minor A snaps down to G rather than the equally distant B.

The scale root is used when set; otherwise, the song root is used. The effective octave offset is applied afterward.
features.musical_use: Leave On so merge results stay inside the five-note selection; turn Off to hear the merge results unchanged.

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select Lock merged to pent.. Change its value.
controls.result: On snaps merged scale degrees to Mosaic’s scale-specific five-note selection; the lower pitch wins exact ties and snapping can cross octaves. Default: On.

recipes.title: Compare merged notes with and without the filter
recipes.text:
Lock merged to pent. is On by default. Merge modes can produce notes that no pattern contains, such as an average between two degrees; this option snaps those results onto the five-note version of the scale. Use this recipe to hear the difference.

Starting point: channel 1 is empty and the scale is C major.

1. Build pattern 1 on degrees I, III, V, VII (C E G B) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 on III, V, VII, I (E G B C) on steps 1 to 4, as in Build a phrase, and pattern 3 as a velocity source (four trigs on steps 1 to 4, never assigned to the channel). Both note patterns have a trig on all four steps.

2. Assign both patterns to channel 1 with (1,2) and (2,2).

3. Choose the merge modes. Both patterns trig on the same steps, and the default trig merge, Skip, silences steps that trig in more than one pattern, so set the trig merge to All: press the trig merge button (14,8) until Channel tasks > Merge modes shows ALL. Check that the note merge reads AVERAGE; the average of each pair of degrees is II, IV, VI, IV (D, F, A, F).

4. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Tap Play: 62, 65, 69, 65 (D, F, A, F). Tap Play to stop.

5. Turn Lock merged to pent. On and play again: 62, 64, 69, 64. The two F notes become E, because F is not in the pentatonic.

recipes.title: Play a minor scale on the white keys
recipes.text:
Starting point: a MIDI keyboard is connected to Mosaic's MIDI input on port 1, channel 1 has a device selected (it plays through the test or your own synth) and the scale is C major. The norns names MIDI 60 as C3, so the key you call middle C sounds 60.

2. Open the Scale Editor (4,8). Turn E2 to Scale, turn E3 to natural minor and press K3 to apply it. Return to the Channel editor (3,8).

3. Play C to C on the white keys again: 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72. The keyboard keeps its layout while the scale underneath it has changed.

features.title: UI Motion
features.summary: Enable decorative screen motion. Default: On. This setting does not change sequencer timing or input.
features.prose:
UI motion is On by default. It controls the decorative animation of the norns screen only; it never changes sequencer timing, input or the notes you hear. With Off the screen is still.

With On, a miniature graphic in the header identifies the screen and moves with the music: while playing it follows the sequencer's transport pulses, while stopped it follows the selected norns musical clock without starting playback. With Off, or if the clock is missing or invalid, it holds its rest pose. The start-up animation, the shadow that glides across the Masks and Trig params grids, values that roll into place, the characters on some screens and the small dial beside a single numeric value are decoration and are governed by the same setting.

Only the selected label or value that is too long for its row scrolls right to left. Fitting labels, neighbouring rows, the title and controls stay still. A long selected value first gets its own full-width row. With motion Off, shortened text ends in ~, and an exact value that cannot fit shows LAYOUT OVERFLOW instead of silently changing.

The light running round the Mosaic mark, the shadow gliding across the Masks and Trig params grids (diagonally when it changes row) and values rolling into place all stop with motion Off. The Rhythm Doctor dances to the tempo of the captured bank, and the Merge Shape garden sways and the Harmony choir bobs while the sequencer plays. Motion never delays input and never hides a value for more than a moment.
features.musical_use: Turn Off for a calm, still screen, or when photographing or filming the display; leave On for animated feedback.

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select UI motion. Change its value.
controls.result: Off keeps the screen still; On enables decorative motion and musical characters without changing input or sequencer timing. Default: On.

details.title: Selected overflow text
details.text: Overflow scrolling is restricted to the selected label or value. Fitting text and neighboring rows remain stationary. Off stops scrolling; ~ indicates shortened text, and exact values that cannot fit report LAYOUT OVERFLOW.

details.title: Miniature header timing
details.text: Playing uses musical sequencer transport position. Stopped uses the selected musical clock and does not start Mosaic or sound notes. Off or missing/invalid clock holds the rest pose. Native PARAMS owns its own screen.

recipes.title: Compare the screen with motion Off and On
recipes.text:
Use this to see what the setting does before you film or photograph the display. Changing a value only makes the screen react: the point is the header mark.
1. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select UI motion in the Screen section and turn E3 to Off.
2. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, select Clock and press K3. Turn E3 to /1.5 and press K3, then restore /1. All values stay readable and the header mark does not move.
3. Return to PARAMS, set UI motion to On, and repeat. The header mark now animates; values are as readable as before.
4. Play the pattern in each setting. The notes and timing are identical.

Mosaic supports Matrix mod and toolkit. Matrix routes modulation sources to device parameters; toolkit supplies LFOs and other rhythmic modulators.

features.title: Musical Merge and Voice Leading
features.summary: Foundation and Fragments reshape merged output without rewriting patterns. Harmony places output voices; its default is Off.
features.prose:
Merge Shape changes a channel’s merged rhythm. Harmony places output notes in specified registers. Neither feature rewrites source patterns. Older projects restore their saved Skip, Only or All Strategy and retain its original MIDI, timing and random behavior. Foundation and Fragments are other exclusive choices of the same Strategy selector.

Merge modes, Merge Shape and Harmony are consecutive Channel tasks. Merge Shape and Voice leading use vertical lists. Editable rows display their current value. Submenus display OPEN >. The selected row is marked >.

1. Open Merge Shape or Harmony from Channel tasks.
2. Turn E2 to select a row.
3. Turn E3 to change a staged value.
4. Press K3 on OPEN > to open that settings list. The bottom line names the action, for example K3 OPEN RHYTHM.
5. Press K3 on an ordinary value row to validate and apply the complete draft.

Action rows, including Create group, Four-part smooth, Delete group and Reset map, display a plain >. Delete group and Reset map require confirmation.

Press K2 to discard a dirty draft, or to return from an opened list to its parent. Turn E1 to return to the feature’s first screen and discard an unapplied draft. From the first screen, E1 returns to Channel tasks.

A stopped edit applies immediately. During playback, Merge Shape displays NEXT CYCLE and applies before the next channel-cycle onset. Harmony displays NEXT PATTERN and applies at the next global pattern boundary. Stop activates the latest applied request for the next start.

Merge Shape shows a read-only Strategy summary. Its Strategy selector action discards an unapplied parameter draft and opens the shared selector on Merge modes. Grid (14,8) selects the same Skip, Only, All, Foundation and Fragments choices. A strategy request is immediate; parameter drafts still need K3 Apply. Active is sounding output, while Pending is an accepted request awaiting its displayed boundary.
features.musical_use: Use Merge Shape to add or remove channel trigs without editing the assigned patterns. Use Harmony to set output registers.

controls.gesture: In Channel tasks, turn E2 to Merge Shape or Harmony. Press K3.
controls.result: The selected feature opens.

controls.gesture: Turn E2.
controls.result: The selected row changes.

controls.result: The draft value changes.

controls.result: The selected settings list opens.

controls.gesture: Press K3 on a value row.
controls.result: Mosaic validates and applies the draft.

controls.gesture: Press K2.
controls.result: A dirty draft is discarded. In an opened settings list, the parent list returns.

controls.gesture: Turn E1.
controls.result: An unapplied draft is discarded and the feature’s first screen returns. From that screen, Channel tasks returns.

details.title: Applying changes
details.text: Stopped edits apply immediately. During playback, Merge Shape normally displays NEXT CYCLE and applies at the next channel-cycle onset. Harmony displays NEXT PATTERN and applies at the next global pattern boundary. A shared group-reference change can also queue Merge Shape for NEXT PATTERN. Stop settles the latest applied request.

details.title: Source patterns
details.text: E3 edits a draft until K3 applies it. Grid editing can cancel a dirty draft. Merge Shape and Harmony change channel output; they do not rewrite source patterns.

features.title: Merge Shape
features.summary: Foundation keeps one anchor pattern’s trigs and adds a repeatable selection of trigs from the other assigned patterns; Phrase changes how many additions play from loop to loop.
features.prose:
Merge Shape turns several assigned patterns into one channel part. The Anchor pattern’s trigs always play. Trigs from the other assigned patterns are additions: Merge Shape decides how many of them play, how loud, and how close to an anchor. The source patterns are never changed.

Terms used on this page: Anchor is the pattern whose trigs are protected. An addition is a trig from another assigned pattern that Foundation admits. A draft is a set of edits shown on screen but not yet applied; K3 applies it and K2 discards it. Active is the strategy that is sounding, and Pending is a request waiting for its boundary.

[Captured two-cycle Build workflow](#merge-shape/foundation-two-cycle-build)

[Captured Foundation settings and output](#merge-shape/foundation-protected-and-added)

Choose Foundation with the shared Strategy selector on grid (14,8) or Merge modes. Merge Shape shows Strategy as a read-only summary; its Strategy selector action opens Merge modes and discards an unapplied parameter draft. K2 returns with the accepted configuration loaded. Foundation controls trigs only; note, velocity and length merge settings remain active. Choose Skip, Only or All to restore legacy trig merging with retained values. Foundation selects
one assigned pattern as the protected Anchor. Other assigned trig patterns offer
candidate additions at non-anchor steps; overlaps remain one anchor. Amount
admits a deterministic, seed-ranked subset, Accent scales addition velocity, and
Gap suppresses additions within 0–8 circular channel steps of an anchor. Anchor
velocity remains authored. Explicit channel/step masks still win, probability
can still reject an onset, and source patterns are never flattened or changed.

Phrase Cycles can be 1, 2, 4 or 8. Flat, Build, Answer and Fill are stored as
visible per-cycle percentages; changing a percentage makes a Custom curve.
Fixed repeats the same ranked additions. Per phrase changes ranking only after a
complete phrase. Each channel loop advances its own CYCLE counter—even with
polymetric ranges, swing or mute—and Stop restarts at cycle 1.

Keep anchor pitch uses the anchor pattern's relative note on anchor steps before
normal scale conversion. Addition Target can be Legacy, the full effective
scale, selected effective degree indices, or the immutable material of an enabled
Harmony Ensemble group. Targets affect admitted additions only. Note masks,
random shifts and fixed-note operations keep their existing precedence and show
a bypass rather than being quantised twice. Nearest-note ties choose the lower
pitch. A missing/empty target visibly falls back to the legacy pitch.

Foundation ranking is repeatable for the saved seed and grows as a nested set:
raising Amount cannot remove an already selected addition while source, gap,
seed and phrase are unchanged.

Fragments is another shared Strategy choice. Foundation's Interlock and Structure settings remain staged parameter edits: K3 applies the draft, K2 discards it. During playback the shown boundary is NEXT CYCLE, or NEXT PATTERN when applicable. Strategy choices themselves request immediately and do not need K3 Apply.
features.musical_use: Use Foundation to keep one pattern as the spine of a part and vary how many extra notes, and how loud, other patterns add. Use Phrase to build the part up over two to eight loops.

controls.gesture: On Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 to FOUNDATION, or press grid (14,8) until it selects Foundation.
controls.result: A valid assigned anchor allows the request: Active reads FOUNDATION and grid (14,8) brightens. NEEDS ANCHOR leaves the request unapplied and the previous strategy keeps sounding.

controls.gesture: On Merge Shape, select Strategy selector and press K3.
controls.result: An unapplied parameter draft is discarded and the shared selector opens on Merge modes. Strategy itself is read-only on Merge Shape.

controls.gesture: Select Rhythm. Press K3.
controls.result: The Rhythm list opens: Anchor, Add amount, Amount detail, Add accent, Anchor gap, Seed and Interlock.

controls.gesture: Select Phrase. Press K3.
controls.result: The Phrase list opens: Cycles, Shape, one Cycle row per cycle, and Variation.

controls.gesture: On Phrase, select Cycles and turn E3. Then select Shape and turn E3.
controls.result: Cycles steps through 1, 2, 4 and 8. Shape steps through Flat, Build, Answer, Fill and Custom, and the Cycle rows show the stored percentage for each cycle (Build with 2 cycles reads 50 then 100).

controls.gesture: In Foundation, select Pitch. Press K3.
controls.result: Keep anchor, Add target, Target setup and Structure open.

controls.gesture: Press K3 on a value row.
controls.result: The whole draft applies and the footer reads APPLIED. While playing, the footer reads NEXT CYCLE and the edit starts at the next channel loop.

controls.gesture: Press K2.
controls.result: A dirty draft is discarded, or an opened list returns to its parent.

details.title: Anchor and precedence
details.text: Foundation retains anchor velocity. Note, velocity and length merge settings still apply. Explicit masks take precedence. Probability can reject an onset. Source patterns are unchanged.

details.title: Saved trig merge while Foundation is active
details.text: While Foundation is Active, Merge modes shows Active FOUNDATION and Foundation decides the channel's trigs. Your saved Skip, Only or All trig merge setting is kept and is not edited. Choose Skip, Only or All on the Strategy selector to restore it. Note, velocity and length merge rows stay editable.

details.title: Undo
details.text: Applying a Merge Shape draft, including the Interlock and Structure edits made in the same draft, is one step in the channel's Memory. Open History in Channel tasks and turn E3 back one step to restore the previous configuration.

details.title: Amount and variation
details.text: For unchanged source, Gap, Seed and phrase, increasing Amount retains previously admitted additions. Fixed repeats the ranking. Per phrase changes the ranking after a complete phrase.

details.title: Amount, Accent and Phrase do different jobs
details.text: Add amount and the Phrase curve decide how many additions play. Add accent decides how loud they are. Lowering Add accent therefore makes additions quieter without removing any; it does not change the Phrase curve.

recipes.title: Set a two-cycle Build phrase
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: build a part over two loops. Loop 1 plays the anchor line with one extra note. Loop 2 plays the same line with both extra notes.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop at 90 BPM with the default Rate /1, so each step is one sixteenth note (one sixth of a second). Pattern 1 holds C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97). Pattern 2 holds a C on steps 5 and 7, and both patterns are assigned to the channel. Strategy is SKIP.

1. Press E1 to open Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3. The Merge Shape list opens: Strategy, Rhythm, Phrase, Pitch, Result.
2. Select Rhythm with E2 and press K3. The Rhythm list opens with Anchor on the first row.
3. Turn E3 once so Anchor reads 01, then press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Pattern 1 is now the anchor, so its four trigs always play.
4. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until it reads FOUNDATION (or press grid (14,8) until it does). Active reads FOUNDATION. The channel grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7: four anchors and two possible additions.
5. Return to Merge Shape. Select Phrase with E2 and press K3. The Phrase list opens: Cycles, Shape, Variation.
6. Select Cycles and turn E3 once right. Cycles reads 2 and two Cycle rows appear.
7. Select Shape and turn E3 once right, from FLAT to BUILD. Cycle 1 reads 50 and Cycle 2 reads 100, so the first loop admits half of the additions and the second loop admits all of them.
8. Press K3 on a value row. The footer reads APPLIED.
9. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to four loops, then press Stop. Loop 1 plays C D E F and one extra C on step 7; loop 2 plays C D E F and extra Cs on steps 5 and 7; then the two loops repeat. The extra notes play at velocity 70, quieter than the anchors.

What each loop plays (an added C is shown as +C):

Loop 1: steps 1 to 4 C D E F, step 5 rest, step 7 +C.

Loop 2: steps 1 to 4 C D E F, step 5 +C, step 7 +C.

Listen for the loop-to-loop change: the extra C on step 5 is present in every second loop only.

To make the additions quieter or louder without changing how many play, change Add accent in Rhythm.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured two-cycle Build workflow](#merge-shape/foundation-two-cycle-build).

features.title: Fragments
features.summary: Fragments cuts the channel loop into 4-, 8- or 16-step sections and plays each section from one assigned pattern, chosen by a repeatable seed.
features.prose:
[Captured Fragments seed and playback workflow](#fragments/fragments-seed-source-choice)

Fragments is a separate mode for building a phrase from pieces of the assigned
patterns. Choose Fragments with the shared Strategy selector, then open Rhythm from Merge Shape for Size (4,
8 or 16 steps), Keep anchor, Anchor (shown only with Keep anchor) and Seed. The
channel loop is cut into fragments of Size steps counted from the channel's own
start step; the last fragment is shorter when the loop does not divide evenly,
and a loop shorter than Size is one fragment. Fragments never cross the loop end.

Each fragment plays one assigned pattern, chosen repeatably by the Seed: the
same seed always gives the same choice. The fragment keeps that pattern's own
trigs, notes, velocities and lengths exactly, so the legacy trig, note,
velocity and length merge modes and merged-pentatonic do not apply while
Fragments is active. Merge modes marks its retained note, velocity and length rows inactive, with values such as `AVERAGE SAVED`. These rows and their grid buttons do not edit saved values. Choose Skip, Only or All to restore the retained settings. A note longer than the gap to
the next onset on the loop is shortened to that gap. Keep anchor also plays the
Anchor pattern's trigs where the fragment's own pattern has none; where both have
a trig, the fragment's pattern wins. With no assigned pattern the mode falls back
to legacy merging and Result says `ASSIGN PATTERN`.

Phrase shows only Cycles and Variation in this mode. Fixed repeats the same
fragment sources every phrase; Per phrase draws new ones for each phrase.
Shape percentages, Amount, Accent and Gap do not apply. Fragments hides Pitch; choose the adjacent Harmony task directly for voice leading. Explicit masks still win and probability can still reject an
onset. The channel grid shows exactly the trigs the fragments play.
features.musical_use: Use Fragments to build one phrase from sections of several patterns, for example the first half of a sparse pattern and the second half of a busier one, while every section keeps its authored notes, velocities and lengths.

controls.gesture: On Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 to FRAGMENTS, or press grid (14,8) until it selects Fragments.
controls.result: Active reads FRAGMENTS. Fragments owns all four merge attributes, and the note, velocity and length rows on Merge modes show values such as AVERAGE SAVED and are inactive.

controls.gesture: On Merge Shape, select Rhythm. Press K3.
controls.result: The Fragments list opens: Size, Keep anchor, Seed, and Anchor when Keep anchor is ON.

controls.gesture: Select Size. Turn E3.
controls.result: Fragment size changes between 4, 8 and 16 channel steps. A draft is shown until K3 applies it.

controls.gesture: Select Seed. Turn E3.
controls.result: Seed changes from 0 to 65535. The same seed always chooses the same source pattern for each fragment.

controls.gesture: Select Keep anchor. Turn E3.
controls.result: When ON, the Anchor row appears and the anchor pattern’s trigs fill positions where the fragment’s source has no trig.

controls.gesture: Press K3 on a value row.
controls.result: The draft applies and the footer reads APPLIED. The channel grid then shows exactly the trigs the fragments play.

controls.gesture: Select Phrase. Press K3.
controls.result: Cycles and Variation open. Fixed repeats the same fragment sources every phrase; Per phrase draws new ones.

details.title: Loop boundaries
details.text: Fragments start at the channel loop’s start step. The last fragment is shorter when the loop does not divide evenly. A loop shorter than Size is one fragment. Fragments do not cross the loop end.

details.title: Overrides and fallback
details.text: Legacy trig, note, velocity and length merges and merged-pentatonic do not apply in Fragments. Explicit masks and probability still apply. With no assigned pattern, Result displays ASSIGN PATTERN and uses legacy merging.

recipes.title: Set four-step fragments
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: build one phrase from two patterns, taking the first half of the loop from one pattern and the second half from the other. Each half keeps its source notes and velocities.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop at 90 BPM and Rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97). Pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6, and both are assigned to the channel. Strategy is SKIP.

1. Press E1 to open Channel tasks, select Merge modes and press K3. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until it reads FRAGMENTS. Active reads FRAGMENTS. A strategy choice applies at once and needs no K3.
2. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape and press K3. Select Rhythm with E2 and press K3. The Fragments list opens: Size 8, Keep anchor OFF, Seed 0; edits on this list are drafts until you press K3.
3. Select Size and turn E3 once left. Size reads 4, so the loop is cut into two fragments: steps 1 to 4 and steps 5 to 8.
4. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the channel grid lights only step 3, because Seed 0 gives the first fragment to Pattern 2 and the second to Pattern 1, and Pattern 1 has no trigs in the second half.
5. Press Play (grid (1,8)), listen to two loops and press Stop. Each loop plays a single C (MIDI 60) at velocity 100, and Pattern 1’s E on step 3 is not mixed in.
6. Select Seed with E2 and turn E3 once right. Seed reads 1, and a seed always makes the same choice, so Seed 1 gives the first fragment to Pattern 1 and the second to Pattern 2.
7. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the grid lights steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6.
8. Press Play. Each loop plays C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and then Pattern 2’s C on step 6 at velocity 100, then press Stop.

Edits stay drafts until K3, so change Size and Seed first and apply once if you prefer. Turn Keep anchor ON to let the anchor pattern fill empty positions. Open Phrase and set Variation to Per phrase if you want new sources each phrase.

The seed is a repeatable dice roll: seed 0 and seed 1 above give opposite choices for the two halves, and every other seed gives its own choice that always repeats. Try a few more seeds and keep the one you like.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured Fragments seed and playback workflow](#fragments/fragments-seed-source-choice).

features.title: Interlock
features.summary: Interlock removes a follower channel’s Foundation additions that fall within 0 to 4 steps of a leader channel’s anchors.
features.prose:
[Captured Interlock Leader and Window workflow](#interlock/interlock-leader-window)

Interlock makes one channel's Foundation additions leave room for another
channel's anchors. On the follower's Rhythm screen, Interlock opens Leader (Off
or any other channel) and Window (0–4 of the follower's steps). An addition is
removed when a leader anchor falls within Window steps of it; Window 0 removes
only additions that start exactly with a leader anchor. Anchors of either channel
are never removed, so an addition removed here simply does not play.

Leader anchors are the anchor pattern's trigs in the leader's loop, planned from
the song, not what the leader happened to sound: probability, mute and swing do
not change them, and swing or shuffle never change which additions are removed.
Channels at different clock divisions or loop lengths are compared in musical
time from Start. The leader must itself use Foundation for its anchors to count;
otherwise Status says `LEADER OFF` or `LEADER MISSING` and nothing is removed.

A channel can follow one leader, and a channel that has a leader cannot be one:
Apply refuses a chain with `LEADER HAS LEADER` or `CHANNEL IS A LEADER` and
keeps your draft. Where Mosaic cannot plan the leader exactly—after a clock
division, loop range or song change while playing (`RESYNC`, until the next
Start or song realign) or beyond its planning budget (`PLAN LIMIT`)—the
follower plays all of its admitted additions for that loop and shows why.
Status on the Interlock screen and the Interlock row on Result show `ON` or the
bypass.

Interlock's planning runs when a follower wraps its loop. On a norns each
follower that wraps on the same step adds about 0.7 ms to that step, so a few
followers wrapping together are inaudible, while every channel following one
leader and wrapping together (15 followers) can make that step land about
10 ms late. Stagger follower loop lengths or wraps if you need very many.
features.musical_use: Use Interlock to keep one channel’s extra notes out of another channel’s way, for example hi-hat additions that never land on the kick’s anchors, bass additions that leave room for a lead, or two parts that should not double each other.

controls.gesture: Select the follower channel on the grid. In Channel tasks, open Merge Shape, select Rhythm and press K3, then select Interlock and press K3.
controls.result: The Interlock list opens: Leader, Window and Status.

controls.gesture: Select Leader. Turn E3.
controls.result: Leader changes between OFF and the other channels. Another Foundation channel becomes the draft leader.

controls.gesture: Select Window. Turn E3.
controls.result: Window changes between 0 and 4 follower steps.

controls.gesture: Press K3 on a value row.
controls.result: The draft applies and the footer reads APPLIED (NEXT CYCLE while playing). Status reads ON when the filter is working. An invalid chain shows a reason and keeps the draft.

controls.gesture: Press K2.
controls.result: The draft is discarded and Rhythm returns.

details.title: Leader anchors
details.text: Mute, probability and swing do not change the nominal leader-anchor decision. Window 0 removes only additions that start exactly with a leader anchor. Interlock compares where leader anchors start, not how long the leader’s note lasts, so it does not keep space free for a sustained leader note.

details.title: Bypass status
details.text: LEADER OFF, LEADER MISSING, RESYNC and PLAN LIMIT identify inactive filtering. During a planning bypass, admitted additions play. Gap and Amount still apply.

recipes.title: Set Window 0
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: stop one channel’s extra notes landing on another channel’s anchor, for example hi-hat additions that never double the kick. Interlock changes only the follower’s additions. Anchors on both channels always play.

Starting point: Foundation is on for two channels, both with 8-step loops. Channel 1 (the follower, MIDI channel 1) has anchor Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) and Pattern 2 (a C on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (the leader, MIDI channel 2) has anchor Pattern 3, a single trig on step 5; channel 1 has no leader, and its grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

1. Select channel 1 on the grid (button (1,1)). Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3.
2. Select Rhythm and press K3, then select Interlock (the last row) and press K3. The Interlock list opens: Leader OFF, Window 0, Status.
3. Select Leader and turn E3 once right. Leader reads CH02. A channel cannot follow itself, so CH01 is not offered.
4. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED, Window stays 0 and Status reads ON. Step 5 goes dark on the channel 1 grid: Pattern 2’s addition starts exactly on the leader’s anchor and is removed. Steps 1 to 4 and step 7 stay lit.
5. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to two loops, then press Stop. Channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and step 7, and channel 2 plays its anchor on step 5; nothing from channel 1 sounds on step 5.
6. Select Window and turn E3 twice right. Window reads 2.
7. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Step 7 also goes dark, because it is two steps from the leader’s anchor on step 5, and only steps 1 to 4 remain on channel 1; if you apply while playing, the footer reads NEXT CYCLE and the change starts at the next loop.

Window 0 removes only additions that start with a leader anchor. Each step of Window widens the gap by one follower step, up to 4.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured Interlock Leader and Window workflow](#interlock/interlock-leader-window).

features.title: Structure
features.summary: Structure moves selected Foundation notes to the nearest pitch class of an enabled Harmony group’s chord.
features.prose:
[Captured Structure group and marker workflow](#structure/structure-anchor-chord-and-delete)

Structure snaps chosen moments of a Foundation line to a chord while the notes
in between keep their own pitch. Pitch opens Structure: Markers (Off, Anchors,
Every 4 or Every 8) and Chord group, an enabled Harmony Ensemble group. Anchors
marks every anchor onset; Every 4 and Every 8 mark steps 1, 5, 9… or 1, 9… of the
channel loop counted from its start step. A note at a marker is converted to the
scale as usual and then moved to the nearest pitch class of the group's chord,
taking the lower one on a tie. Notes between markers keep their Addition Target
(additions) or their own pitch (anchors); Mosaic makes no claim that they
resolve. Note masks, random shifts and fixed notes still win at a marker.

Apply needs an enabled group while Markers is on. If the group becomes
unavailable during playback the markers play their ordinary pitch and Result
says `CHORD MISSING`. Deleting or disabling the group turns Markers Off for every
channel that uses it in the same change; Delete group lists those channels first.
During playback that change waits for the next pattern boundary, and a Merge
Shape edit applied to one of those channels before then waits with it and shows
`NEXT PATTERN` instead of `NEXT CYCLE`.
A snapped marker keeps its chord tone when Harmony Revoice or Ensemble would move
it: Harmony's Result says `MARKER PRIORITY`. With Harmony Pattern, a mapped note
value that snaps to a different pitch class at a marker than it plays between
markers has no single mapped pitch, so it is silent at both, whichever fallback
is chosen; unmapped values keep their own pitch.
features.musical_use: Use Structure to land chosen notes of a Foundation line on the tones of a chord while the notes between them keep their own pitch, for example a bass line that touches C, E or G on the strong beats.

controls.gesture: Choose Foundation on Merge modes or with grid (14,8). On Merge Shape, select Pitch and press K3, then select Structure and press K3.
controls.result: The Structure list opens with Markers.

controls.gesture: Select Markers. Turn E3.
controls.result: Markers changes between OFF, ANCHORS, EVERY 4 and EVERY 8. When Markers is on, a Chord group row appears.

controls.gesture: Select Chord group. Turn E3.
controls.result: An enabled Harmony group becomes the draft chord source.

controls.gesture: Press K3 on a value row.
controls.result: The draft applies. A group that is missing or disabled prevents activation.

details.title: Markers and pitch precedence
details.text: Markers count from the channel loop’s start step. The nearest chord pitch class is selected; ties select the lower pitch. Note masks, random shifts and fixed notes retain their precedence.

details.title: Group deletion and disable
details.text: Deleting or disabling a referenced group turns affected Markers Off in the same transaction. During playback, that change waits for NEXT PATTERN. Pending linked Merge Shape edits wait for the same boundary.

recipes.title: Snap anchors to a chord, then try Every 4
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: land the strong notes of a line on the tones of a chord while the notes between them stay as written. Anchors snaps every anchor note. Every 4 snaps only steps 1 and 5 of an 8-step loop and leaves the rest of the line alone.

Terms: a Harmony group is a stored chord. Its Template count is how many tones the chord has, each Tone row sets that tone's offset from the root, and Group enabled lets other features use it. Structure moves a marked note to the nearest tone of an enabled group's chord.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop with Foundation on. Pattern 1 is the anchor (C D E F on steps 1 to 4, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Pattern 2 supplies additions (a C on steps 5 and 7). If Foundation is not on yet, follow steps 1 to 4 of Set a two-cycle Build phrase first. Steps 1 to 3 build a group that holds the chord C E G; if you already have an enabled group with that chord, start at step 4.

1. Create the group: press E1 for Channel tasks, select Harmony and press K3. Select Groups with E2 and press K3. Select Create group and press K3. Group 1 appears.

2. Set the chord: select Source and press K3. Select Template count and turn E3 twice right, so the chord has 3 tones. Select Tone 2 and turn E3 twice right. Select Tone 3 and turn E3 four times right. With the root, the offsets 2 and 4 are C E G in C major. Press K3 on a value row. The footer reads APPLIED.

3. Enable the group: press K2 to return to Groups. Select Members and press K3, select Group enabled, turn E3 once right to ON and press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Group 1 is enabled.

4. Open Structure: press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape and press K3. Select Pitch and press K3, then select Structure and press K3. The Structure list opens with Markers OFF.

5. Select Markers and turn E3 once right. Markers reads ANCHORS and a Chord group row appears showing 1, then press K3. The footer reads APPLIED.

6. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to two loops. The anchors C D E F sound as C C E E (MIDI 60, 60, 64, 64): D is equally near C and E and takes the lower one, and F is nearer E than G. The additions on steps 5 and 7 stay C. Press Stop.

7. Now the contrast. Select Markers and turn E3 once right. Markers reads EVERY 4, so only steps 1 and 5 are markers. Press K3.

8. Press Play. Step 1 and step 5 are C, which is already a chord tone, so nothing moves. D on step 2 and F on step 4 are not markers any more and return to their own pitches. The line plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, 60 and 60 in each loop. Then press Stop.

Choosing Anchors snaps every anchor, and Every 4 snaps only the beats you choose. Deleting or disabling the group turns Markers OFF.

The captured version, [Captured Structure group and marker workflow](#structure/structure-anchor-chord-and-delete), covers steps 1 to 6 with Anchors and then deletes the group. Steps 7 and 8 are captured in [Mark every fourth step](#structure/structure-every-4-markers), which starts from the enabled C E G group with Foundation on and shows Markers set to Every 4 and the line playing 60, 62, 64, 65, 60, 60 in each loop.

features.title: Result and Reason
features.summary: Result shows what a step is and why. Reason lists, in order, the decisions that excluded an addition.
features.prose:
Use Result and Reason when an expected addition is silent. They tell you whether the step is an anchor, an admitted addition or empty, and which rule removed it, so you can fix the setting instead of editing a pattern or adding a mask.

The examples below use a follower channel with Foundation (anchor Pattern 1 on steps 1 to 4, additions from Pattern 2 on steps 5 and 7) that follows channel 2 through Interlock, where channel 2 has an anchor on step 5. See Interlock to set that up.

1. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3. Select Result and press K3.
2. Select Step with E2. Turn E3 to the step to inspect. Role and Decision show that step.
3. Select Reason with E2 and press K3. The Merge Reason dashboard opens with six rows. K2 returns to Result.

The six rows of Reason:

- Step: the step you are inspecting.
- Role: what the step is, followed by its source patterns. ANCHOR is a trig from the anchor pattern, ADDITION P2 is an addition taken from Pattern 2, and EMPTY means nothing plays.
- Decision: OK when the step plays, otherwise every rule that excluded it, in order. GAP comes first, then INTERLOCK CH02. When both apply, both are listed, as in GAP, INTERLOCK.
- Interlock: ON while the leader’s anchors are being avoided, OFF when there is no leader, RESYNC or PLAN LIMIT when Interlock cannot plan the leader and is bypassed.
- Velocity: the velocity the step plays, or NONE when it does not play.
- Pitch target: LEGACY unless an Addition Target or Structure marker applies.

A suppressed addition shows Role EMPTY with its source patterns, for example EMPTY P2, and Velocity NONE. EMPTY P2 does not mean Pattern 2 has no trig on that step. Read Decision to see why the candidate was removed.

During a planning bypass, Gap and Amount still decide the step as if Interlock were Off.

A fragment step names its fragment and source, for example FRAGMENT 1 P03 or KEPT ANCHOR. A Structure marker shows MARKER CHORD G01 when its pitch is snapped, CHORD MISSING when the group is unavailable, or a reason such as BYPASS NOTE MASK, BYPASS RANDOM, BYPASS FIXED or BYPASS QUANTISED FIXED.

When a leader is set, Result also shows the Interlock status. A queued edit refused at the loop boundary is shown as Rejected. Silence-aware Interlock, which would keep space free while another channel’s notes sustain, is not available in this release.
features.musical_use: Open Result and Reason before changing a pattern or adding a mask to bring back an addition that does not play.

controls.gesture: Open Result in Merge Shape.
controls.result: The selected step’s Role and Decision are displayed.

controls.gesture: In Result, select Step with E2 and turn E3.
controls.result: The inspected step changes. In the Interlock example, steps 5 and 7 are the interesting ones.

controls.gesture: In Result, select Reason with E2. Press K3.
controls.result: The Merge Reason dashboard opens for the step selected in Result. Its Step row is read-only. K2 returns to Result.

details.title: Combined reasons
details.text: Reason can display GAP and INTERLOCK together, with GAP first. The Interlock row is separate and shows ON, OFF, RESYNC or PLAN LIMIT. A planning bypass does not remove Gap or Amount decisions.

details.title: Pitch status
details.text: MARKER CHORD G01 identifies a snapped marker. BYPASS NOTE MASK, BYPASS RANDOM and fixed-note bypasses identify retained pitches. CHORD MISSING identifies the ordinary-pitch fallback.

details.title: Suppressed addition readout
details.text: A suppressed Foundation addition shows Role EMPTY with its source patterns, and Velocity NONE. Decision tells you whether a candidate was excluded or the source step was empty.

features.title: Harmony
features.summary: Harmony provides Off, Revoice, Pattern and Ensemble modes for channel output pitch placement.
features.prose:
Harmony changes the pitch a channel sends, not its rhythm. Open it from Channel tasks (Voice leading list: Mode, Group, Preset, Tone Map in Pattern mode, Register, Bass, Groups, Rules, Entry, Result). Tone Map is the page that maps written notes to voices. Register sets each voice’s range. Entry holds the Failure fallback. Result shows what was planned and sent.

[Captured Harmony range failure and fallback](#harmony/harmony-range-failure-and-fallback)

[Captured Harmony Revoice workflow](#harmony/harmony-revoice-two-voices)

Harmony offers four mutually exclusive channel modes:

- Off follows the ordinary Mosaic pitch path exactly.
- Revoice takes the actual root and enabled chord-mask voices after Mosaic's
  pitch-class decisions, preserving their pitch classes and sounding count while
  choosing legal octaves and assignments.
- Pattern maps explicit effective relative values in the current merge binding
  to Bass, Inner1–3 or Top. Repeated mapped values reuse one pitch for the entire
  harmonic frame; unmapped values remain Raw. Random, fixed, absolute-mask and
  chord-mask events visibly bypass Pattern. Conflicting aliases fail closed.
- Ensemble assigns Bass/Inner/Top roles to one to five explicit monophonic
  channels. Each member retains its own rhythm, velocity, gate, clock and route,
  but its pitch is replaced by the shared frame. A conflicting local scale lock
  temporarily uses the ordinary pitch path (`LOCAL SCALE BYPASS`); a channel or
  step octave override does the same (`LOCAL OCTAVE BYPASS`).

Register rows set inclusive MIDI Low/High, Centre and Preferred leap for every
role. Smooth prioritises literal common tones and economical movement; Compact
prioritises register centre/spacing; Independent prioritises movement without a
common-tone score. Hard options cover crossing, exact unison, strict leap and
strict bass direction. Bass can be Root, an explicit Inversion tone, Smooth or
an exact Pedal. Revoice pedals must already be in its input material; only an
Ensemble group can explicitly allow a non-chord pedal.

The deterministic solver searches every legal pitch-class placement inside the
configured ranges (up to five voices) and never clamps an illegal result. A frame
with no solution silences affected mapped voices by default; Legacy fallback is
explicit. A bounded search reports `BUDGET EXCEEDED` rather than emitting a
partial answer. Preparing a frame does not change voice history: the first real
scheduled onset consumes it, while redraws, rests, failed probability, mute and
missing output do not. Delayed strums and arpeggios keep the pitch snapshot made
at their onset, and Note Off always releases the pitch and route actually sent.

[Captured NO VOICING and Legacy fallback](#harmony/harmony-range-failure-and-fallback)

The Channel grid remains the chronological trig/mask surface. Foundation anchors
and additions therefore appear as active steps there. After a step plays, the
Pattern Note grid moves that step's bright note LED to the final effective pitch
that the native 21-position note range can represent. Switch its upper, centred
or lower seven-note bank as usual to inspect octave placement. Raw and bypassed
events use the ordinary pre-Harmony position; turning Harmony Off restores the
ordinary merged/scale positions immediately. An exact pitch outside that native
range has no false in-range LED and remains available in Result/Note Dashboard.

This display is read-only: touching the projected Note fader still edits its
selected source-pattern value. Until the changed step plays again, the edited
source is displayed rather than a stale output. Final Harmony pitches are also
shown on Output (its Pitch and Sent rows) and on Harmony's Result screen, one row
per voice as the planned and sent note (`C3 > C3`). Result uses its Step row to
select one coherent event chain; on Note
Dashboard, holding a grid step temporarily inspects that step instead of combining
it with a later delayed event. A step with no recorded event says `NO EVENT` and
shows no planned or emitted pitch; it never borrows the latest event from another
step. This readout occupies the bottom two lines of the Note Dashboard, which is
the row tooltips use, so while a harmony event is being shown there the page
clears that row and tooltips are not visible on it. Result status names local scale/octave bypasses, explicit Legacy fallback
and the specific no-voicing reason. For an Ensemble group, any member bypass or failure is
surfaced even when another member has a valid voicing. The projection never writes
back into a shared pattern. Copy/save stores
versioned configuration, not running solver or phrase history. Missing optional
configuration loads as Off; unknown schema versions reject the project before it
replaces the active project.
features.musical_use: Use Revoice for root and chord-mask voices, Pattern for repeated relative values, or Ensemble for a chord distributed across monophonic channels.

controls.gesture: In Channel tasks, select Harmony. Press K3.
controls.result: Voice leading settings open.

controls.gesture: Turn E2 to Mode. Turn E3.
controls.result: The draft mode changes between Off, Revoice, Pattern and Ensemble.

controls.gesture: Select Register or another settings row marked OPEN >. Press K3.
controls.result: The selected settings list opens.

controls.gesture: Turn E2 to select a value. Turn E3 to change it. Press K3 on a value row.
controls.result: Mosaic validates and applies the draft. During playback, NEXT PATTERN indicates a queued change.

controls.gesture: Press K2.
controls.result: A dirty draft is cancelled. An opened settings list returns to its parent.

controls.gesture: In Result, select Step.
controls.result: The selected event’s planned and sent pitches are displayed.

controls.gesture: On Note Dashboard, hold a grid step.
controls.result: That step’s event is inspected. A step without a recorded event displays NO EVENT.

controls.gesture: In Pattern mode, select Tone Map. Press K3. Select a Tone row and turn E3.
controls.result: The row changes between RAW, BASS, INNER1, INNER2, INNER3 and TOP. K3 on a value row applies the map.

controls.gesture: Select Register. Press K3. Select a role with the Role row, then select Low, High or Centre and turn E3.
controls.result: The role’s inclusive MIDI range changes. A Low, High and Centre that leave no legal placement for a mapped note give NO VOICING RANGE and silence it.

controls.gesture: Select Entry. Press K3. Select Failure fallback and turn E3.
controls.result: Failure fallback changes between SILENCE and LEGACY. Silence is the default; Legacy plays the ordinary pitch and Result reads LEGACY RANGE.

details.title: Mode selection
details.text: Revoice places the actual root and enabled chord-mask voices in legal octaves. Pattern maps repeated effective relative values to roles. Ensemble assigns a shared harmonic frame to specified monophonic channels; each member retains its rhythm and route.

details.title: No voicing and fallback
details.text: Infeasible registers display NO VOICING RANGE on Result. Silence is the default failure fallback. To change it, open Entry and set Failure fallback to LEGACY. A step with no event reads NO EVENT, which is different from a failed voicing. A solver budget failure does not emit a partial answer.

details.title: Note grid editing
details.text: After a played event, the Note grid displays the final pitch if it is within the native range. Editing a Note fader still edits the selected source pattern. Projected pitches are not written to that pattern.

details.title: Saving and loading
details.text: Saving stores the Harmony settings, not the solver position or phrase history. A project saved with no Harmony settings loads with Harmony Off. A project saved by a newer, unknown Harmony version is refused with a message that names the slot and says voicing schema version, and the project that is running is kept.

recipes.title: Map three relative values
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: pin chosen written notes to fixed voices of a chord frame, each limited to its own register, so a note that repeats in the phrase always lands on the same pitch. Choose Pattern when you want to decide which written note goes to which voice; choose Revoice when the chord notes are already written and you want Mosaic to arrange their octaves. In this phrase the notes are all different, so the repeat rule is explained at the end rather than heard.

Terms used below: a written value is the relative note of a step (0 to 3 here); a voice is Bass, Inner 1 to 3 or Top; a register is the range of MIDI notes a voice may use; RAW means the value is not mapped and keeps its own pitch.

Starting point: channel 1 plays one pattern, C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (written values 0, 1, 2, 3; MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), at 90 BPM. Harmony is Off.

1. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Harmony with E2 and press K3. The Voice leading list opens with Mode OFF.

2. Select Mode with E2 and turn E3 twice right (Off, Revoice, Pattern). Mode reads PATTERN and a Tone Map row appears. The change is a draft until K3.

3. Select Tone Map with E2 and press K3. The Tone Map lists one row for each written value, Tone 0 to Tone 3, all RAW, followed by Reset map.

4. Select Tone 0 and turn E3 once right. It reads BASS. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Press Play and then Stop: C still plays as MIDI 60, because 60 already lies inside the default Bass register (24 to 60), so nothing sounds different yet.

5. Select Tone 2 and turn E3 twice right so it reads INNER1. Press K3. Tone 1 (D) stays RAW.

6. Select Tone 3 and turn E3 five times right so it reads TOP. Press K3.

7. Press E1 to return to the Voice leading list. Select Register with E2 and press K3. The Register list opens: Role (the first role is Bass), Low, High, Centre, Preferred leap, Strict leap.

8. Select High with E2 and turn E3 five times left. High reads 55. Press K3.

9. Press Play and listen to two loops, then press Stop. The Bass register now ends at 55, so 60 no longer fits and C plays as MIDI 48 (C2), the nearest C inside it. D stays at MIDI 62 because it is RAW. E and F are placed in their Inner 1 and Top registers. Open Result straight away (next step) to see each pitch.

10. Press E1 to return to the Voice leading list, select Result and press K3. Select Step and turn E3 to step 1, step 3 and step 4: each shows its planned and sent pitch.

A repeated mapped value uses one pitch for the whole harmonic frame: if the phrase were C D C F, both Cs would sound as MIDI 48. If a role's range leaves no legal placement for a mapped note, Result shows NO VOICING RANGE and that note is silent. See [Captured Harmony range failure and fallback](#harmony/harmony-range-failure-and-fallback).

features.title: Performance Management
features.summary: Channel count, clock rates, parameter slides, trigless locks and n.b. devices affect sequencer workload.
features.prose:
Channel count, clock rate, trig locks, parameter slides and n.b. devices affect Mosaic’s workload. Heavy workload can delay sequencing and make external clock synchronization unreliable.

- Use greater care with high clock rates, trig locks, parameter slides and n.b. devices as channel count increases.
- High clock rates and multipliers increase sequencer workload.
- Use global parameter slides sparingly. Use step parameter slides when global sliding is unnecessary, and limit the total number of slides.
- Disable trigless locks when the additional modulation granularity is not needed.
- Limit the number of n.b. devices.

A test on version 1.1.1 found unreliable external synchronization with one Doubledecker n.b. device at 110 BPM, trigless parameters, locks on most steps for all 10 trig parameters across four channels, and 40 parameters using global parameter sliding. Other combinations can produce different results. This earlier example does not specify a universal limit for the current version.
features.musical_use: Reduce global slides, fast multipliers or trigless-lock density when an arrangement’s timing becomes unreliable.

details.title: Earlier timing test
details.text: The 110 BPM Doubledecker example comes from testing on version 1.1.1. It is not a universal current limit. Host and emulator timing do not establish physical norns scheduling accuracy.

details.title: Reducing workload
details.text: Use step slides where a global slide is unnecessary. Disable trigless locks when their additional modulation detail is not needed. Compare changes using the same arrangement and clock source.

features.title: Development
features.summary: Run the repository tests on a development machine before opening a pull request.
features.prose:
This section is for people changing Mosaic's code, not for playing it. Before opening a pull request, run the repository tests on a development machine:

```
./test.sh
```

Do not run the harness on norns. It downloads a copy of the norns repository, which can conflict with the device's own installation. If you ran it on the device by mistake, delete /code/mosaic/lib/tests/test_artefacts to remove that copy and restore the device.

controls.gesture: Run ./test.sh on the development machine.
controls.result: The Lua test suite runs. Do not run the harness on the norns device.

details.title: Behavior changes
details.text:
1. Add the smallest regression for the change.
2. Confirm that it fails for the expected reason.
3. Make the production change and rerun the regression.
4. Run affected unit, integration and emulator behavior tests, then the full Lua suite.
Follow AGENTS.md. Documentation does not replace observable acceptance.

recipes.title: Check a change before a pull request
recipes.text:
Before you start you need Lua (CI uses 5.3), curl, unzip and network access to GitHub: the first run downloads a copy of the norns repository.
1. On your computer, open a terminal in the Mosaic folder.
2. Run ./test.sh and wait for it to finish. It ends with luaunit's summary, Ran N tests in S seconds, N successes, 0 failures, then OK.
3. Fix any failing test, then run it again until the whole suite passes.
4. Only then open the pull request. CI runs the same ./test.sh on every pull request, so a pass here predicts the check.
5. Never run this on the norns itself. If you did, delete /code/mosaic/lib/tests/test_artefacts to remove the downloaded copy.

features.title: Interesting Components for Norns Script Developers
features.summary: The Lua harness and mocks run norns script tests away from hardware.
features.prose:
Mosaic has a Lua test harness that runs norns scripts away from the hardware. It downloads a copy of the norns repository and uses local mocks and shims so luaunit tests run on a normal computer. The harness and example tests are in the lib/tests folder; start there when you want to test your own script the same way. Run it on a development machine, never on norns.

This program is released under the GNU license. Copyright Andrew Hillel 2024.

details.title: Where to look
details.text: lib/tests/run_tests.lua downloads the norns copy and loads every test file. lib/tests/lib holds the unit tests, for example m_midi_tests.lua (MIDI output with a spy device), scheduler_tests.lua (the scheduler) and ui_adapters_tests.lua (screen pages). lib/tests/lib/integration_tests holds tests that run several modules together. lib/tests/helpers/mocks holds the stand-ins for norns, params, MIDI and the scheduler.

recipes.title: Read a harness example
recipes.text:
1. Open lib/tests/lib/m_midi_tests.lua in the Mosaic repository. Its helper with_output_spy swaps the global midi_devices for a stub that records note_on and note_off calls, runs the module under test and checks what was sent with luaunit.assert_equals. That is a complete example of testing a norns script without hardware. The helper, lines 3-14 of the file:
```lua
local function with_output_spy(run)
  local original_devices=midi_devices
  local sent={}
  midi_devices={{
    note_on=function(_,note,velocity,channel) sent[#sent+1]={"on",note,velocity,channel} end,
    note_off=function(_,note,velocity,channel) sent[#sent+1]={"off",note,velocity,channel} end
  }}
  midi_output:reset_note_counts()
  local ok,err=pcall(run,sent)
  midi_output:reset_note_counts();midi_devices=original_devices
  if not ok then error(err,0) end
end
```
The test that uses it, lines 33-38 of the file: it releases a note that was never played with an out-of-range value, and the spy shows the value clamped to 127 before it is sent.
```lua
function test_unmatched_midi_release_is_clamped_before_safety_send()
  with_output_spy(function(sent)
    midi_output:note_off(200,77,4,1)
    luaunit.assert_equals(sent,{{"off",127,77,4}})
  end)
end
```
2. Open lib/tests/helpers/mocks to see the other stand-ins (norns_mock.lua, params_mock.lua, scheduler_mock.lua, m_midi_mock.lua) and search lib/tests/lib for the tests that include them.
3. Run every test with ./test.sh on your computer. To run a single test, change into lib/tests and run lua ./run_tests.lua with luaunit's -p option and part of the test's name, for example -p test_unmatched_midi_release.

features.title: Masks
features.summary: Override channel and step trig, note, velocity, length and chord values.
features.prose:
Masks override attributes of the merged pattern data. They can overwrite pattern values or create steps the patterns do not have, and they accept triggers, notes, velocities and chords. Set a channel default to affect every step, or hold a step to set an individual override. Unset attributes use the channel default or merged pattern data. Each Masks recipe below starts from the four-step loop in Make your first loop (channel 1, pattern 1, steps 1-4). A masked value always wins over the pattern for that step; the channel default wins over the pattern for every step without its own mask.
The Masks screen shows the value you are editing as you turn E3, with note names for the Note row, so stop on the readout instead of counting detents. One detent moves a note by one MIDI note and other values by one unit.

[Masks demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=1740s)
features.musical_use: Set a note mask to change the pitch of one step while the pattern keeps its rhythm; set a velocity mask to accent or soften a step; fill the Chd rows to add chord voices; add a trig mask to put a note on an empty step. To run channels at different lengths, see Channel Length.

controls.gesture: Grid (3,8) → E1 tasks → E2 Masks → K3
controls.result: Open the eight mask values.

controls.gesture: E2
controls.result: Choose Trig, Note, Vel, Len, Chd1–Chd4.

controls.gesture: E3, no step held
controls.result: Edit the channel default.

controls.gesture: Hold step + E3
controls.result: Edit that step's exception.

controls.gesture: Hold K1 + tap step
controls.result: Add or remove a trig mask.

controls.gesture: Hold step + K2
controls.result: Clear all mask attributes for the held step.

controls.gesture: K1 + K2, no grid keys held
controls.result: Clear channel step overrides; preserve defaults.

details.title: Unset values and precedence
details.text: X is an unset attribute, not zero. A step's explicit attribute wins over the channel default; an unset step uses the default; an unset default falls back to merged pattern data. Clearing step overrides does not erase the defaults.

details.title: Chord masks
details.text: Chd1–Chd4 add four scale-relative voices above or below the root. 3rd and 5th specify intervals, not MIDI note numbers. From X, turn E3 right for a voice above the root and left for a voice below it; each row reaches 14 scale steps either way. Select a polyphonic output to play simultaneous chord voices. Use strum and chord velocity to adjust their timing and level.

details.title: Scale, degree and rotation
details.text: Note masks snap to the selected scale by default. Degree and rotation apply only when full quantisation is enabled. See Snap Note Masks to Scale, Quantise Note Masks and Fully Quantise Mask for their precedence. Turn off Snap note masks to scale in the Mosaic params to enter accidentals or dissonant notes.

details.title: MIDI and clearing
details.text: Hold a step and play a MIDI keyboard to enter notes and chords. Live recording also enters masks. With a step held, K2 clears that step even if K1 is held. Other channels are unaffected.

details.title: If a new note is silent
details.text: Check the selected channel's output, active range and mute state. A trig alone needs an audible note, velocity and length. A mono voice cannot sound all chord voices together. To undo an exception, hold that step and press K2.

details.title: Note names on the Masks screen
details.text: The Masks screen uses norns musicutil: floor(MIDI note / 12 − 2). MIDI note 60 is displayed as C3. The Fixed Note parameter uses a different label convention and displays MIDI note 60 as C5. Use numeric MIDI notes when comparing these controls.

recipes.title: Try a different ending for a four-note melody
recipes.text:
Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop. Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with channel defaults Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, so it repeats one note four times. The Masks screen shows the note name for the value you are editing, and one detent of E3 moves one MIDI note, so turn E3 until the screen reads the name given below instead of counting. Norns shows MIDI 60 as C3, so 72 is C4, 74 is D4, 76 is E4 and 79 is G4.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and, with no step held, the Note row shows the channel default, C3.

2. Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)). The header gains ST01, which means edits now apply to that step only. Turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (12 detents), then release the step.

3. Hold step 2 (2,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads D4 (14 detents) and release the step.

4. Hold step 3 (3,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads G4 (19 detents) and release the step.

5. Hold step 4 (4,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads E4 (16 detents) and release the step. After each release the screen goes back to the channel default, C3; each step you set keeps its own note.

6. Tap Play at (1,8). The loop plays C4, D4, G4, E4 (72, 74, 79, 76). Tap Play again to stop.

7. Hold step 4 and turn E3 left until the screen reads D4 (two detents). Release the step and tap Play: the phrase now ends C4, D4, G4, D4. Only step 4 changed; steps 1-3 keep their masks. Tap Play to stop.

8. To end on the root instead, hold step 4 and turn E3 left until the screen reads C4 (two more detents). Release the step and tap Play: the phrase is C4, D4, G4, C4.

All of these notes are in the default C major scale, so scale snapping leaves them unchanged. A note outside the scale is moved onto it. The captured example "Change the ending of a four-note melody" runs steps 1 to 8 on the four-note loop and shows the MIDI strip after each change (its pattern keeps its own velocities, so the recipe's Vel 80 is not repeated there); "Set channel and step note masks" shows the same hold-and-turn gestures on a different loop.

recipes.title: Add a ghost note before an accent
recipes.text:
Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop, with channel default Vel 80. A ghost note is a very quiet note played just before a louder one; it makes the louder note feel pushed.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Turn E2 to Vel. With no step held the screen reads 80, the channel default.

2. Hold step 3 (grid (3,4)) and turn E3 right until the screen reads 100. Release the step. Step 3 is now the accent.

3. Hold step 2 (2,4) and turn E3 left until the screen reads 35. Release the step. Step 2 is the ghost note.

4. Tap Play at (1,8). The velocities are 80, 35, 100, 80: a soft tap on step 2 leads into the loud step 3. Tap Play again to stop.

The captured example "Set a ghost note and an accent" shows steps 1 to 4 and the velocities 80, 35, 100, 80 in the MIDI strip (that loop plays C, D, E and F, not one repeated note); "Set velocity and length masks" shows the Vel row and the MIDI velocities each edit produces. To make the ghost note come and go, continue with Make the ghost note intermittent.

recipes.title: Make the ghost note intermittent
recipes.text:
Starting point: the ghost-note loop from Add a ghost note before an accent (step 2 at velocity 35, step 3 at 100). Velocity decides how loud a note is; Trig Probability decides whether the trig plays at all.

1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. The screen shows all ten slots at once. A slot that has no parameter assigned yet is an empty slot.

2. Turn E2 to the first empty slot. E2 stops at slot 1 and at slot 10.

3. Press K2, turn E3 until Trig Probability appears, press K3 to assign it and press K2 to return to slot selection. The slot now carries Trig Probability.

4. Hold step 2 (grid (2,4)) and turn E3 until the screen reads 50. Release the step. Step 2 now has its own probability of 50; the other steps use the channel default and still play every time.

5. Tap Play at (1,8) and listen over several passes: the ghost note sounds on about half of them and the other three notes never drop out. Tap Play again to stop.

6. To remove the exception, hold step 2 on Trig params and press K2. This clears every parameter lock on that step.

Steps 1 to 3 (moving to an empty slot and assigning Trig Probability) are shown screen by screen in the captured example "Turn chance into explicit rests".

recipes.title: Add chord voices over a bass
recipes.text:
Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop on channel 1, and a second channel for the chord. Channel 1's device can be monophonic. Channel 2 needs a polyphonic device, because one step plays several notes together. The audio example "A bass with room above it" below plays the same idea with Polyperc 1 for the bass and Doubledecker for the chords; its notes and levels differ from the values used here.

Set up the bass on channel 1.

1. Tap (1,1) to select channel 1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3.

2. With no step held, set Note to C2 (MIDI 48), Vel to 70 and Len to 1/2. Channel 1 now plays bass notes on steps 1-4.

Set up the chord channel.

3. Tap (2,1) to select channel 2. Open Channel tasks, choose Device and pick a polyphonic voice; press K3 to apply it.

4. Assign pattern 1 to channel 2: tap pattern slot (1,2).

5. Set channel 2 to the same four steps: hold step 1 (1,4), tap step 4 (4,4), then release step 1.

6. On Masks, with no step held, set channel 2's Note to C3 (MIDI 60), Vel to 60 and Len to 1/2. It now plays single notes over the bass.

Add the chord voices.

7. Turn E2 to Chd1 and, with no step held, turn E3 two detents to 3rd. Every step adds the scale third above its root: 64.

8. Turn E2 to Chd2 and turn E3 four detents to 5th. Every step adds the scale fifth: 67.

9. Tap Play at (1,8). Channel 2 plays C3, E3 and G3 (60, 64, 67) together on every step over the bass C2 (48). Tap Play again to stop.

Change the voicing.

10. Turn E2 to Chd3 and set 6th (five detents): the chord adds A (69). Hold a single step and change a Chd row to give only that step a different voicing.

Chd values are scale intervals above the root, not MIDI note numbers. In another scale the same 3rd and 5th give that scale's intervals. The captured example "Set chord masks" shows each Chd edit and the MIDI notes it produces.

features.title: Creating a First Loop
features.summary: Hear a repeating four-note loop.
features.prose:
Before starting: Start a new project with Record off. No output, patterns or masks have been entered yet. The walkthrough below begins by choosing an output for channel 1, so you can follow it from an empty project. [Configuring an Output](#setup) explains the choices.

### Choose the output

1. Tap Channel (3,8). The header reads CH01.
2. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, select Device with E2 and press K3.
3. Select a working output with E3: the basic MIDI device (CC Device), your own configuration, or Polyperc 1 for internal sound. Press K3 to apply.

Device shows the output you chose. A selection that has not been applied with K3 is only a draft.

### Enter four attacks

1. Tap Pattern (5,8) to Trig. The header names pattern 1.
2. Tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4), (4,4).

Four active attacks light on row 4. Each lit step is a trig, a point where a note can sound. If you are editing another pattern, select pattern 1 on the top row first.

### Assign and shorten

1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Tap pattern slot (1,2).
3. Hold step (1,4), tap (4,4), release (1,4). To set a range, hold its first step, tap its last step, then release the first.

Pattern 1 feeds channel 1 across a four-step range, so the channel loops steps 1 to 4.

### Give the attacks a pitch and level

1. Open Channel tasks → Masks.
2. With no step held, select Note with E2 and set MIDI 60 with E3 (C3). The Masks screen labels MIDI 60 as C3.
3. Select Vel and set 80.
4. Select Len and set 1/2.

These are channel masks: all four attacks share one pitch, velocity and length. A step could override them later.

### Play and stop

1. Tap Play (1,8).
2. Listen for four equal C notes repeating, with a playhead moving along the grid. At 90 BPM and the default Rate /1 each step lasts one sixth of a second, so the loop repeats about every two thirds of a second.
3. Tap Play again to stop; hold K1 too if Shift press stop is enabled.

Four equal C notes repeat. Playback stops with notes released.

Resulting project: Pattern 1 attacks 1–4; CH01 assigned P1; range 1–4; Note 60/Vel 80/Len1/2; no step exceptions; stopped.

details.title: Coordinates and pitches
details.text: The first channel steps run across row 4. Coordinates count from the grid’s top-left corner. Octave labels vary between screens: this tutorial uses the Masks field, where MIDI 60 is C3. Numeric MIDI is the reliable reference when moving between instruments or controls.

details.title: Walkthrough Result
details.text: The walkthrough above shows each setting on screen and plays two cycles of four equal MIDI notes (MIDI 60, velocity 80), then stops playback. It does not include a live audio recording of the first loop.

details.title: Recovery
details.text: If silent, follow No Sound in transport → assignment → range → masks → output order.

details.title: Course continuity
details.text: Continue the same project through Make a piece. The separate reference demonstrations below start from their stated starting projects; they do not load a replacement into your project.

features.title: Troubleshooting No Sound
features.summary: Check transport, channel data and output settings in order.
features.prose:
Use the loop in [Creating a First Loop](#first-sound). Check the following in order.

1. Check that the grid playhead moves. If it does not, press Play. For an external clock source, check that the source is running and sending clock. Use the internal clock for a standalone check.
2. Select the intended channel and check that it is unmuted. Assign a pattern or enter trig masks. An unassigned source pattern does not play through the channel.
3. Check that active attacks are inside the channel range. If several patterns are assigned, check whether Skip removes their overlaps. Compare one assigned pattern or All trig merge.
4. Open Masks. Check Trig, Note, Vel and Len at channel and held-step scope. An explicit step value overrides its default. Velocity 0 is silent. Clear an exception to restore inheritance.
5. Open Device. Apply the selection with K3; a draft is not the active destination. For MIDI, match output port and receive channel. For n.b., check that the player is installed, enabled and supported. Check norns audio level and the listening path.

For hanging notes, stop playback, then hold a non-selected page navigation key to invoke panic. Panic sends Note Off messages but does not stop playback. A running sequence can sound new notes after the sweep.

The examples on this page each show one of these checks. Keep each channel independent shows that Device belongs to one channel, so a channel with Device None makes no sound (check 5). Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed shows the channel range in check 3: a range gesture whose end would come before its start is refused, the previous valid range stays, and only the attacks inside that range sound. Merge two patterns shows how Skip removes the trigs two patterns share (check 3). Set velocity and length masks shows that velocity 0 is silent and that X lets the pattern's own velocity through (check 4). Create a four-step loop from an empty project is the working loop to compare against.

review.native_gap: Native scoped scenes cover basic playback, device scope, mutes, ranges, mask silence and merge choices. Physical cabling/audio setup is external. Panic is documented in its separate guide and awaits its own scene.

features.title: Creating a Phrase and Arrangement
features.summary: Turn four fast attacks into four evenly spaced beats.
features.prose:
Before starting: Use channel 1 with pattern 1 assigned, active attacks at steps 1–4 and range 1–4. Set channel Masks Note to MIDI 60, Vel to 80 and Len to 1/2; clear existing step exceptions. Stop playback. [Creating a First Loop](#first-sound) gives the complete preparation route.

### Extend the range

1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Hold (1,4), tap (16,4), release.
3. Turn E1 to Channel tasks; select Clock with E2 and press K3.
4. Select Rate with E2; set /1 with E3 (sixteenth notes, the default).
5. Press K3 to apply while stopped.

The channel traverses16 steps before repeating.

### Move the attacks

1. Open Pattern Trig, pattern 1.
2. Remove steps 2,3,4.
3. Add steps 5,9,13; keep step 1.

Four attacks now sit on the four beats. The old attacks have been removed explicitly.

### Hear the longer phrase

1. Play two bars.
2. Stop.

C–C–C–C remains the pitch sequence; the space between attacks has increased.

Resulting project: P1 attacks 1/5/9/13; CH01 range 1–16; sixteenth-note rate; Note 60/Vel 80/Len1/2 unchanged.

The examples below extend this phrase. Set channel and step note masks shows how a step's own note beats the channel default. Save D major, then apply it shows how a scale slot can be edited and saved without changing what plays until you apply it. The last three examples walk through the whole workflow in order: Add a second pattern in D major merges two patterns on channel 1, Add a second channel with its own output gives channel 2 its own MIDI port, and Chain song slots an octave apart plays two song slots.

details.title: Mask Defaults and Pattern Editing
details.text: The first-loop tutorial sets channel Note, Vel and Len defaults. Leaving them set would override later pattern edits. X restores inheritance. Step-specific overrides still take precedence; the initial tutorial does not create any.

details.title: Recovery
details.text: Remove an accidental attack by tapping it again in Pattern Trig.

features.title: Saving and Loading a Project
features.summary: Restore the arrangement from a named project.
features.prose:
Before starting: Use any stopped project containing a named arrangement. The worked reload check uses slot 1 with channel 1 muted and another channel audible. For another project, make a reversible visible change before loading and confirm the saved state returns.

### Save the arrangement

1. Tap K1 briefly to enter the norns system menu.
2. Open PARAMS → MOSAIC → Save project.
3. Enter Four notes and confirm.

The named project stores the two-section arrangement.

### Prove the saved version

1. Return to Mosaic, select Song slot 1, then open Channel.
2. Hold K1, tap channel 1 at (1,1), release K1 to unmute it temporarily.
3. With playback stopped, open PARAMS → MOSAIC → Load project.
4. Select Four notes and confirm.

Slot 1 returns to bass alone; the temporary change is removed.

### Replay the restored sections

1. Select slot 1.
2. Play four section passes and stop.

The saved bass-only/full-phrase alternation is restored. Continue with merge, recording or modulation task guides without replacing this saved version.

Resulting project: Named project Four notes contains both sections and restores their exact playback. Transport stopped with no held notes.
