features.title: Four-Bar Percussion, Bass and Chord Example
features.summary: Build a four-bar loop of drums, bass and a moving chord on three channels at 90 BPM in C major.
features.prose:
Build a four-bar loop on three channels: Oilcan 1 plays drums on channel 1, Polyperc 1 plays a bass line on channel 2 and Doubledecker plays chords on channel 3. The drum and bass phrases repeat unchanged in every bar. Only the chord roots change, in bar 4, so you hear the harmony move while the groove stays put. Play "Rhythm, bass and a changing chord" under Listen to hear the finished result first.

Before you start:

1. Set 90 BPM in Song tasks → Tempo & feel (E3, then K3). Keep the default Rate /1 on every channel: one step is a sixteenth note, 16 steps are one bar and 64 steps are four bars.

2. Set the range of channels 1–3 to steps 1–64.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, so that MIDI 37 (C#1) in the drum channel is not snapped to C major.

How notes are entered in these recipes: open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). E2 chooses the value (Trig, Note, Vel, Len, Chd1–Chd4). With no step held, E3 sets the channel default, which every step uses unless it has its own value. Hold K1 and tap a step to add or remove a trig on it. Hold a step and turn E3 to give that step its own value. Hold a step and press K2 to remove its own values. The grid shows sixteen steps at a time: bar 1 is steps 1–16, bar 2 is steps 17–32, bar 3 is steps 33–48 and bar 4 is steps 49–64, so move to the right sixteen-step page before you tap steps in a later bar. In bars after the first, add 16 to each step number of bar 1.

Build the channels in order: Percussion Channel, Bass Channel, Chord Channel. Press Play after each one to hear the loop grow before you add the next channel.

Finish with a contrasting section: open the Song Editor, copy the song slot and mute one channel in the copy (see Song Composition). Numeric MIDI notes are used throughout, because Masks shows MIDI 36, 48 and 60 as C1, C2 and C3 while other controls label octaves differently. Each n.b. player is unique: Polyperc 1 cannot be assigned to another channel once it is assigned to the bass.
features.musical_use: Build the rhythm, bass and chords as separate channels and play the loop after each one. Then change only the chord roots in bar 4 and listen to the harmony move over an unchanged groove.

details.title: Example Scope
details.text: The recipes give the exact settings of the recorded example, so you can reproduce it. The recording is the authored version only: other values you try are not part of it. Listen to the recording first if you want a target for each channel.

details.title: Recorded Example: Rhythm, bass and a changing chord
details.text:
Four bars at 90 BPM.

Channel 1, Oilcan 1, velocity 38: in every bar MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9, MIDI 38 on steps 4 and 12 and MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13.

Channel 2, Polyperc 1, velocity 42: in every bar MIDI 48 on steps 1, 5 and 13 and MIDI 55 on step 9.

Channel 3, Doubledecker, velocity 26, three steps long, Chd1 3rd and Chd2 5th: in bars 1 to 3 the chord roots are MIDI 60 on step 1 and MIDI 62 on step 9 of the bar. In bar 4 they are MIDI 67 on step 49 and MIDI 60 on step 57.

Play the loop and listen for the chord at the start of bar 4: the drums and bass are unchanged, while the chords move from C and D to G and C.

recipes.title: Percussion Channel
recipes.text:
Starting point: the three settings under Before you start are done (90 BPM, steps 1-64, Snap note masks to scale Off) and channel 1 is empty. The steps below build a six-hit drum bar and repeat it in all four bars.

1. Select channel 1 (1,1). Press E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Oilcan 1 and press K3 to assign it.

2. Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, turn E2 to Note and turn E3 to MIDI 36 (C1). Turn E2 to Vel and set 38. Turn E2 to Len and set ½ step. Every trig you add now plays MIDI 36 at velocity 38 for half a step. In the default Oilcan kit MIDI 36, 37 and 38 trigger three different drum timbres.

3. In bar 1 (steps 1-16), hold K1 and tap steps 1, 4, 5, 9, 12 and 13. Six trigs light on the grid.

4. Turn E2 back to Note. Hold step 4 and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then release. Do the same for step 12. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release, and do the same for step 13. Steps 1 and 9 keep the default MIDI 36.

5. Listen: press Play and hear bar 1 loop. MIDI 36 falls on beats 1 and 3, MIDI 37 on beats 2 and 4, and each MIDI 38 hit sounds one step before a MIDI 37 hit. Press Stop.

6. Repeat steps 3 and 4 in each of the other three bars, moving the grid to that bar's sixteen-step page first. Each pair below is a step number and its MIDI note:
Bar 2: 17/36, 20/38, 21/37, 25/36, 28/38, 29/37.
Bar 3: 33/36, 36/38, 37/37, 41/36, 44/38, 45/37.
Bar 4: 49/36, 52/38, 53/37, 57/36, 60/38, 61/37.

The channel now has 24 trigs in a repeating one-bar (four-beat) drum figure. Press Play and listen before you continue: the same bar repeats four times. Press Stop.

recipes.title: Bass Channel
recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays the drums and channel 2 is empty. Masks work as in the percussion recipe: E2 chooses the value, E3 sets it, and holding a step gives that step its own value.

1. Select channel 2 (2,1). Press E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Polyperc 1 and press K3 to assign it.

2. Open Masks. With no step held, turn E2 to Note and set MIDI 48 (C2), turn E2 to Vel and set 42, and turn E2 to Len and set ½ step.

3. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.

4. Select Note with E2, hold step 9 and turn E3 to MIDI 55 (G2), then release. Steps 1, 5 and 13 keep the default MIDI 48.

5. Listen: press Play. The bass plays C2 on beats 1, 2 and 4 and G2 on beat 3, under the drums. Press Stop.

6. Repeat steps 3 and 4 in bars 2 to 4, adding 16 to each step number of bar 1. Each trig list is followed by the step that takes MIDI 55:
Bar 2: trigs on 17, 21, 25, 29; 25 is MIDI 55.
Bar 3: trigs on 33, 37, 41, 45; 41 is MIDI 55.
Bar 4: trigs on 49, 53, 57, 61; 57 is MIDI 55.

Listen for the pitch pattern C, C, G, C repeating once per bar under the drums.

recipes.title: Chord Channel
recipes.text:
Starting point: channels 1 and 2 play the drums and bass; channel 3 is empty. Doubledecker plays several notes at once, so it can sound the chord. The grid shows sixteen steps at a time: bar 1 is steps 1-16, bar 2 steps 17-32, bar 3 steps 33-48 and bar 4 steps 49-64, so move to that bar's page before tapping its steps. Hold K1 and tap a step to add or remove a trig; hold a step and turn E3 to give that step its own value.

1. Select channel 3 (3,1). Press E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Doubledecker and press K3 to assign it.

2. Open Masks. With no step held, set Note to MIDI 60 (C3), Vel to 26 and Len to 3 steps. Select Chd1 and set 3rd; select Chd2 and set 5th. Every chord now plays the root plus the notes a third and a fifth above it in the scale.

3. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1 and 9. Select Note, hold step 9 and turn E3 to MIDI 62 (D3), then release. Step 1 keeps the default MIDI 60. Press Play: the chord alternates C-E-G and D-F-A, two chords a bar, quietly above the bass. Press Stop.

4. In bar 2, add trigs on steps 17 and 25, and set step 25 to MIDI 62 as in step 3.

5. In bar 3, add trigs on steps 33 and 41, and set step 41 to MIDI 62.

6. In bar 4, hold K1 and tap steps 49 and 57. Hold step 49 and set Note to MIDI 67 (G3). Step 57 keeps the default MIDI 60.

7. Listen to the whole four bars: press Play and wait for bar 4. The drums and bass repeat unchanged, but the chords move to G-B-D and then back to C-E-G. The chord intervals follow the C-major scale, so the 3rd above D is F and the 3rd above G is B. Press Stop.

review.native_gap: Mask controls and the authored three-player recording are demonstrated. Each player contributes verified solo PCM before the mix publishes. Suggested song-slot mutes use their own native workflow evidence; physical norns output and player installation are separate.

features.title: Adding a Ghost Note
features.summary: Compare two bars of main hits with two bars that add a quiet hit before an accent.
features.prose:
Compare two ways of playing the same four-beat drum figure on Oilcan 1. Bars 1 and 2 contain only the main hits (MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9, MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13, all at velocity 90). Bars 3 and 4 add one quiet hit, MIDI 38 at velocity 35, on step 12 of the bar, just before the accent on step 13. This is a ghost note: a soft hit that adds movement without changing the main hits.

Settings: 90 BPM, Rate /1 (the default, one step is a sixteenth note), range 1–64 and length ½ step on all notes. Play "Adding a Ghost Note" under Listen to hear the target, then build it with the first recipe.

Two further recipes follow: an optional probability variation of the ghost notes, and a separate, denser drum pattern at velocity 48 (the "Three sounds, one pocket" recording) that does not use ghost notes.
features.musical_use: Add one quiet hit just before an accent and compare the bar with and without it. Use a ghost note to add movement to a drum pattern without changing the main hits.

details.title: Comparison settings
details.text: The ghost-note comparison uses Oilcan 1. Every bar has four main attacks at velocity 90. Bars 3 and 4 each add one velocity-35 hit. The "Three sounds, one pocket" recording is an independent pattern at a constant velocity of 48. MIDI note mappings can differ on another instrument.

recipes.title: Make the recorded ghost-note comparison
recipes.text:
Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped and channel 1 selected. The numbers 1–64 are step numbers across four bars: bar 1 is steps 1–16, bar 2 is 17–32, bar 3 is 33–48 and bar 4 is 49–64. The grid shows sixteen steps at a time, so move to the sixteen-step page of the bar you are editing.


Setup (steps 1 to 3 prepare the instrument; do them once).

1. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–64 (see Channel Length). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Set 90 BPM: open Song tasks, choose Tempo & feel, turn E3 to 90 and press K3.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, then return to Mosaic. MIDI 37 (C#1) is not in C major and would otherwise be snapped to a scale note.


Main hits (steps 4 to 7 build and audition the bar without ghost notes).

4. Add the main hits. Open Pattern Trig on pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 in each bar: bar 1 uses 1, 5, 9, 13; bar 2 uses 17, 21, 25, 29; bar 3 uses 33, 37, 41, 45; bar 4 uses 49, 53, 57, 61. Sixteen trigs are lit.

5. Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, select Note and set MIDI 36 (C1), select Vel and set 90, select Len and set ½. All sixteen hits now play MIDI 36 at velocity 90.

6. Select Note. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release. Do the same for steps 13, 21, 29, 37, 45, 53 and 61, so that the second and fourth beat of each bar play MIDI 37.

7. Press Play and listen to four bars of main hits only, then press Stop. You hear two timbres alternating on beats 1 to 4 of every bar.


Ghost notes (steps 8 to 10 add the quiet hit to bars 3 and 4).

8. Return to Pattern Trig and tap step 44 (step 12 of bar 3) and step 60 (step 12 of bar 4).

9. Open Masks and hold step 44. Select Note and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then select Vel and set 35, then release step 44. Repeat both edits on step 60: first Note 38, then Vel 35.

10. Press Play. Bars 1 and 2 are unchanged. In bars 3 and 4 you hear a quiet third timbre one step before each MIDI 37 accent. Press Stop.


Undo (step 11 returns to the main-only phrase).

11. Open Masks, hold step 44 or 60 and press K2 to remove the values you set, then remove its trig on Pattern Trig.

recipes.title: Optional probability variation
recipes.text:
Starting point: the ghost-note comparison above, with ghost trigs on steps 44 and 60. This variation is not part of the recording because its random result changes from loop to loop. The extremes 0 and 100 are predictable, so check those first and then listen to 50.

1. Select channel 1 and open Channel tasks → Trig params. Turn E2 to a slot, press K2, turn E3 to Trig Probability and press K3. With no step held, turn E3 until the channel default reads 100, so every main hit plays every time.

2. Check 0 and 100 on the ghost notes. Move to the sixteen-step page for steps 33–48, hold step 44, turn E3 to 0 and release. Move to the page for steps 49–64 and set step 60 to 0 in the same way. Play: the ghost note never sounds in bars 3 and 4. Stop, set both steps to 100 and play again: it always sounds, exactly as in the recording.

3. Now set both steps to 50 in the same way. Play several loops. In bars 3 and 4 the quiet hit is sometimes present and sometimes missing, while the main hits always play. No two runs need match.

Return the two steps to 100 or remove the lock (hold the step and press K2) to restore the fixed comparison. For a captured example of probability at 0 and 100, see Trig Probability, "Turn chance into explicit rests".

recipes.title: Separate fixed percussion example
recipes.text:
This is the "Three sounds, one pocket" recording. It is a different, denser four-bar drum pattern and does not use ghost notes. It teaches one idea: a third sound (MIDI 38) fills the gaps between the two accents. Every hit is at velocity 48, a constant quiet level chosen so you hear rhythm and timbre only, with no accent or quiet ghost hit. Starting point: the ghost-note comparison recipe's steps 1 to 3 (Oilcan 1 on channel 1, range 1–64, 90 BPM, Snap note masks to scale Off) and an empty channel.

The bar template, as step/MIDI note: 1/36, 4/38, 5/37, 7/38, 9/36, 12/38, 13/37 and 15/38.

Step:  1   4   5   7   9   12  13  15

Note:  36  38  37  38  36  38  37  38

1. Open Masks. With no step held, set Note to MIDI 36, Vel to 48 and Len to ½.

2. Enter the trigs. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 13 and 15 to add eight trigs.

3. Edit the notes. Select Note and give steps 4, 7, 12 and 15 MIDI 38, and steps 5 and 13 MIDI 37, holding each step and turning E3. Steps 1 and 9 keep MIDI 36.

4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 in bars 2 to 4, adding 16 to each step number.

Play four bars. Listen for MIDI 36 on beats 1 and 3, MIDI 37 on beats 2 and 4, and the MIDI 38 hits filling the gaps between them. Unlike the ghost-note comparison, every hit has the same velocity, so nothing sounds accented or quiet. Listen to "Three sounds, one pocket" under Listen to compare.

review.native_gap: The new exact main-only/ghost comparison is authored and awaiting native capture. Existing fixed Oilcan evidence and probability endpoint scenes retain their separate scope. The optional 50% version is not a matching recording.

features.title: Changing Harmony with Scale Slots
features.summary: Compare the same relative patterns under C major for two bars and D major for two bars.
features.prose:
Hear one pair of relative-note patterns in two keys. Doubledecker on channel 1 plays an upper phrase and Polyperc 1 on channel 2 plays a bass. For bars 1 and 2 the global scale is C major (scale slot 1); for bars 3 and 4 it is D major (scale slot 2). The patterns hold scale degrees, not fixed pitches, and the Note masks stay X (unset), so changing the applied scale moves every pitch while rhythm, velocity and length stay the same. Play "Changing Harmony with Scale Slots" under Listen to hear the target.

Settings: 90 BPM, Rate /1 (the default, one step is a sixteenth note) and a 16-step range that loops once per bar. The bass velocity is 60 and its notes last ½ step in this comparison. The "A bass with room above it" recording is a different example, in fixed notes in C major.
features.musical_use: Change the applied scale slot to move a whole phrase and bass to a new key while keeping its rhythm. Use it to make a simple pattern sound like a chord progression.

details.title: Pitch and output scope
details.text: This comparison uses relative pattern notes (scale degrees) with the Note masks left at X. A Note mask would replace the pattern note and fix the pitch, so no scale change could move it. Polyperc 1 is assigned once, to the bass. Numeric MIDI notes are used for expected results because the controls label octaves differently.

recipes.title: Make the relative-note scale comparison
recipes.text:
Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped. Part 1 builds the upper phrase on channel 1, part 2 builds the bass on channel 2, part 3 prepares the second key and part 4 performs the change. In the note page, the column is the step and the row is the degree: y=7 is degree 0 (I), y=6 is degree 1 (II) and y=3 is degree 4 (V).

Part 1: upper phrase

1. Set 90 BPM (Song tasks, Tempo & feel, E3, K3). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Open the Scale editor (4,8). Slot 1 at (1,3) is the applied slot. Check Root C and Scale Major on the Scale screen; if you change either, press K3 to save it.

3. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1. Open Pattern Trig, select pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.

4. Open Pattern Note (tap Pattern (5,8) until Note is shown) and set the degrees: tap (1,7), (5,7) and (9,7) for degree 0, and (13,6) for degree 1. Set the channel range to steps 1-16.

5. Open Masks. Leave Note at X. Set Vel to 80 and Len to ½. Hold step 13 and set Vel to 50, then release. The phrase ends with a softer last note. Press Play and listen: in C major the upper phrase is MIDI 60, 60, 60, 62. Press Stop.

Part 2: bass

6. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 2 and select pattern 2 for the channel. On pattern 2, tap steps 1 and 9 on Pattern Trig, then on Pattern Note tap (1,7) for degree 0 and (9,3) for degree 4. Set the range to steps 1-16 and the channel octave to -1 with (9,8).

7. Open Masks with channel 2 selected, leave Note at X, set Vel to 60 and Len ½. Press Play: the bass adds MIDI 48 on beat 1 and MIDI 55 on beat 3 under the upper phrase. Press Stop.

Part 3: prepare the second key

8. While stopped, open the Scale editor. Hold K1 and press slot 2 at (2,3) to select it for editing without applying it. On the Scale screen set Root to D and Scale to Major with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save the slot. Slot 1 stays applied, so playback is still C major.

Part 4: perform the change (choose one)

9a. Stopped: play two bars in C major and stop. Short-press slot 2 at (2,3) to apply D major and play two more bars.

9b. Live: while playing, short-press slot 2 at (2,3) at the end of bar 2.

In D major the upper phrase becomes MIDI 62, 62, 62, 64 and the bass becomes MIDI 50 and 57: the same rhythm moved up a whole tone. Short-press slot 1 at (1,3) to restore C major.

recipes.title: Separate fixed bass-and-chord example
recipes.text:
Why it is here: this example uses fixed Note masks, so its pitches do not move when the scale changes. It is the counterpart of the scale-slot comparison above, where the notes are relative degrees that move with the scale, and it shows how to layer quiet chords above a bass. It is the "A bass with room above it" recording and stays in C major.

Starting point: an empty project, 90 BPM, Rate /1, Snap note masks to scale at its default, and channels 1 and 2 with their range set to steps 1-16 (hold step 1 and tap step 16 on the channel page).

1. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1. Open Masks and set Note to MIDI 48, Vel to 48 and Len to ½.

2. Hold K1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Hold step 9 and set Note to MIDI 55.

3. Assign Doubledecker to channel 2. Open Masks and set Note to MIDI 60, Vel to 32 and Len to 3 steps. Set Chd1 to 3rd and Chd2 to 5th.

4. Hold K1 and tap steps 1 and 9, then hold step 9 and set Note to MIDI 62.

5. Press Play. The bass plays C2, C2, G2, C2 on beats 1 to 4 and the chords sound C-E-G on beat 1 and D-F-A on beat 3. The chords are deliberately quieter (velocity 32) than the bass (velocity 48), so they sit above it without covering it.

review.native_gap: The new exact C-to-D relative-note comparison is authored and awaiting native capture. Existing fixed C-major bass-and-chord evidence remains separate.

features.title: Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops
features.summary: Use independent channel lengths to create a 12-step repeating relationship.
features.prose:
Run two channels at the same clock rate with different lengths: channel 1 loops a four-step phrase and channel 2 loops a three-step phrase. Both channels start together on step 1, drift apart, and meet again after 12 steps, the smallest number that both 4 and 3 divide into. At the default Rate /1 and 90 BPM, 12 steps last two seconds. Playback is continuous: each channel simply starts its own loop again when it reaches the end of its range.

1. On channel 1, assign a pattern with active steps 1–4. Using the default C-major scale, set relative pattern notes 0, 1, 2 and 3, which produce MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Set the velocities to 127, 117, 107 and 97 and each note length to one step. Set the range to steps 1–4 (hold step 1, tap step 4, release step 1).

2. On channel 2, assign the same pattern and set the range to steps 1–3.

3. Open channel 2 Masks. With no step held, set the channel defaults to Note MIDI 79, Vel 40 and Len ½.

4. Hold step 2 and set Note MIDI 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Release the step. Channel 2 now repeats MIDI 79, 81, 79, independent of the four notes on channel 1.

5. Start playback. Both channels begin together. Compare their first steps again after 12 steps (about two seconds).

6. Stop playback before changing the arrangement.

Use separate MIDI routes for the two instruments. For internal sound, assign different supported players, for example Polyperc 1 for channel 1 and Doubledecker for channel 2. Song transitions and reset options can restart channels earlier than 12 steps; the second recipe shows how.
features.musical_use: Give two channels different lengths so a short and a long phrase drift apart and realign. Use it for evolving rhythmic patterns from simple loops, and use song reset options when each section should restart together.

details.title: Example Scope
details.text: These recipes specify suggested musical settings. Attached audio demonstrates only its authored version. Suggested variations are not covered by that recording.

recipes.title: Comparing the Loop Alignment
recipes.text:
Starting point: the six steps above are done and playback is stopped. Both channels run at the same rate. At 90 BPM and Rate /1 one step is a sixth of a second, so you can count 12 steps in two seconds.

1. Press Play and count steps. Channel 1 plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 and then repeats, so it completes three phrases in 12 steps. Channel 2 plays MIDI 79, 81, 79 and repeats, so it completes four phrases in the same 12 steps.

2. Listen at step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together. They do not coincide again on steps 2 to 12: for example, on step 4 channel 1 plays MIDI 65 while channel 2 starts a new phrase with MIDI 79.

3. Listen at step 13, two seconds after step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together again, and the pattern repeats every 12 steps. Press Stop when you have heard the alignment.

4. Optional extra check, unrelated to the alignment: with both channels playing, try a reversed range on channel 1. Hold step 4 as the start, press step 2 as the end and release both. The reversed range is rejected with a message, the ranges stay 1–4 and 1–3, and neither phrase changes timing.

recipes.title: Comparing Song Boundary Resets
recipes.text:
Starting point: the two looping channels above (channel 1 range 1–4, channel 2 range 1–3), with Song slot 1 holding them and playback stopped. Song mode is On by default, so the slots play in turn, and Reset on song seq change (PARAMS > MOSAIC) is On by default while Reset on pattern repeat is Off. This comparison hears how the first option changes both channels at a slot boundary.

1. Copy the slot. Open the Song Editor, hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1) and release slot 1. Slot 2 is now a copy of slot 1, so slots 1 and 2 play one after the other.

2. Set the slot length. Use the global length fader at the lower left of the Song Editor (see Adjusting Song Sequence Length) to set 10 steps. The length belongs to the whole song, so both slots get it. 10 is not a multiple of 4 or of 3, so each channel is part-way through its loop when a slot ends.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and check that Reset on song seq change reads On. Play both slots. At the start of slot 2 both channels restart from step 1: channel 1 plays MIDI 60 and channel 2 plays MIDI 79. The 4-against-3 pattern starts again from the beginning in every slot. Press Stop.

4. Set Reset on song seq change to Off and play both slots again. Now neither channel restarts: at the start of slot 2 channel 1 continues with MIDI 64, the third note of its phrase (10 steps is two phrases and two steps), and channel 2 continues with MIDI 81, the second note of its phrase (10 steps is three phrases and one step). The two channels no longer meet at the slot boundary. Press Stop.

5. Set Reset on song seq change back to On to restore the default.

Use Off when you want the 12-step relationship to carry across slots without a restart; use On when each slot should begin with both loops on their first step.

recipes.title: Run two channels at different lengths
recipes.text:
Starting point: two channels with audible notes. Give each channel a voice (for example Oilcan 1 on channel 1 and Polyperc 1 on channel 2, or any two MIDI outputs) and set Note, Vel and Len on each channel's Masks page as in Make your first loop (a channel needs at least one audible note to be heard).

Enter the two patterns. Tap Pattern (5,8) for the Trig view. In pattern 1 tap steps (1,4), (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4): a drum pattern with trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. In pattern 2 tap steps (1,4), (3,4) and (4,4): a short figure with trigs on steps 1, 3 and 4.

1. Channel 1: tap (1,1) and assign pattern 1 at (1,2). Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)), tap step 16 ((16,4)), then release step 1. Steps 1-16 on row 4 are now brighter.

2. Channel 2: tap (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 ((5,4)), then release step 1. On this channel only steps 1-5 are brighter.

3. Tap Play at (1,8). The drum channel repeats every 16 steps (four hits per bar) and the figure repeats every 5 steps, so its three notes slide across the drum hits. Listen for the figure landing on a different drum beat each bar.

4. Keep listening until the start of drum bar 6. After 80 steps (five drum bars, sixteen figure passes) both channels start together again. 80 is the first step count that both 16 and 5 divide. Tap Play again to stop.

If the song moves to another song pattern, channels are reset together while Reset at Song Sequence Change (on by default) is enabled, so the 80-step cycle only completes while the same song pattern keeps playing. Use the Options page to change how channels of different length behave. The captured example [Play sixteen steps against five](#loops-that-meet/loops-sixteen-against-five) builds this setup and plays the 80 steps until both channels start together again. The captured example "Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed" shows the range gesture and what happens when the end comes before the start.

review.native_gap: The unchanged native case verifies independent four-/three-step phrases, simultaneous first onsets, exact timing and gates, and a rejected range edit preserving both schedules. The 12-step relationship is the least common multiple of those lengths. Physical sound and the optional song-reset comparison are separately scoped.

doctor-local-capture-and-paint.title: Record audio and paint detected attacks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 has a MIDI device on OUT 1 with pattern 1 assigned (range steps 1-64) and playback is stopped. Play a steady loop into the norns audio input, with a short thump on every beat at 120 BPM; the example uses a 29-second loop, so use one at least that long. Press Pattern (5,8) and choose the Rhythm Doctor algorithm at (16,2). Rhythm Doctor opens on the norns: Record READY, Tempo AUTO, Manual BPM 120, Input STEREO. The bank is EMPTY, so no lane buttons are lit yet.

Turn E2 to Tempo and E3 to MANUAL, then press K3 to confirm: Manual BPM reads 120, so you tell Doctor the tempo instead of letting it estimate. Tap Record at (1,2). Doctor starts listening to the audio input; the screen reads CAPTURE, MORE AUDIO NEEDED, RECORDING.

Let the take run until the screen reads ENOUGH / REC OR K3 (about 25 seconds of the loop; this is real time, so wait for the readout), then press K3. Doctor stops recording and analyses it: ANALYSING, Lanes BD SD CYM.

Wait while the norns analyses the recording; a short take takes roughly half a minute, and this wait cannot be shortened. When it finishes, the Window screen shows READY with Window bar 1, Window step 1, Sensitivity 0 and Paint policy TOGGLE. Window bar moves the view by 16 steps and Window step by one, Sensitivity is set for the selected lane, and Paint policy (Toggle, Add or Replace) decides how painted hits meet trigs already in the pattern. The lane buttons BD (bass drum), SD (snare) and CYM (cymbal) light at (3,2) to (5,2).

Select the BD lane (bass drum) at (3,2) and tap Paint at (16,8). The grid flashes the detected bass-drum hits on steps 11, 15, 19 and so on every fourth step to step 63, one per beat at 120 BPM. The first hit is on step 11, not step 1, because Manual starts the phrase at the very start of the recording and the first thump comes some way into it. This is only a preview: nothing is stored yet. The screen reads PAINT, Policy TOGGLE, Destination 1.
Press Paint at (16,8) again to commit. The tooltip reads Pattern painted and the flashing steps become solid trigs in pattern 1, on the same steps as the preview. The captured bank stays unchanged.

Press Channel (3,8), then Play at (1,8). Channel 1 sends MIDI note 60 on each painted step at velocities near 123, taken from the recording, one hit per beat; the painted steps are the bass-drum hits. The frame shows the Masks screen with the pattern stopped; check the MIDI strip below for the notes sent. Press Play again after about three seconds to stop.

doctor-local-capture-and-paint.starting_state: Channel 1 has a MIDI device on OUT 1 with pattern 1 assigned (range steps 1-64), and playback is stopped. The audio input will receive a synthetic test recording, 29 seconds of a short thump on every beat at 120 BPM, once Record starts. Tempo will be set to Manual at 120 BPM.

doctor-local-auto-capture-and-paint.title: Record audio in Auto mode and paint detected attacks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 has a MIDI device on OUT 1 with pattern 1 assigned (range steps 1-64) and playback is stopped. Play a steady loop into the norns audio input, with a short thump on every beat at 120 BPM; the example uses a 29-second loop, so use one at least that long. Press Pattern (5,8) and choose the Rhythm Doctor algorithm at (16,2). Rhythm Doctor opens on the norns: Record READY, Tempo AUTO, Manual BPM 120, Input STEREO. The bank is EMPTY, so no lane buttons are lit yet.
Leave Tempo on AUTO and tap Record at (1,2). Doctor starts listening to the audio input and will estimate the tempo and phrase start itself. The screen reads CAPTURE, MORE AUDIO NEEDED, LISTENING.

Let the take run until the screen reads ENOUGH / REC OR K3 (about 25 seconds of the loop; this is real time, so wait for the readout), then press K3. Doctor stops recording and analyses it: ANALYSING, Lanes BD SD CYM.

Wait while the norns analyses the recording; a short take takes roughly half a minute, and this wait cannot be shortened. When it finishes, the Window screen shows READY with Window bar 1, Window step 1, Sensitivity 0 and Paint policy TOGGLE. Window bar moves the view by 16 steps and Window step by one, Sensitivity is set for the selected lane, and Paint policy (Toggle, Add or Replace) decides how painted hits meet trigs already in the pattern. The lane buttons BD (bass drum), SD (snare) and CYM (cymbal) light at (3,2) to (5,2).

Select the BD lane (bass drum) at (3,2) and tap Paint at (16,8). The grid flashes the detected bass-drum hits on steps 10, 14, 18 and so on every fourth step to step 62, one per beat. The first hit is on step 10, not step 1, because Auto estimates the phrase start from the recording and the first thump comes some way into it; a Manual-tempo take of the same loop shows it on step 11. This is only a preview: nothing is stored yet. The screen reads PAINT, Policy TOGGLE, Destination 1.
Press Paint at (16,8) again to commit. The tooltip reads Pattern painted and the flashing steps become solid trigs in pattern 1, on the same steps as the preview. The captured bank stays unchanged.

Press Channel (3,8), then Play at (1,8). Channel 1 sends MIDI note 60 on each painted step at velocities between 123 and 126, taken from the recording, one hit per beat. The frame shows the Masks screen with the pattern stopped; check the MIDI strip below for the notes sent. Press Play again after about three seconds to stop.

doctor-local-auto-capture-and-paint.starting_state: Channel 1 has a MIDI device on OUT 1 with pattern 1 assigned (range steps 1-64), and playback is stopped. The audio input will receive a synthetic test recording, 29 seconds of a short thump on every beat at 120 BPM, once Record starts. Tempo stays on Auto.

first-sound-equal-note-loop.title: Create a four-step loop from an empty project

steps.caption: Starting point: a new, empty project, stopped, with Record off. No channel has an output, no pattern has trigs and no masks are set. Tap Channel (3,8): the header reads CH01. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, choose Device with E2 and press K3. Turn E3 one detent to the first output in the list and press K3 to apply it. Whichever name the row shows is fine for this walk-through; in your own project pick the note-capable output you set up in Connect a sound. The Device page for CH01 stays on screen.
Tap Pattern (5,8) for the Trig view of pattern 1, then tap steps (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Four steps light on row 4. Each lit step is a trig, a moment where a note will sound.

Tap Channel (3,8), then tap pattern slot (1,2) to feed pattern 1 to channel 1. Next limit the channel to four steps: hold step 1 at (1,4), tap step 4 at (4,4), then release step 1. Hold the first step of the range, tap the last, then let go. The channel now loops steps 1 to 4, and those four steps are brighter than the rest of row 4.

Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll up to Masks with E2 and press K3. Select Note with E2, then turn E3 right until the screen reads C3, which is MIDI 60. The Note row shows the name, so stop on the readout instead of counting. With no step held this sets the channel note for all steps.
Turn E2 one detent to select Vel, then turn E3 right until the screen reads 80. Every step now plays at velocity 80, a medium-loud level.

Turn E2 one detent to select Len, then turn E3 until the screen reads 1/2, so each note lasts half a step. Tap Play (1,8) to hear four equal C notes (MIDI 60, velocity 80) repeating as the playhead runs along steps 1 to 4; the frame shows the Masks screen, so listen to your output or check the MIDI strip below. Tap Play again to stop.

first-sound-equal-note-loop.starting_state: A new empty project, stopped, with Record off. No channel has an output, no pattern has trigs and no masks are set. One MIDI output is available to choose on channel 1.

mask-precedence.title: Set channel and step note masks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads G3 (MIDI 67). The screen shows the note name, so stop on the readout. This is the channel note mask: all four steps now play G, and their velocities stay as they were.

Hold step 1 at (1,4). The header gains ST01, which means edits now apply to that step only. Turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (MIDI 72, five detents up from G3). Step 1 has its own note, which overrides the channel default.
Release step 1. The header loses ST01 and the screen returns to the channel default, G3. Playback now starts with C4 (72) and continues G, G, G: a step mask beats the channel mask.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads D4 (MIDI 74) and release the step. Steps 1 and 2 each have their own note (C4, D4), and steps 3 and 4 still play the channel note G.
Hold step 1 and press K2, then release the step. Step 1's mask is cleared, so it plays G3 again from the channel default, and step 2 still plays D4.
With no step held, hold K1 and press K2. Every step exception is cleared at once and the channel default stays: the screen still reads G3 and all four steps play G again.

mask-precedence.starting_state: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. No masks are set, so every step uses the pattern's own note. The sequencer is stopped and the Channel screen is showing.

mask-expression.title: Set velocity and length masks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Vel. The value reads X: there is no channel velocity mask, so every step plays the velocity it has in pattern 1. X means inherit.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 50. This channel velocity mask replaces the pattern's velocities: every note now plays at 50, so the whole phrase is softer. Pitch and timing are unchanged.

Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads 90 and release the step. A step mask overrides the channel mask, so step 1 plays at 90 as an accent while steps 2 to 4 keep the channel velocity of 50. The screen goes back to the channel value, 50.

Hold step 2 at (2,4) and keep holding it. Turn E3 left until the screen reads 0. Velocity 0 is a silent step, which is different from X: X means inherit and still plays. Step 2 is now muted, so a pass plays steps 1, 3 and 4 only. Step 2 is still held in this frame.
Release step 2. The screen returns to 50, but step 2 stays silent: read the MIDI strip, where the loop plays C3 (60) at 90, then E3 (64) and F3 (65) at 50, and step 2's D is missing.
Hold step 2 again, press K2 to clear its masks and release it. The step mask is gone, so step 2 plays at the channel velocity of 50 again and step 1 keeps its accent at 90: velocities 90, 50, 50, 50.
With no step held, turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until the screen reads 1/2. All four notes now have a half-step gate. The velocities stay at 90, 50, 50 and 50.

mask-expression.starting_state: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. No masks are set (every mask reads X), the sequencer is stopped and the Channel screen is showing.

mask-chords.title: Set chord masks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and no masks are set. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Chd1. The four chord rows Chd1-Chd4 add voices above each step's root, and X means no voice.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 3rd (two detents). Every step now plays its root and the scale third above it: 60+64, 62+65, 64+67, 65+69. Chord values are scale intervals, not MIDI numbers. Read the MIDI strip: each step sends its root and its chord note together.
Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)) and turn E3 right until the screen reads 5th (two more detents). Step 1 now plays 60 and 67; the screen shows 5th while the step is held.

Release step 1. The screen shows the channel default 3rd again, but step 1 keeps its own fifth: the phrase is 60+67, then 62+65, 64+67, 65+69. Read the MIDI strip: step 1 sends 60 and 67 together, the other steps their roots and thirds.
Hold step 1, press K2 and release the step. The fifth is cleared and step 1 returns to the channel third: 60+64, then 62+65, 64+67, 65+69.

mask-chords.starting_state: Channel 1 sends to the emulator test device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. No masks are set.

mask-melody-ending.title: Change the ending of a four-note melody

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The value reads X.
With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads C3 (MIDI 60). The channel note replaces the pattern's notes, so the MIDI strip shows C3 four times; the velocities stay the pattern's.
Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (12 detents) and release the step. The screen goes back to C3, and the loop now starts on C4 (72) before three C3 notes.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 right until it reads D4 (14 detents) and release. The MIDI strip shows 72, 74, 60, 60.
Hold step 3 at (3,4), turn E3 right until it reads G4 (19 detents) and release. The MIDI strip shows 72, 74, 79, 60.
Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 right until it reads E4 (16 detents) and release. The melody ends on E4: 72, 74, 79, 76.
Hold step 4 and turn E3 left until it reads D4 (two detents), then release. Only step 4 changed: the phrase now ends 72, 74, 79, 74.
Hold step 4 and turn E3 left two more detents until it reads C4, then release. The phrase ends on the root: 72, 74, 79, 72.

mask-ghost-note.title: Set a ghost note and an accent

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Vel. The value reads X.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 80. The channel velocity replaces the pattern's velocities: every note plays at 80. This loop plays C, D, E and F, not one repeated note, so read the pitches in the MIDI strip.
Hold step 3 at (3,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads 100 and release. Step 3 is the accent: the MIDI strip shows 80, 80, 100, 80.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 left until the screen reads 35 and release. Step 2 is now a soft ghost note before the accent: 80, 35, 100, 80.

mask-trigs.title: Add and remove trig masks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 in an eight-step loop. Steps 1-4 hold four notes and steps 5-8 are empty. No masks are set. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The value reads X.

With no step held, turn E3 right until Note reads C3 (MIDI 60). The channel default replaces the pattern's notes on every step, so all four steps now play C3: read the MIDI strip, which shows C3 four times at the velocities the pattern already had (127, 117, 107, 97).
Turn E2 to Vel and turn E3 right until it reads 80. The channel velocity replaces the pattern's velocities too: the MIDI strip now shows C3 at velocity 80 four times.

Turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until it reads 1/2. The four notes now have a half-step gate. A trig mask has no pattern note of its own, so a trig you add next will use these three channel defaults.

Turn E2 back to Note. Hold step 5 at (5,4), turn E3 right four detents until the screen reads E3 (MIDI 64) and release it. Step 5 now has its own note, but it still has no trig, so nothing new sounds. Then hold K1 and tap step 5, release the step, then release K1. A trig mask now forces step 5 on, so the loop plays a fifth note after the four notes on steps 1-4: E3 (64) at velocity 80, shown in the MIDI strip and by the new lit step 5 on the grid.

Hold K1 and tap step 5 again, release the step, then release K1. The same gesture toggles the trig mask off, so the loop returns to four C3 notes on steps 1-4. Step 5 keeps its note mask but has no trig, so it stays silent.

mask-trigs.starting_state: Channel 1 plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 followed by four empty steps, in an eight-step loop. No masks are set.

random-pentatonic-on.title: Lock random notes to pentatonic: On

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent. are both On, and no trig params are assigned yet.

steps.title: Check Lock random to pent.
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 right to On (the default). The row shows On. Notes moved by Random Note or Twos Random Note will snap to the five-note selection.

steps.title: Turn Lock merged to pent. Off (not needed here)
steps.caption: Select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 left to Off. The row shows Off. That option only affects notes made by merge modes, so it has no effect on this lesson's random notes; the recording turns it Off here and you can leave it On.

steps.title: Assign Random Note
steps.caption: Close the menu. On Channel tasks > Trig params assign Random Note to the first slot. The slot list shows Random Note; its value is still 0, so the pattern is unchanged.

steps.title: Assign Twos Random Note
steps.caption: Assign Twos Random Note to the second slot in the same way. It stays at 0, so it adds nothing to this lesson; only Random Note is used.

steps.title: Hear random notes locked to pentatonic
steps.caption: Select the Random Note slot, turn E3 right to 4 and press Play (1,8). Random Note 4 offsets each note by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees chosen at random; with Lock random to pent. On every result snaps to the five-note selection C D E G A. Listen to several loops and press Stop. The recorded run begins 60, 64, 64, 64, 60, 64, 67, 64: step 4, a plain F (65), now sounds as E (64). Random notes change on every run, so your notes will differ. A step whose random offset is 0 keeps its own note, so a plain pattern note outside the selection, such as F, can still sound.

random-pentatonic-off.title: Lock random notes to pentatonic: Off

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. steps.title: Turn Lock random to pent. Off
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 left to Off. The row shows Off. Random note offsets will now land on any degree of the seven-note scale.

steps.title: Turn Lock merged to pent. Off (not needed here)
steps.caption: Select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 left to Off. The row shows Off. That option only affects notes made by merge modes, so it has no effect on this lesson's random notes; the recording turns it Off here and you can leave it On.

steps.title: Assign Random Note
steps.caption: Close the menu. On Channel tasks > Trig params assign Random Note to the first slot. The slot list shows Random Note; its value is still 0, so the pattern is unchanged.

steps.title: Assign Twos Random Note
steps.caption: Assign Twos Random Note to the second slot in the same way. It stays at 0, so it adds nothing to this lesson; only Random Note is used.

steps.title: Hear the plain pattern
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) with Random Note at 0: the pattern repeats C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) with no random offsets. Stop playback.

steps.title: Hear random notes on all seven degrees
steps.caption: Raise Random Note to 4 in single steps: turn E3 right once, press Play (1,8) and Stop, and repeat until it reads 4. Random Note 4 offsets each note by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees chosen at random, and with Lock random to pent. Off the results use all seven degrees of C major. The recorded final run begins 57, 64, 67, 62, 64, 59, 65, 65. F (65) and B (59) are in C major but outside C D E G A, so hearing them shows the lock is off. Random notes change on every run: play several loops and expect F and B to turn up now and then.

merged-pentatonic-on.title: Lock merged notes to pentatonic: On

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. Lock merged to pent. is at its default On. Only pattern 1 exists and is assigned to channel 1; patterns 2 and 3 are built in the next steps.

steps.title: Check Lock merged to pent.
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 right to On (the default). The row shows On.

steps.title: Enter pattern 1
steps.caption: Close the menu. Press Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1) and tap (1,7), (2,5), (3,3) and (4,1) to rewrite its four notes as scale degrees I, III, V, VII (C E G B). The four notes light on the grid.

steps.title: Enter pattern 2
steps.caption: Choose pattern 2 at (2,1), add four trigs on steps 1 to 4 and tap (1,5), (2,3), (3,1) and (4,7): degrees III, V, VII, I (E G B C). Pattern 2 is a second voice that overlaps pattern 1 on every step.

steps.title: Build pattern 3 as a velocity source
steps.caption: Choose pattern 3 at (3,1), add four trigs on steps 1 to 4 and put their notes on the top row, (1,1) to (4,1); the four top-row notes light. Pattern 3 will never be assigned to the channel. It is only a velocity source: every trig has the default velocity 100, and its notes are ignored by the merge, so the notes you hear come only from patterns 1 and 2.

steps.title: Choose Strategy ALL
steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), tap pattern slot 2 at (2,2) so patterns 1 and 2 are both assigned, then press the trig merge key at (14,8) twice. Strategy moves from Skip to Only to ALL and the key lights at medium brightness. With Skip every step both patterns share would be silenced; ALL lets every trig sound.

steps.title: Take velocity from pattern 3
steps.caption: Hold the velocity merge key (16,8), tap pattern slot 3 at (3,2) and release. Slots 1 and 2 stay lit as the assigned patterns and slot 3 stays dim because it is not assigned: it only supplies the velocity of the merged notes. Note merge stays on its default, Average.

steps.title: Hear the averaged phrase snap to pentatonic
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8), listen to two loops and press Play again to stop. The average of each step's degrees is II, IV, VI, IV, which in C major is D, F, A, F. With Lock merged to pent. On, F is not in the C D E G A selection and snaps to the nearer E, so you hear 62, 64, 69, 64 (D E A E) at velocity 100, taken from pattern 3. Compare the Off lesson, which plays F (65) on steps 2 and 4.

steps.title: Switch Note merge to Higher and listen
steps.caption: Tap the note merge key at (15,8) once; it brightens as Note merge moves from Average to Higher. Press Play (1,8), listen to two loops and press Play again to stop. Higher adds the spread (the highest minus the lowest degree) to the rounded average, so the four steps become degrees IV, VI, VIII and X: F, A, C and E in C major. Lock merged to pent. On snaps F to the nearer E, so the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step" shows 64, 69, 72, 76 at velocity 100. Compare the Off lesson, which plays F (65) on the first step.

steps.title: Hear the averaged phrase unchanged

song-tempo-across-slots.title: Set Tempo and feel across Song slots

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Song slot 1 holds the four-step phrase on channel 1 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and slot 2 is a copy with channel 1 raised one octave. Song mode is Off, the tempo is 90 BPM, slot 1 is selected and playback is stopped. Song tasks > Tempo / feel is the screen that holds the song's one tempo, next to its swing and shuffle feel.

steps.title: Turn Tempo down to 30
steps.caption: Close the menu. With slot 1 selected at (1,1), turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Tempo / feel and press K3. Turn E3 all the way down: Tempo reads 30, the lowest value.

steps.title: Hear slot 1 at 30 BPM
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then press Play (1,8) to hear the phrase at 30 BPM and press Play again to stop. Swing type stays Swing and Swing 0.

steps.title: Slot 2 reads the same tempo
steps.caption: Select slot 2 at (2,1), the copy that plays an octave higher, then turn E1 to Song tasks, E2 to Tempo / feel and press K3. It already reads 30: tempo belongs to the whole song, not to one slot.

steps.title: Turn Tempo up to 300
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) and Stop to hear slot 2 at 30 BPM. With slot 2 selected, open Tempo / feel again, turn E3 all the way up: Tempo reads 300, the highest value. Press K3 to apply.

steps.title: Hear slot 2 at 300 BPM
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) to hear slot 2 at 300 BPM, ten times as fast as before, then press Play again to stop.

steps.title: Slot 1 reads 300
steps.caption: Select slot 1 at (1,1) and open Tempo / feel again. It reads 300, the value you set while slot 2 was selected.

steps.title: Set Tempo back to 90
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) to hear slot 1 at 300 BPM and Stop. Open Tempo / feel on slot 1, turn E3 down to 30, then up 60 detents to 90, and press K3 to apply.

steps.title: Hear slot 1 at 90 BPM
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) to hear slot 1 at 90 BPM, the starting tempo, then press Play again to stop.

steps.title: Slot 2 follows to 90
steps.caption: Select slot 2 at (2,1) and open Tempo / feel. It reads 90 too: the tempo you set on any slot applies to every slot.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). Only Song slot 1 is filled. Song mode is Off, the global length is 32 steps (fader cell (4,7) on the Song page; Song Playback reads Global length 32) and playback is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

steps.title: Copy a populated slot
steps.caption: Close the menu and press Song at grid (6,8). Hold slot 1 at (1,1), press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both: slot 1 is copied to slot 2. Tap (2,1) to select slot 2. The top row now reads slot 1 mid-bright (filled), slot 2 bright (selected) and slot 3 dim (empty). The norns shows Slot setup for SONG 02 with the message Song sequence 2 selected.

assertion.characterisation: Stopped selected slot is also bright (outside the README playing-only wording).

steps.title: Give slot 2 Repeats 2
steps.caption: Turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Slot setup and press K3. Turn E3 up to Repeats 2 and press K3 to apply. Song mode is Off, so Repeats does not hold the slot for extra passes here; it only shows as the pass count on Song Playback.

steps.title: Play the selected slot
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8) and then Play at (1,8). Slot 2 plays the phrase C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and stays bright; slot 1 stays mid-bright and empty slot 3 stays dim. Song Playback reads Playing SONG 02, Pass 1 / 2, Song mode MANUAL.

assertion.characterisation: Stopped selected slot is also bright (outside the README playing-only wording).

steps.title: Queue slot 1 while slot 2 plays
steps.caption: Do these in order. 1: press Stop (1,8). 2: press Song (6,8) and select slot 1 at (1,1). 3: press Channel (3,8) and tap octave +1 at (11,8), so slot 1 sounds an octave higher. 4: press Song (6,8) again, select slot 2 at (2,1) and press Play (1,8). 5: while slot 2 sounds, press slot 1 at (1,1) to queue it. Slot 1 now blinks between dim and mid-bright (a still shows one moment of the blink) while slot 2 stays bright. Song mode is Off, so playback continues on slot 2 until one pass of its sequence ends.

assertion.characterisation: Characterisation outside README: populated queued slot alternates exact LED levels1/7 on the source0.4s blink clock; controlled samples are exactly0.4s apart. Real native visual dwell bounds derive from the20Hz grid flush plus the existing10ms clock allowance; fast observations do not assume the global blink phase.

steps.title: Hear the queued slot take over
steps.caption: Do nothing for about five seconds: slot 2 plays its full 32 steps (32 steps at one sixth of a second each). Slot 1 then becomes bright and plays its phrase an octave higher (MIDI 72, 74, 76, 77); slot 2 returns to mid-bright. Press Stop at (1,8). Song Playback reads Playing SONG 01.

steps.title: Erase by copying an empty slot
steps.caption: With playback stopped, hold empty slot 3 at (3,1), press slot 2 at (2,1) and release: the empty slot is copied over slot 2 and erases it. Tap slot 1 at (1,1). Slot 1 is bright; slots 2 and 3 are both dim. There is no undo.

assertion.characterisation: Stopped selected slot is also bright (outside the README playing-only wording).

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Song slot 1 holds the four-step phrase (channel 1: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and has just been copied to slot 2, which is selected. The top row of the Song page reads slot 1 mid-bright, slot 2 bright and slot 3 dim. Song mode is Off and playback is stopped. Repeats is the number of passes a slot plays before Song mode advances to the next slot; it ranges from 1 to 16.

assertion.characterisation: Stopped selected slot is also bright (outside the README playing-only wording).

steps.title: Open Slot setup: Repeats 1
steps.caption: With slot 2 selected, turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Slot setup and press K3. Slot setup lists Repeats and Song mode. Repeats reads 1 for this freshly copied slot.

steps.title: Set Repeats 16
steps.caption: Repeats is already selected. Turn E3 up 15 detents to 16 and press K3 to apply. The screen shows OK and Repeats reads 16, the highest value.

steps.title: Set Repeats 2
steps.caption: Turn E3 down 14 detents to 2 and press K3 to apply. Repeats reads 2. With Song mode on, slot 2 would play two passes before the next slot. Song mode is Off in this example, so the value does not hold the slot here; it shows as Pass 1 / 2 on Song Playback.

steps.title: Play the same phrase with motion On
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8), let the four-note pattern play and press Play again to stop. The notes (60, 62, 64, 65), velocities (127, 117, 107, 97), gates and transport LED are exactly what they were with UI motion Off: it changes only what the screen draws.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device at 90 BPM, Rate /1. Only Song slot 1 is filled, Song mode is at its default On and playback is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

steps.title: Shorten the song to 8 steps
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8) and tap fader cell (2,7) on the Song page, then tap (8,7) seven times: Song Playback reads Global length 8, so one pass of a slot lasts 8 steps (about 1.3 seconds).

steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2 an octave higher with Repeats 2
steps.caption: Hold slot 1 at (1,1), press slot 2 at (2,1) and release; tap (2,1) to select slot 2. Press Channel (3,8) and tap octave +1 at (11,8), then press Song (6,8). Turn E1 to Song tasks, E2 to Slot setup and press K3, turn E3 up one detent and press K3: Repeats reads 2 for slot 2.

steps.title: Play slot 1 once
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 is bright and plays C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65); Song Playback reads Pass 1 / 1. Watch the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step": each note is one sixth of a second after the last.

steps.title: Slot 2, first of two passes
steps.caption: After eight steps the song moves on by itself. Slot 2 is bright and slot 1 mid-bright; the phrase sounds an octave higher (MIDI 72, 74, 76, 77) and Song Playback reads Pass 1 / 2.

steps.title: Slot 2, second pass
steps.caption: Slot 2 stays bright and plays the same octave-higher phrase again; Song Playback reads Pass 2 / 2. Repeats held the slot for exactly two passes.

steps.title: The song loops back to slot 1
steps.caption: Slot 3 is empty, so after slot 2 the song returns to slot 1: it is bright again, the notes drop back to C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and Song Playback reads Pass 1 / 1. Press Stop at (1,8).

panic-stops-sounding-note.title: Panic silences a note that is still sounding

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped and three MIDI ports are connected. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

steps.title: Start one long note
steps.caption: On Channel, hold step 1 at (1,4) and tap step 24 to set the channel range to steps 1 to 24. Open Pattern (5,8) and tap steps 2, 3 and 4 to clear those trigs, then hold step 1 and tap step 24 to give the one remaining trig a length of 24 steps: four seconds. Press Song (6,8), then Play (1,8). C (MIDI 60) starts and keeps sounding; the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step" shows only its Note On.

steps.title: Hold Channel to panic
steps.caption: While the note sounds, hold Channel (3,8), a page you are not on, for about two seconds and release it. The note is cut off about a second and a quarter after it started, well before its four seconds are up: the MIDI strip shows the 6,144 note-offs of the panic sweep, 128 notes on each of the 16 MIDI channels of the three ports. The screen stays on Song and playback carries on, so C starts again when the loop comes round. Press Stop at (1,8).

pocket-ghost-bar.title: Build a four-bar groove with ghost trigs

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped and the norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

steps.title: Set a 64-step range and add the main hits
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), hold step 1 at (1,4) and tap step 64 at (16,7): the range is now four rows of sixteen steps, bars 1 to 4 on rows 4 to 7. Press Pattern (5,8) and tap steps 2, 3 and 4 to clear those trigs, then tap the first step of each beat: (5,4), (9,4), (13,4), then (1,5), (5,5), (9,5), (13,5), and the same four columns on rows 6 and 7. Step 1 is already lit. Press Channel (3,8): sixteen trigs are lit, four in each row.

steps.title: Add the ghost trig in bar 3
steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) and tap step 44, step 12 of bar 3, at (12,6). Press Channel (3,8): a seventeenth trig is lit on row 6, one step before the beat on step 45.

steps.title: Add the ghost trig in bar 4
steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) and tap step 60, step 12 of bar 4, at (12,7). Press Channel (3,8): the same trig is lit on row 7, one step before the beat on step 61. Bars 1 and 2 are unchanged, and bars 3 and 4 each carry one extra trig.

polymeter-song-reset.title: Restart or carry on at a song slot change

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: A new project with playback stopped and Rate /1. Channel 1 plays range 1-4, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, to its own MIDI output. Channel 2 is not set up yet. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

steps.title: Build channel 2 and a two-slot song
steps.caption: Give channel 2 its own MIDI output on the Device page, pattern 1 and the range steps 1-3, then open Masks and set its values: Note 79, Vel 40 and Len ½ on every step, with step 2 locked to Note 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Select channel 1. Press Song (6,8), set the global length fader to 10 steps and copy slot 1 into slot 2 (hold (1,1) and tap (2,1)). Each slot is now ten steps long and both play the same four-against-three pair.

steps.title: Check Reset on song seq change
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Reset on song seq change and turn E3 right to On (the default). The row reads On.

steps.title: Both loops restart at slot 2
steps.caption: Close the menu, tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Play slot 1 and the first four steps of slot 2, then press Stop. Ten steps in, the song moves to slot 2 and both channels start their loops again: channel 1 plays 60 and channel 2 plays 79 on step 11, as the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step" shows.

steps.title: Switch Reset on song seq change Off
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Reset on song seq change and turn E3 left to Off. The row reads Off.

steps.title: Neither loop restarts
steps.caption: Close the menu, tap slot 1 and press Play again, then press Stop after the first four steps of slot 2. This time the loops carry on across the slot change: on step 11 channel 1 plays 64, the third note of its four-note loop, and channel 2 plays 81, the second note of its three-note loop.

course-getting-started.title: 1. Meet Mosaic

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Open channel 1
steps.caption: You start from a new, empty project: transport stopped, nothing set up, channel 1 selected. Tap Channel (3,8), the third button on the bottom row. The screen opens NOTE MASKS for CH01 with eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4) that all read X: no value is set, because a new channel has no pattern, pitch or sound yet. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because channel 1 is the channel you edit, and (3,8) is lit because it is the page you are on.

steps.title: Try the Pattern button
steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), the fifth button on the bottom row. The grid and screen switch to the pattern editor: the title row reads PATTERN TRIG with PAT01 CH01, and every step is dim because pattern 1 has no trigs yet. (1,1) is lit because pattern 1 is the pattern you edit, and (5,8) is lit because you are on the Pattern page.

course-getting-started.starting_state: A new, empty project with the transport stopped: no output, pattern or tempo has been set up yet. Channel 1 is selected.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: A new, empty project with the transport stopped and nothing assigned to a channel. The pattern editor from chapter 1 is on screen. Channel 1 has no output chosen yet and no tempo has been set; the rest of the course uses MIDI port 1, MIDI channel 1 for channel 1.

steps.title: Open Channel tasks
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then turn E1 right three detents. The title row reads CHANNEL TASKS with CH01: a list of the pages of channel 1, each marked OPEN >, with the footer Channel Editor. This list is how you reach every channel page (Masks, Trig params, Output, Clock, Merge modes, Merge Shape, Harmony, Device and History).

steps.title: Open Device
steps.caption: Turn E2 down the list to Device, the eighth task (seven detents below Masks), and press K3. The title row reads DEVICE with CH01. Only the Device row is listed, set to None: the MIDI channel and MIDI port rows appear once you choose a device.

steps.title: Choose CC Device (draft)
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent to choose the first entry after None, CC Device (a generic MIDI device). DEVICE CH01 now lists Device CC Device, MIDI channel CC1, MIDI port OUT 1 and Device locks RESET, and the last line reads Press K3 to confirm: this is only a draft, the channel still has no output and K2 would cancel it.

steps.title: Choose a device and apply it
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply the draft. The Press K3 to confirm line is replaced by OK, and notes from channel 1 now leave on MIDI port 1, MIDI channel 1. With your own gear, choose its device entry and set its port and channel; with no external gear, choose Polyperc 1 for the norns voice.

steps.title: Open Tempo
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), turn E1 right one detent to Song tasks, turn E2 to Tempo & feel and press K3, then turn E2 up to Tempo. GLOBAL FEEL for SONG 01 lists Tempo, Swing type and Swing, and Tempo shows the norns clock tempo; in this recording it already reads 90, the value every timing in the chapters ahead assumes. On your norns it may read something else, such as 120.

steps.title: Set the tempo to 90
steps.caption: Tempo moves one BPM per detent between 30 and 300, with no coarse step. To see it work, turn E3 left or right and watch the number follow, then bring it back to 90 and press K3 to apply. GLOBAL FEEL shows Tempo 90, which makes a beat exactly 2/3 s for every timing in the chapters ahead.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: The project from chapter 2: channel 1 sends to a MIDI instrument on port 1, MIDI channel 1 (its Device page shows CC Device, MIDI channel CC1, MIDI port OUT 1), and the tempo is 90 BPM (GLOBAL FEEL shows Tempo 90). No pattern has trigs yet, nothing is assigned to a channel and playback is stopped.

steps.title: Enter four trigs
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1), then tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Row 4 holds steps 1 to 16, so these are the first four steps. PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows four bright trigs at the left of row 4. Four neighbouring trigs are a deliberately plain rhythm to hear first; chapter 4 spreads them out.

steps.title: Assign pattern 1
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then tap (1,2), the first pattern slot on row 2, to give channel 1 pattern 1. Mosaic opens MERGE MODES for CH01 because assigning a pattern always shows it, and the tooltip reads Pattern 1 added to ch. 1. Patterns reads 01; ignore the other rows for now.

steps.title: Loop four steps
steps.caption: Row 4 of the channel page is the range row: hold (1,4), tap (4,4) and release (1,4) to loop only steps 1 to 4. Steps 1 to 4 stay bright, the rest go dark, and the tooltip reads Channel 1 length changed.

steps.title: Open Masks
steps.caption: Turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 lists eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4), all X: no mask is set, so the channel has no pitch, velocity or length yet. With no step held, E2 chooses a cell and E3 sets that cell for every step of the channel.

steps.title: Give the trigs a pitch, level and length
steps.caption: Select Note with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads C3 (it starts at X, so about 60 detents), select Vel and turn E3 right to 80 (about 80 detents), then select Len and turn E3 right to 1/2 (8 detents). NOTE MASKS CH01 now lists Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2, the defaults for every step.

steps.title: Play and stop
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen for two repeats of the four-step loop, then tap Play again. While it plays the screen stays on NOTE MASKS, the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows note 60 (C3) at velocity 80 about every 167 ms (1/6 s): four notes per repeat, so you hear a fast stutter rather than a tune. Stop leaves no note sounding. This confirms the whole chain (pattern, channel, masks, output) before you shape the rhythm.

course-build-a-phrase.title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1 to 4 and is assigned to channel 1, which loops steps 1 to 4. Channel 1's Masks are Note C3 (60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, and the tempo is 90 BPM. Playback is stopped.

steps.title: Loop all 16 steps
steps.caption: Hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4): the range is now 16 steps, one bar. On row 4, steps 5 to 16 now glow dimly because they are inside the loop (they were dark at range 4), and the trigs are still on steps 1 to 4. Then open the Clock page for the next step: turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3.

steps.title: Check the rate
steps.caption: Select Rate (the top row of the CLOCK page; turn E2 up if it is not highlighted) and press K3. CLOCK CH01 shows Rate /1, the default sixteenth-note rate: each step lasts 1/6 s at 90 BPM and the 16 steps last 2.7 s. Nothing changes here; this confirms the rate that every timing in the course relies on.

steps.title: Move the trigs onto the beats
steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), tap (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4) to remove those trigs, then tap (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4) to add trigs. Keep (1,4). PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: four steps apart is one beat at 90 BPM.

steps.title: Open Masks for the next chapter
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 as before, and row 4 of the grid shows the four trigs one beat apart inside the 16-step range. Masks stays open so chapter 5 starts on the page it needs.

steps.title: Hear the longer phrase
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two 16-step passes run (about 5.3 s), then tap Play to stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4, one beat at a time over the four trigs. The MIDI strip shows note 60 (C3) at velocity 80 once per beat, about 667 ms (2/3 s) apart: the same note as chapter 3, spread over a bar instead of 167 ms apart. Stop leaves no note sounding.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1, trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13, over steps 1 to 16 at Rate /1 and 90 BPM. Its channel masks are Note C3 (60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, and the NOTE MASKS page is open; no step has a mask yet. Playback is stopped.

steps.title: Find the channel default
steps.caption: With no step held, turn E2 to Note. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3 in the highlighted cell. With no step number in the title row, C3 is the default for every step of the channel; no step has a mask of its own yet.

steps.title: Select the last beat
steps.caption: Hold (13,4), the fourth trig, and keep holding it. The title row changes to CH01 ST13: from now the screen edits step 13 only, and its Note still reads C3 because step 13 has no exception yet.

steps.title: Raise the last note
steps.caption: While you hold (13,4), turn E3 right two detents. NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3: a pitch for step 13 only, two semitones above the default.

steps.title: Release the step
steps.caption: Release (13,4). The title row returns to CH01 and Note shows the channel default C3 again. Step 13 still keeps D3: hold (13,4) again to see it, or listen in the next step.

steps.title: Hold the step again
steps.caption: Hold (13,4) again. The title row returns to CH01 ST13 and Note reads D3: step 13 kept its own note when you let go, and holding it is how you see it. Release (13,4) before the next step.

steps.title: Hear the new ending
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen to two passes, then tap Play to stop. The screen is back on the channel defaults, the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows C, C, C, D: steps 1, 5 and 9 sound note 60 and step 13 sounds note 62, all at velocity 80, one beat apart.

steps.title: Make the ending softer
steps.caption: Select Vel with E2, hold (13,4) and turn E3 left 30 detents. While you hold it, NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Vel 50 and Note D3: both belong to step 13 alone. Keep holding for this frame, then release (13,4).

steps.title: Hear the softer ending
steps.caption: After you release (13,4) the screen shows the channel default Vel 80 again. Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows notes 60, 60, 60 at velocity 80 and note 62 at velocity 50.

steps.title: Set the channel default to G3
steps.caption: With no step held, select Note with E2 and turn E3 right seven detents to G3 (MIDI 67, seven semitones above C). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note G3: the default for the whole channel changed.

steps.title: Check step 13 kept its own note
steps.caption: Hold (13,4) again. NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 still shows Note D3 and Vel 50: step 13 keeps its own values whatever the channel default says. Release (13,4).

steps.title: Hear the new default
steps.caption: Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows 67, 67, 67 on steps 1, 5 and 9 and 62 at velocity 50 on step 13: you hear G, G, G, D because step 13 keeps its own note.

steps.title: Restore the default
steps.caption: Turn E3 left seven detents to return the default Note to C3 (MIDI 60). Play two passes and stop. The MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62 again, and step 13 is still at velocity 50.

steps.title: Hold step 13 before clearing
steps.caption: Hold (13,4) and keep holding it. NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3 and Vel 50, the exceptions you built for this step.

steps.title: Clear it with K2
steps.caption: While you still hold (13,4), press K2. The tooltip reads Masks for step 13 cleared and the screen shows Note C3 and Vel 80, the channel defaults: K2 on a held step removes every mask on that step and leaves the channel defaults alone. Release (13,4).

steps.title: Hear the cleared step
steps.caption: Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows 60 at velocity 80 on all four steps.

steps.title: Rebuild: raise step 13 to D3
steps.caption: Rebuild the ending with the two edits you already know. Select Note, hold (13,4) and turn E3 right two detents: NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3 while you hold.

steps.title: Rebuild: step 13 velocity 50
steps.caption: Release, select Vel, hold (13,4) and turn E3 left 30 detents: NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3 and Vel 50 together. Release (13,4).

steps.title: Hear the rebuilt ending
steps.caption: Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60 at velocity 80 and 62 at velocity 50.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
