steps.caption: Channel 1 plays C, C, C, D over 16 steps at 90 BPM: step 13 has Note D3 (62) and Vel 50, the other trigs use C3 at 80. Channel 2, pattern 2 and a second MIDI output are still to be set up.

steps.title: Enter two bass trigs
steps.caption: Pattern 2 starts empty. Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap (1,4) and (9,4) for two trigs. PATTERN TRIG PAT02 CH01 shows the two trigs as bright squares on steps 1 and 9, and the tooltip reads Pattern 2 selected.

steps.title: Give them notes
steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) again to open the note view, then tap (1,7) for degree 0 on step 1 and (9,3) for degree 4 on step 9. PATTERN NOTE PAT02 shows the tooltip Step 9 note set to 4. Only those two note taps are yours: the bright band along row 7 is the note view's degree 0 baseline, and the extra pad at (13,6) is not one of your notes and does not play. It is the note view also showing what channel 1 last played on step 13, D3 (degree 1); pattern 2 has no trig there.

steps.title: Open channel 2's Device page
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 until Device is highlighted and press K3, as in chapter 2. DEVICE CH02 opens with its own Device row: channel 2 needs its own output, different from channel 1's.

steps.title: Apply the second output
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent to CC Device, turn E2 down to MIDI channel and E3 one detent to CC2, turn E2 down to MIDI port and E3 one detent to OUT 2, then press K3 to apply. DEVICE CH02 lists Device CC Device, MIDI channel CC2 and MIDI port OUT 2, and the last line reads OK.

steps.title: Assign pattern 2
steps.caption: Tap (2,2) to give channel 2 pattern 2. MERGE MODES for CH02 shows Patterns 02 and the tooltip reads Pattern 2 added to ch. 2.

steps.title: Loop 16 steps
steps.caption: Set the range, a gesture and not a trig: hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4), so channel 2 loops the same 16 steps as channel 1. The tooltip reads Channel 2 length changed.

steps.title: Drop it an octave
steps.caption: Tap (9,8) for octave -1. The screen reads NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and the tooltip shows Ch. 2 octave: -1; (2,2) and (9,8) are lit.

steps.title: Hear the two parts
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two passes run, then tap Play to stop. While it plays the screen stays on NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and the Play pad (1,8) is lit. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 on port 1: notes 60, 60, 60 at velocity 80 and 62 at velocity 50, a beat apart. Channel 2 is on port 2: note 48 on step 1 and note 55 on step 9, both at velocity 100. That is the phrase above a low C and G.

steps.title: Add pattern 2 to channel 1 (Skip)
steps.caption: Optional detour. Select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot (2,2) to add pattern 2 next to pattern 1: MERGE MODES shows Patterns 01 02 and Strategy SKIP, the default. Play two passes and stop. Skip plays a step only when exactly one assigned pattern has a trig there, so with both patterns trigging steps 1 and 9, only steps 5 and 13 stay bright on row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding only 60 and 62 at velocity 50; the bass (48, 55) is unchanged.

steps.title: Press the merge button once
steps.caption: Tap (14,8) once. MERGE MODES shows Strategy ONLY with the tooltip ONLY APPLIED, and the (14,8) button changes brightness. The button steps through Skip, Only, All and further strategies. Only plays a step only when more than one assigned pattern has a trig there: on row 4 just steps 1 and 9 stay bright.

steps.title: Hear Only
steps.caption: Play two passes and stop, with Strategy still ONLY. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding only note 60 at velocity 80, on steps 1 and 9, two beats apart; the bass (48, 55) is unchanged. These are exactly the steps Skip silenced.

steps.title: Merge mode All
steps.caption: Tap (14,8) once more: Strategy reads ALL and all four trigs on row 4 light again. Play two passes and stop. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 60, 60, 60, 62 (velocity 80, 80, 80, 50): channel 1's Note and Vel masks supply the pitch and velocity, whichever pattern's trig fires.

steps.title: Remove pattern 2 again
steps.caption: Tap (2,2) to remove pattern 2 from channel 1, then play two passes and stop. MERGE MODES now shows Patterns 01. Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, 60, 60, 60, 62, and channel 2 keeps 48 and 55. Strategy stays on ALL, which makes no difference with one pattern. Another tap of (14,8) would move on to a different strategy this course does not use, so leave it.

course-harmony-design.title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, C, C, C, D, from channel and step masks: Note C3 (60), Vel 80, and on step 13 Note D3 (62) at Vel 50; NOTE MASKS CH01 is open. Channel 2 plays pattern 2 (degrees 0 and 4, octave -1) as MIDI 48 and 55. The merge Strategy is still All, which changes nothing with one pattern. Scale slot 1 is C major and the tempo is 90 BPM.

steps.title: Let the pattern notes through
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Note and turn E3 left until it reads X (no mask). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X: the channel no longer decides the pitch, the pattern notes will.

steps.title: Restore the quiet ending
steps.caption: Hold (13,4) and press K2: the tooltip reads Masks for step 13 cleared, and K2 removes every mask on the step, so its Note 62 and Vel 50 both go. Then select Vel, turn E3 left 30 detents to 50 while still holding: NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note X and Vel 50, the quiet ending back on step 13 alone. Release (13,4).

steps.title: Back to the channel defaults
steps.caption: Release (13,4). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X and Vel 80 (the channel defaults); step 13's own Vel 50 only shows while you hold it.

steps.title: Write the melody as degrees
steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1), tap Pattern (5,8) again for the note view and tap (1,7), (5,7), (9,7) and (13,6): degree 0 on steps 1, 5 and 9, and degree 1, one row up and the next note of the scale, on step 13. PATTERN NOTE PAT01 CH01 shows the tooltip Step 13 note set to 1.

steps.title: Play it from the pattern
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), play two passes and stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 60, 60, 60, 62 from the pattern's own notes, step 13 at velocity 50, and channel 2 sounding 48 and 55.

steps.title: Prepare a second scale
steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) to open the scale page, tap scale slot 2 at (2,3), then play two passes and stop. While it plays the screen shows SCALE SLOT 02 with Root C and Scale Major. Slot 2 holds C major like slot 1, so nothing changes: the MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62 on channel 1 and 48 and 55 on channel 2. Ignore the Degree and Transpose rows on this page; they stay at I and 0.

steps.title: Draft D as the root
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Root and turn E3 right two detents to D. SCALE SLOT 02 shows Root D, Scale Major and the line Press K3 to confirm. The change is only a draft until K3, so playback would still use C major.

steps.title: Check the Scale row
steps.caption: Turn E2 down to Scale. SCALE SLOT 02 shows Scale Major beside the draft Root D, and Press K3 to confirm is still on screen: nothing is applied yet.

steps.title: Apply D major
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply: the Press K3 to confirm line disappears. Play two passes and stop. While it plays SCALE SLOT 02 shows Root D and the Play pad (1,8) is lit. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 62, 62, 62, 64 (the last at velocity 50) and channel 2 sounding 50 and 57: the same rhythm in D major.

steps.title: Return to C major
steps.caption: Tap scale slot 1 at (1,3), press K3 to apply, then play two passes and stop. SCALE SLOT 01 shows Root C. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 back on 60, 60, 60, 62 and channel 2 on 48 and 55.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: The project at the end of chapter 7: channel 1 plays degrees 0, 0, 0, 1 from pattern 1 with step 13 at velocity 50, channel 2 plays its bass, and C major is applied. Step 15 has no trig. Playback is stopped.

steps.title: Add the late trig
steps.caption: Choose pattern 1, tap (15,4) on Pattern Trig to add a trig on step 15, press Pattern (5,8) once to open the note view and tap (15,7) for degree 0. PATTERN NOTE PAT01 CH01 shows the tooltip Step 15 note set to 0 and a trig stripe on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15.

steps.title: Open Masks
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X (the pattern notes decide pitch), Vel 80 and Len 1/2: the channel defaults the new trig will use until you give step 15 its own velocity.

steps.title: Set step 15 to velocity 35
steps.caption: Select Vel with E2, hold (15,4) and turn E3 left 45 detents until Vel reads 35. While you hold the step, NOTE MASKS CH01 ST15 shows Vel 35, that step's own value. Keep holding for this frame, then release (15,4).

steps.title: Hear the quiet pickup
steps.caption: After you release, the screen shows the channel default Vel 80 again. Play two passes and stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows the phrase (60 at velocity 80, then 62 at 50) and a quiet 60 at velocity 35 on step 15, just before the bar restarts.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Slot 1 holds the whole project, including the pickup on step 15 at velocity 35. Global length is the default 64, Repeats is 1 and Song mode is On; slots 2 and 3 are empty. Playback is stopped.

steps.title: Copy the complete section
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1), release slot 1 and tap (2,1) again to select slot 2. Holding slot 1 while you tap slot 2 copies the whole section (patterns, channel settings, masks and mutes). The screen reads SLOT SETUP, SONG 02, the tooltip says Song sequence 2 selected, and (2,1) is the bright slot button. The next two steps check the copy: slot 2 stays audible when slot 1 is muted.

steps.title: Mute channel 1 in slot 1
steps.caption: Select slot 1 at (1,1), tap Channel (3,8), then hold K1, tap (1,1) and release K1. K1 is the shift key from chapter 1: K1 plus a channel button mutes that channel in this slot only. The title reads CH01 MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 muted: slot 1 will play the bass alone.

steps.title: Check slot 2 stays full
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 2 at (2,1) and tap Channel (3,8). The title reads CH01 S02 with no MUTE: channel 1 is audible in slot 2, so slot 2 keeps the full phrase.

steps.title: Set slot 1 to one bar
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 1 at (1,1), tap (3,7) on the length fader, then tap (8,7) three times. The fader is row 7, columns 1 to 8: (3,7) jumps to 13 steps and each tap of (8,7) adds one, so 13 + 3 = 16. SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 01 shows Global length 16; Song mode reads AUTO there, which means Song mode is on and advancing.

steps.title: Optional: check Repeats for slot 1
steps.caption: Optional check. Open Slot setup from Song tasks (E1 right one detent, E2 to Slot setup, K3), select Repeats, turn E3 left until it reads 1 and press K3. Repeats already starts at 1: SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 shows Repeats 1.

steps.title: Set slot 2 to one bar
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 2 at (2,1), tap (3,7), then tap (8,7) three times: 13 + 3 = 16 again. SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 02 shows Global length 16.

steps.title: Optional: check Repeats for slot 2
steps.caption: Optional check. Open Slot setup, select Repeats, turn E3 left until it reads 1 and press K3. SLOT SETUP, SONG 02 shows Repeats 1, the default.

steps.title: Optional: check Song mode
steps.caption: Optional check. In Slot setup select Song mode, turn E3 right to On and press K3. SLOT SETUP, SONG 02 shows Song mode On, the default: the song moves from slot 1 to slot 2 and wraps to slot 1 because slot 3 is empty.

steps.title: Hear slot 1
steps.caption: Select slot 1, tap Play (1,8) and listen to slot 1 first. SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 stays on screen with Song mode On, the slot button (1,1) is bright, and the MIDI strip shows only the bass (port 2: note 48, then 55, velocity 100) because channel 1 is muted in this slot.

steps.title: Hear slot 2 join
steps.caption: Keep listening for the second section (about 2.7 s later) and then tap Play to stop; four 16-step sections run in all (about 10.7 s). The screen follows the song to SLOT SETUP, SONG 02 and the bright slot button moves to (2,1). The MIDI strip now shows the phrase on port 1 (60, 60, 60 at velocity 80, 62 at 50 and the pickup 60 at 35) joining the bass, only in the sections that play slot 2.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Slot 1 has channel 1 muted and slot 2 has both channels audible, each 16 steps with Repeats 1 and Song mode On. The project has not been saved under a name yet and playback is stopped.

steps.title: Open Save project
steps.caption: Tap K1 briefly for the norns menu, turn E1 to PARAMS and press K3, open MOSAIC and turn E2 to < Save project. The norns menu lists Pattern project management with Save project selected.

steps.title: Save the arrangement
steps.caption: Press K3 on < Save project. The norns text entry screen opens with the suggested name new: press K3 on DEL to delete it, then turn E2 to each character of Four notes and press K3 to enter it, and confirm. Saving writes Four notes.ptn and Four notes.pset. Tap K1 to return to Mosaic, which still shows SLOT SETUP, SONG 01; the text entry itself is on the norns menu, not on this frame.

steps.title: Make an unsaved change
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then hold K1, tap (1,1) and release K1. The title reads CH01 with no MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 unmuted: slot 1 now plays the phrase. This change is not saved.

steps.title: Open Load project
steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn E2 to > Load project. The norns menu shows Load project selected; K2 would cancel the dialog.

steps.title: Reload the saved version
steps.caption: Press K3 on > Load project, turn E2 to Four notes in the file list and press K3, then tap K1 to return to Mosaic and tap Channel (3,8). The title reads CH01 MUTE again: the unsaved change is gone and slot 1 is bass alone.

steps.title: Replay slot 1
steps.caption: Select slot 1, tap Play (1,8) and listen. SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 is on screen and the bass alone (48, 55) sounds, as before the save.

steps.title: Replay slot 2
steps.caption: Keep listening: the screen follows the song to SONG 02 and the phrase and pickup join the bass, as in chapter 9. Let four 16-step sections run, then tap Play to stop. The MIDI strip lists the same notes as the arrangement in chapter 9.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped. Channel 1's output is a test device whose parameter Control 1 sends MIDI CC 1 from 0 to 127 and has an Off position shown as X. No value is stored for Control 1 yet. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

steps.title: Select Control 1
steps.caption: Choose the test device on channel 1's Device screen. Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC, open channel 1's device parameters and turn E2 to Control 1. It reads X: Off, so no CC is sent.

steps.title: Turn up from X to 0
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent right from X. Control 1 reads 0 and sends MIDI CC 1 with value 0.

steps.title: One more detent
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent right. Control 1 reads 1 and sends MIDI CC 1 with value 1. Each detent moves the value by one.

steps.title: Turn up to the middle
steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right until Control 1 reads 64, passing 63. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 shows 63 and then 64.

steps.title: Turn up to just below the top
steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right until Control 1 reads 126, one below the highest value.

steps.title: Turn up to the top and stop
steps.caption: Turn E3 right once more: Control 1 reads 127, the highest value, and sends MIDI CC 1 with 127. One more turn leaves it at 127.

steps.title: Turn down to X
steps.caption: Turn E3 left: the value falls to 64, then 1, then to X, which means Off: no CC is sent. One more turn down stays at X. The last frame shows Control 1 back at X.

device-stored-value-and-step-lock.title: Keep a stored value while locking a step

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped. The test device has a CC 1 control; no value is stored for it yet. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.

steps.title: Store CC 1 at 63
steps.caption: Choose the test device on channel 1's Device screen. Press K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC > channel 1's device parameters, select CC 1 and turn E3 right until it reads 63. This is the stored value: the level CC 1 holds whenever no step overrides it.

steps.title: Assign CC 1 to a Trig params slot
steps.caption: Close the menu. On Channel tasks > Trig params assign CC 1 to a slot with E3 and K3. Its slot is the one you will lock per step.

steps.title: Lock step 1 to 99
steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm the assignment and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 right 36 detents from 63 to 99. Slot 1 shows 99 with an L in its corner while the step is held. The stored value, 63, is not changed. Release the step.

steps.title: Play two loops
steps.caption: Press Play, let two loops sound and press Play again to stop. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 = 99 comes just before step 1's note, and CC 1 = 63, the stored value, before the other steps; at the very first note the stored 63 is sent first and then the lock 99.

steps.title: The stored value is unchanged
steps.caption: Press K1 and reopen the device parameters: CC 1 still reads 63, because a lock never changes the stored value.

range-reject-and-recover.title: Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. The channel range is steps 1 to 4, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.

steps.title: Set steps 2 to 4
steps.caption: Hold step 2 (2,4), tap and release step 4 (4,4), then release step 2. The range is now steps 2 to 4 and those steps brighten. Tap Play (1,8) and listen: the channel loops D, E, F (62, 64, 65). Tap Play again to stop.

steps.title: Refuse an end before the start
steps.caption: Hold step 4 (4,4), tap step 2 (2,4), then release step 2 and step 4. The end would come before the start, so Mosaic refuses it: the footer reads End must follow start and the grid still shows steps 2 to 4.

steps.title: Refuse a start released first
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and Stop to check: it still loops D, E, F, because the refused gesture changed nothing. Then press step 2 (2,4), press step 4 (4,4) and release step 2 before step 4. The order of release matters: the footer reads End must follow start again and steps 2 to 4 stay bright. To set a range, release the later step first.

steps.title: Still D, E, F
steps.caption: Tap Play and listen: D, E, F (62, 64, 65) loop with the same timing, because neither refused gesture altered the range. Tap Play to stop.

steps.title: Choose a valid range
steps.caption: Hold step 3 (3,4), tap and release step 4 (4,4), then release step 3. Steps 3 and 4 are bright and steps 1, 2 and 5 are dark: a correctly ordered gesture is accepted again.

steps.title: Hear the new range
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen: E and F (64, 65) loop with the same step timing and gate lengths. Tap Play again to stop.

mute-live-resume.title: Mute a channel and bring a running phrase back

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. No channel is muted, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.

steps.title: Select channel 1 without muting
steps.caption: Press channel button (1,1) and let go after about half a second, well before one second is up. A short press only selects the channel, so the button stays bright and nothing is muted.

steps.title: Hear channel one
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen: channel 1 plays C, D, E, F (60, 62, 64, 65), and the strip below lists the four notes. Tap Play again to stop.

steps.title: Mute with a long press
steps.caption: Hold (1,1) for a full second, then let go. The button dims to show channel 1 is muted; a muted channel still counts as selected.

steps.title: Listen to the muted channel
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen for about a second and a half: the dimmed channel sends no notes, and the strip below stays empty. Playback keeps running, so the other channels would carry on.

steps.title: Unmute with K1
steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens again, so channel 1 is unmuted.

steps.title: Hear it again
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8): with channel 1 unmuted, C, D, E, F (60, 62, 64, 65) sound again. Tap Play to stop.

steps.title: Mute while it plays
steps.caption: Tap Play. While the phrase sounds, hold (1,1) for a full second: the button dims and the notes stop. The clock keeps running, but no new notes sound for the next second and a half.

steps.title: Bring channel one back
steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens and the phrase comes back in time with the running pattern, picking up wherever the loop has reached rather than starting over.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. Nothing is assigned to Trig params yet, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.

steps.title: Give Chord Note Strum a slot
steps.caption: Open Trig params (E1 to the channel's Trig params page), press K2 to enter the slot list, turn E3 until the parameter reads Chord Note Strum, press K3 to assign it to the first slot, then press K2 to leave the list. The slot shows as Strm on the screen: it is the strum slot.

steps.title: A new slot starts at X
steps.caption: Press K3 to select the Strm slot. It reads X, which means no strum: the notes of a chord sound together. Every strum division is chosen with E3 from here.

steps.title: First supported division
steps.caption: Turn E3 left a few detents: nothing happens, because X is the lowest value. Then turn E3 one detent right. The slot reads 1/24, one twenty-fourth of a channel step between chord notes, the smallest strum division.

steps.title: Climb to the upper bound
steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right, about ninety detents, through the supported divisions until the slot reads 128 channel steps, then turn a few detents further: it stays at 128 and extra turns do not go higher.

steps.title: One step back down
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent left. The slot reads 120, the next supported division below 128; turning back left continues down towards 1/24 and X.

parameter-slot-endpoints.title: Use the first and last Trig params slots

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. No Trig params slot is assigned yet, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Assign CC 1 to slot 1
steps.caption: Open Trig params, press K2 to enter the slot list and turn E3 to CC 1, press K3, then K2. Slot 1 now holds CC 1.

steps.title: Assign CC 2 to slot 2
steps.caption: Turn E2 one slot right, press K2, turn E3 to CC 2 and press K3, then K2. Slot 2 now holds CC 2 and slot 1 still holds CC 1.

steps.title: Carry on to slot 5
steps.caption: Repeat for slots 3, 4 and 5 (E2 to the next slot, K2, E3 to the next controller, K3, K2). Slot 5 now holds CC 5.

steps.title: Fill slots 6 to 10
steps.caption: Repeat for CC 6 up to CC 10 on slot 10. All ten slots are now assigned: the list holds CC 1 to CC 10, the most a channel can hold.

steps.title: The first and last slots hold their ends
steps.caption: Select slot 10 and keep turning E2 right: it stops at slot 10. Hold step 1 (1,4) and turn E3 to set the value to 0. Turn E2 left well past slot 1: it stops at slot 1. Hold step 2 (2,4) and set the value to 1. Tap Play (1,8). Before its note, step 1 sends CC 10 and step 2 sends CC 1: look for the two controller changes in the strip below. Tap Play again to stop.

transpose-next-onset.title: Transpose the next note without cutting the current one

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Press +1 while it plays
steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8) to open the Scale Editor, then tap Play (1,8). One step lasts about a sixth of a second at 90 BPM, so the four-note phrase repeats about every two thirds of a second; exact timing does not matter. While it loops, press (16,8) on the transposition fader once. The screen shows Scale overview with Transpose +1: the note sounding at that moment keeps its pitch and length, and the next notes play a semitone higher, MIDI 61, 63, 65 and 66, as the MIDI strip lists.

steps.title: Press -12 a few notes later
steps.caption: After a few more notes press (9,8) to set -12. Transpose reads -12: again the sounding note is untouched and the next notes drop an octave below the written pitches, 48, 50, 52 and 53.

steps.title: Stop
steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Transpose still reads -12, and in the strip every note-on has its own matching note-off.

steps.title: The whole run
steps.caption: Both edits changed only the next onset: the notes before the first edit are 60, 62, 64, 65, then 61, 63, 65, 66, then 48, 50, 52, 53, and each held note finished at its own pitch and length.

keyboard-white-key-options.title: Let a keyboard follow the scale

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on the test device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4. The scale is C major, a MIDI keyboard is connected on port 1 and Map scale to white keys is off, its default. The sequencer is stopped, so the keyboard plays the channel's output directly. The norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Raw notes by default
steps.caption: Play the white keys C, D, E, F, G, A, B, then the black keys between them. With Map scale to white keys off every key sends its own pitch: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71 for the white keys, with 61, 63, 66, 68, 70 for the black keys. The strip below lists the notes in the order you played them.

steps.title: Turn the mapping on
steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC, open the MIDI controller options and turn Map scale to white keys On. The row now reads On.

steps.title: White keys follow the scale
steps.caption: Leave PARAMS and play the white keys again. They now follow the selected scale with its root on C: in C major C D E F G A B C sound as 60 62 64 65 67 69 71 72, the same pitches as before. What changes is the black keys: each one repeats the white key above it, so C# sounds 62 instead of 61.

steps.title: Change the scale, change the keys
steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8), turn E3 two detents to change the scale from Major to natural minor and press K3, then tap Channel (3,8). Play the white keys: C D Eb F G Ab Bb C sound as 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72. Black keys still repeat the white key above them: C# plays 62 and D# plays 63. Read the strip below for the thirteen keys C to C: 60 62 62 63 63 65 67 67 68 68 70 70 72, the eight white keys being 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72.

steps.title: Set degree II, rotation 2 and +2
steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8). Turn E2 once and E3 to set the scale degree to II, press K3, turn E2 three detents and E3 to set rotation 2, press K3, then raise the transposition fader (the minimum at (9,8), then (16,8) fourteen times) to +2. Press Channel (3,8) and play the white keys C to C. All three Honour options are still Off, so the keys follow plain natural minor: look in the strip for 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72, with each black key repeating the white key above it.

steps.title: Honour scale degree
steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC > MIDI controller options and turn Honour scale degree On, leave PARAMS and play the keys again. The seven white keys now start on degree II, so the whole run shifts: read the new notes in the strip below.

steps.title: Add rotation
steps.caption: Turn Honour scale rotations On as well and play the keys again. Rotation 2 drops the last two of the seven positions by an octave: compare the strip with the previous step.

steps.title: Add transposition
steps.caption: Turn Honour scale transpose On too and play the keys again. Everything now sounds two semitones higher than in the previous step.

steps.title: Turn mapping off
steps.caption: Turn Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations Off and play, then Honour scale transpose Off, and finally turn Map scale to white keys Off in PARAMS > MOSAIC. Press Channel (3,8) and play C to C: every key plays its own pitch once more, 60 to 72, whatever scale is selected.

song-mode-groups-and-selection.title: Loop a song group or hold one slot

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: A fresh session with Song mode On, its default. Channel 1 plays its default phrase through the test device and the norns shows the Device page; nothing is playing. You build the song in the next step: a two-note motif (MIDI 60, 62) copied into slots 1, 2, 4 and 5, with slots 3 and 6 left empty.

steps.title: Set the global length to 2
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once. The Playback screen reads Global length 2, so every slot plays a two-note motif, 60 and 62.

steps.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2 and raise it an octave
steps.caption: Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, then tap slot 2. Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 will sound 72 and 74.

steps.title: Add slots 4 and 5
steps.caption: Repeat for slot 4, leaving slot 3 empty: copy slot 1 into slot 4 and give it octave +2 at (12,8). Then copy slot 1 into slot 5 and give it octave -1 at (9,8). Slots 3 and 6 stay empty, so there are two groups: slots 1 and 2, and slots 4 and 5.

steps.title: Loop the first group
steps.caption: Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 sounds 60, 62, then slot 2 sounds 72, 74. Slot 3 is empty, so the group ends and playback returns to slot 1: 60, 62, 72, 74, 60, 62, 72, 74. Press Stop.

steps.title: A second group
steps.caption: Tap slot 4 at (4,1) and press Play. Slot 4 sounds 84, 86 and slot 5 sounds 48, 50. Slot 6 is empty, so this second group repeats on its own: 84, 86, 48, 50, 84, 86, 48, 50. Press Stop.

steps.title: Select the next slot while playing
steps.caption: Tap slot 4 at (4,1) and press Play: slot 4 sounds 84, 86. While it plays, press slot 2 at (2,1). The press is queued, not instant. Slot 4 finishes, then slot 2 plays (72, 74) and its group carries on with slot 1 (60, 62) and slot 2 (72, 74). Press Stop; the screen shows where playback ended.

steps.title: Two presses before the boundary
steps.caption: Tap slot 1 and press Play. After the first note, press slot 4 and then slot 5 before slot 1 ends. Slot 1 finishes (60, 62), then the later press wins: slot 5 plays (48, 50), and its group continues with slot 4 (84, 86) and slot 5 again. Press Stop.

steps.title: Turn Song mode off
steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns menu, choose PARAMS > MOSAIC, find Song mode and turn E3 to Off. The row reads Off.

steps.title: Song mode off holds the slot
steps.caption: Press K2 to leave the menu, select slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play. Slot 1 repeats, 60, 62, 60, 62, and does not advance to slot 2. Slot setup shows Song mode Off. Press Stop.

steps.title: Manual selection still works
steps.caption: With Song mode Off, press Play on slot 1, then tap slot 2 at (2,1) while it plays. The press is still queued: slot 1 finishes (60, 62), then slot 2 repeats (72, 74, 72, 74) and keeps repeating. Song Playback reads Song mode MANUAL and Next HOLD.

steps.title: Song mode back on
steps.caption: Turn Song mode On again the same way (PARAMS > MOSAIC), select slot 2 and press Play. Progression resumes inside the group: slot 2 (72, 74), slot 1 (60, 62), slot 2, slot 1.

merge-shape-owns-trigs.title: Foundation and All: who decides the trigs

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the test device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Both patterns are assigned, Add amount is 100 and Add accent is 70. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

steps.title: Open Merge modes
steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Merge modes and press K3. Strategy reads FOUNDATION: Foundation, not the saved trig merge, is choosing this channel's trigs.

steps.title: Foundation decides the trigs
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Active. Strategy and Active both read FOUNDATION and Pending reads NONE. The Strategy key (14,8) glows at its brightest, the sign that Foundation is in charge: the four anchors on steps 1 to 4 plus additions on steps 5 and 7.

steps.title: Hear Foundation
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. You hear C D E F (60, 62, 64, 65) followed by the additions, a C on steps 5 and 7. Look at the strip below: the additions are quieter, velocity 70, because Add accent 70 scales pattern 2's velocity of 100.

steps.title: Switch the Strategy to All
steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to ALL. Strategy and Active read ALL and the Strategy key (14,8) dims: the saved trig merge is deciding again, with every trig of both patterns.

steps.title: Hear All
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. The same notes sound, but the additions on steps 5 and 7 now keep pattern 2's own velocity, 100, so they are louder than Foundation's 70 in the strip below.

steps.title: Return to Skip
steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to SKIP. The footer reads SKIP APPLIED, Strategy and Active read SKIP and the Strategy key (14,8) dims further. Skip, Only and All hand the trigs back to the saved legacy merge; Foundation's protection and accent no longer apply.

merge-shape-skip-shared-step.title: Skip and All on a step both patterns trig

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the test device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100) has trigs on steps 3 and 7, so step 3 is a step both patterns trig. Both patterns are assigned. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 4 and 7.

steps.title: Open Merge modes
steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Merge modes and press K3. Strategy reads FOUNDATION: Foundation, not the saved trig merge, is choosing this channel's trigs.

steps.title: Hand the trigs back to Skip
steps.caption: Turn E3 left to SKIP. The footer reads SKIP APPLIED and the Strategy key (14,8) dims. Skip applies a trig only if it appears in exactly one selected pattern, so step 3, where both patterns trig, will not sound.

steps.title: Hear Skip
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. The strip below lists C D F (60, 62, 65) from pattern 1 on steps 1, 2 and 4, then a C at velocity 100 on step 7, which only pattern 2 trigs. Step 3 is silent: there is no E and no merged note.

steps.title: Switch the Strategy to All
steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to ALL. Strategy and Active read ALL. All applies a trig if it appears in any selected pattern, so step 3 now sounds.

steps.title: Hear All
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. Step 3 now sounds, merged from both patterns: the Average note merge puts the E (degree III) and the C (degree I) on degree II, a D (62), and the Average velocity merge turns 107 and 100 into 104. Look for D at velocity 104 between 62 and 65 in the strip below; step 7 is still a C at velocity 100.

harmony-range-failure-and-fallback.title: See a failed voicing and choose a fallback

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on MIDI channel 1: C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 at 90 BPM, rate /1. Harmony is Off with its default registers and Failure fallback SILENCE. Playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page. This scene shows what happens when a register leaves no room for a note, as it can after you shift a voice into an unusual range.

steps.title: Open the Bass register
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony. Its list holds Mode, Register, Tone Map, Result and the Entry / Failure row used later. Turn E3 to set Mode to PATTERN, select Register with E2 and press K3.

steps.title: Raise Bass Low to 50
steps.caption: On the Bass rows turn E2 to Low and E3 to set it to 50. The Low row reads 50.

steps.title: Lower Bass High to 50
steps.caption: Turn E2 to High and E3 to set it to 50. The High row reads 50, so the register is now the single note 50.

steps.title: Centre the Bass register on 50
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Centre and E3 to set it to 50. MIDI 50 is a D, so this register holds no C at all. The Centre row reads 50.

steps.title: Send the written C to Bass
steps.caption: Press K3, then E1 back to the Harmony list, select Tone Map with E2 and press K3. Turn E3 so Tone 0, the written C, goes to Bass, and press K3.

steps.title: Hear the silent step
steps.caption: Tap Play for two loops, then Stop. Step 1 is silent while D, E and F sound (MIDI 62, 64, 65 in the strip below), because Bass has no C to play.

steps.title: Open Result
steps.caption: Press E1 to go back to the Harmony list, select Result with E2 and press K3.

steps.title: Read the failure
steps.caption: Read Result for step 1. Status reads NO VOICING RANGE and CH1 reads NO EVENT, because nothing was sent; a Failure details row appears and K3 opens it.

steps.title: Find Entry / Failure
steps.caption: Optional check first: turn E3 to step 5; Status and CH1 read NO EVENT there because the loop has no trig on step 5, which differs from step 1, where an event existed but could not be voiced. Turn Step back to 1, press K2 to return to the list, select Entry and press K3. The Entry / Failure page lists Failure fallback.

steps.title: Choose Legacy
steps.caption: Select Failure fallback and turn E3 once right: it reads LEGACY. Press K3 to apply.

steps.title: Hear the fallback
steps.caption: Tap Play for two loops, then Stop. C D E F return (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65): step 1 now plays through its original C instead of falling silent.

steps.title: Confirm Legacy in Result
steps.caption: Reopen Result: step 1 now reads Status LEGACY RANGE and CH1 C3 > C3 (planned > sent), the sign that the written pitch was used on purpose.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, the Song editor holds only slot 1, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8) to open the Song editor. Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both, and tap slot 2. Slot 2 is selected and bright, slot 1 is lit: slot 2 holds a copy of the melody.

steps.title: Raise the copy by two semitones
steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8). Press the left end of the transposition fader at (9,8) to set -12, then press (16,8) fourteen times to reach +2. The Scale overview shows Transpose +2 for this slot.

steps.title: Hear the copy
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen, then tap Play to stop. The copy loops D, E, F sharp, G: MIDI 62, 64, 66 and 67 in the strip below.

steps.title: Slot 1 keeps its pitches
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and tap Play (1,8). Slot 1 still loops C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65): the transposition belongs to the copy only. Tap Play to stop.

lock-lead-menu-values.title: Send lock values before their notes

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-note phrase through a MIDI device. The tempo is 130 BPM, the sequencer is stopped, the norns shows channel 1's Device screen and the PARAMS menu is closed. No trig params are assigned yet, so no CC values are sent.

steps.title: Assign CC 1 to a Trig params slot
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and tap step 5 at (5,4) to extend the channel range to steps 1 to 5. Then on Channel tasks > Trig params assign CC 1 to a slot with E3 and K3, so steps can carry CC lock values. The phrase plays from the internal clock at 130 BPM.

steps.title: Give steps CC values, set lead to 0
steps.caption: On Trig params, hold each of steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 in turn and turn E3 to give it its own CC 1 lock value. Then tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, choose MOSAIC and select Lock lead time (ms) in the Parameter locks section. Turn E3 to 0. At 0 each lock value is sent at the same moment as its step, together with the note. This is the original timing.

steps.title: Hear it at 0 ms
steps.caption: Close the menu and press Play (1,8), listen to the phrase and press Play again to stop. In the MIDI strip every CC 1 value sits at the same millisecond as its Note On.

steps.title: Set 25 ms lead
steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Lock lead time (ms) and set it to 25, the default. At 130 BPM each lock value will now leave about 29 ms before its step (25 ms rounded up to a whole clock pulse of 4.8 ms). The notes keep their exact times.

steps.title: Hear it at 25 ms
steps.caption: Close the menu, press Play (1,8) and Stop. In the MIDI strip each CC 1 value now arrives about 29 ms before its Note On, which still falls at its usual time. A synth that smooths incoming CC changes has already reached the new value when the note starts.

steps.title: Set 50 ms lead
steps.caption: Tap K1, reopen Lock lead time (ms) and set it to 50. At 130 BPM lock values will leave about 53 ms (11 pulses) ahead of their step, and the notes still sound at their usual times. Use the larger lead for slow filters or effects that need longer to settle.

steps.title: Hear it at 50 ms
steps.caption: Close the menu, press Play (1,8) and Stop. In the MIDI strip each CC 1 value arrives about 53 ms before its Note On, so the change lands before the note rather than gliding through it. The notes do not move.

panic-from-song-channel.title: Panic by holding Channel while on Song

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Pattern 1 is assigned to channel 1 over steps 1 to 4. The sequencer is stopped, so no note is sounding, and three MIDI ports are connected. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen; the next step opens Song.

steps.title: Open the Song page
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8). The Song page opens (Song Playback, SONG 01) and Song is the lit page button. Panic only works from the button of a page you are not on, so every other page button, including Channel (3,8), is a panic button from here.

steps.title: Hold Channel for two seconds
steps.caption: Hold the Channel button (3,8), a page you are not on, for about two seconds, then release it. Mosaic sends Note Off for every one of the 128 notes on all 16 MIDI channels of each of the three connected ports, 6,144 messages. Nothing was sounding, so you hear no change and the screen stays on Song; the sweep only matters when a note is stuck. Holding the button of the page you are already on does nothing. Playback is not stopped by a panic.

panic-from-song-pattern.title: Panic by holding Pattern while on Song

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Pattern 1 is assigned to channel 1 over steps 1 to 4. The sequencer is stopped, so no note is sounding, and three MIDI ports are connected. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen; the next step opens Song.

steps.title: Open the Song page
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8). The Song page opens (Song Playback, SONG 01) and Song is the lit page button. Panic only works from the button of a page you are not on, so every other page button, including Pattern (5,8), is a panic button from here.

steps.title: Hold Pattern for two seconds
steps.caption: Hold the Pattern button (5,8), a page you are not on, for about two seconds, then release it. Mosaic sends Note Off for every one of the 128 notes on all 16 MIDI channels of each of the three connected ports, 6,144 messages. Nothing was sounding, so you hear no change and the screen stays on Song; the sweep only matters when a note is stuck. Holding the button of the page you are already on does nothing. Playback is not stopped by a panic.

transpose-explicit-zero-and-clear.title: Lock transposition without losing the global setting

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. The Scale page is open on the transposition fader along the bottom row. Global transposition is +4 (set at (13,8)). Scale-track step 2 has a transposition lock of 0, the fader's centre at (12,8), and step 1 has a lock of -12, the lowest value at (9,8). The MIDI strip reads 48, 62, 64, 65: step 1 sounds an octave below its written note, while steps 2 to 4 ignore the global +4 because the zero lock on step 2 holds for the rest of the loop. This is how you keep one part of a song at its written pitch while the rest is transposed.

steps.title: Walk step 1 up to an explicit zero
steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press the right end of the fader, (16,8), twelve times, playing as you go if you like. Each press adds one semitone, from -12 up to 0. A lock of 0 is an explicit lock: it overrides the global +4, so step 1 plays MIDI 60 and not 64.

steps.title: Walk on up to +12
steps.caption: Keep holding step 1 and press (16,8) twelve more times. Each press adds one semitone, up to +12. The first note jumps an octave to MIDI 72. Steps 2 to 4 still follow the zero lock on step 2 and stay at MIDI 62, 64 and 65.

steps.title: Clear the lock on step 1
steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press K2 to remove its lock. Step 1 now follows the global +4 and plays MIDI 64. The zero lock on step 2 is still active for steps 2 to 4, so the loop plays MIDI 64, 62, 64 and 65.

transpose-lock-direct-taps.title: Jump a transposition lock straight to a value

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. The Scale page is open on the transposition fader along the bottom row. Global transposition is +4. Scale-track step 2 has a transposition lock of 0, the fader's centre at (12,8), and step 1 has just been locked to -12 with one tap on the lowest value, (9,8), while it was held. The MIDI strip reads 48, 62, 64, 65.

steps.title: Jump to an explicit zero
steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and tap the centre of the fader, (12,8), once. The lock moves from -12 straight to 0 with no walking. A lock of 0 overrides the global +4, so step 1 plays MIDI 60 and not 64.

steps.title: Jump up an octave
steps.caption: Hold step 1 and tap (15,8) once. The lock jumps to +12, and the first note sounds an octave up at MIDI 72. Steps 2 to 4 still follow the zero lock on step 2, MIDI 62, 64 and 65.

steps.title: Clear the lock on step 1
steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press K2 to remove its lock. Step 1 follows the global +4 again and plays MIDI 64, so the loop plays 64, 62, 64 and 65.

octave-local-over-global.title: Place one step in another octave

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI notes 60, 62, 64 and 65. The channel octave is 0 and no step has an octave lock. The Device page is showing. The octave buttons sit along the bottom row, (8,8) for -2 up to (12,8) for +2, with (10,8) the written octave.

steps.title: Drop the channel two octaves, and lock step 2 to the same
steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3. With no step held, tap octave -2 at (8,8): the channel octave is -2 and the whole melody will drop two octaves. Hold step 2 and tap (8,8) too, then keep holding step 2: (8,8) is lit, showing that step's octave.

steps.title: A lock equal to the channel octave sounds the same
steps.caption: Release step 2, press Play (1,8), then Stop. The MIDI strip reads 36, 38, 40 and 41 (C1, D1, E1, F1). A lock equal to the channel octave changes nothing you can hear. A low channel octave suits a bass line.

steps.title: Lock step 2 one octave higher
steps.caption: Hold step 2 and press K2 to clear its lock; play and stop, and all four steps follow the channel octave again. Then hold step 2 and tap octave -1 at (9,8), and keep it held: (9,8) lights while the step is held. Play, then Stop: step 2 sounds at MIDI 50, one octave above the channel setting, and the other steps stay at 36, 40 and 41.

steps.title: A local octave overrides the channel
steps.caption: Hold step 2, press K2 to clear its lock, play and stop. Then hold step 2 and tap octave 0 at (10,8). 0 is a lock like any other: step 2 returns to its written octave and sounds two octaves above its neighbours. MIDI 36, 62, 40 and 41.

steps.title: K2 restores the channel octave
steps.caption: Hold step 2 and press K2 to clear its octave lock. All four steps follow the channel octave -2 again: MIDI 36, 38, 40 and 41.

steps.title: Lock a step above the written octave
steps.caption: Hold step 2 and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Step 2 sounds at MIDI 74, an octave above its written note, while the other steps stay at 36, 40 and 41.

scale-lock-scope-and-lifetime.title: Let a scale lock last for the phrase

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of C major, so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 in the plain scale. The scale track is four steps long. Scale slot 2 (D major) is applied, slot 3 is E major (root up four semitones) and slot 4 is G major (root up seven). A global scale lock puts slot 4 on scale-track step 2, and a channel lock puts slot 3 on channel step 1. Scales lock until ptn end is On, its default, so the channel lock beats the global lock for the whole pattern. The MIDI strip reads 64, 66, 68, 69: E major.

steps.title: Turn the lifetime option off, then play
steps.caption: Press K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Scales lock until ptn end Off. Return and Play. The channel lock now ends at the next trig that plays. Step 2 clears it, so steps 2 to 4 follow the global G-major lock: the strip reads MIDI 64, 69, 71 and 72.

scale-lock-skipped-trig.title: Keep a scale lock through a silent step

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the same four-step melody (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 in plain C major) through a MIDI device. Slot 3 (E major) is locked on channel step 1, slot 4 (G major) is locked globally on scale-track step 2, and Scales lock until ptn end is Off, so the channel lock ends at the next trig that plays. All four steps play, so the strip reads MIDI 64, 69, 71 and 72: E major on step 1, then G major.

steps.title: A trig that does not play keeps the lock
steps.caption: Open Trig params and assign Trig Probability to a slot. Hold step 2 and set its probability to 0, so step 2 is silent, then Play. A trig that does not play does not clear the lock; step 3 is the next trig that plays and clears it. The strip reads MIDI 64, 71 and 72, with a gap where step 2 was.

steps.title: Clear the probability lock
steps.caption: Hold step 2 and press K2 on Trig params to remove its probability lock, then Play. Step 2 plays again and clears the channel lock, so the notes return to MIDI 64, 69, 71 and 72.

steps.title: A rest also leaves the lock in place
steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor with (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1) and press step 2 to remove its trig, then return to the Channel editor with (3,8) and Play. A rest does not clear the lock either; the next trig that plays does. The strip reads MIDI 64, 71 and 72.

scale-lock-replacement.title: Replace a scale lock with a later one

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step melody through a MIDI device with the scale locks from the last scenes: slot 3 (E major) locked on channel step 1, slot 4 (G major) locked globally on scale-track step 2, and Scales lock until ptn end Off. Step 2 is a rest, so the strip reads MIDI 64, 71 and 72 with a gap where step 2 was.

steps.title: A new channel lock replaces the old one
steps.caption: Put the trig back on step 2. Hold channel step 3 and press scale slot 2 at (2,3) to lock it to D major, then Play. With the option Off, E major applies at step 1 and ends at step 2, and D major applies at step 3 and ends at step 4. The strip reads MIDI 64, 69, 66 and 72.

steps.title: Turn the option back on, then play
steps.caption: Press K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Scales lock until ptn end On, then return and Play. The E-major lock now lasts until the step 3 lock replaces it, and the D-major lock lasts to the end of the pattern. The strip reads MIDI 64, 66, 66 and 67.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned in an eight-step loop. Pattern 1 plays four notes (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) and is saved as its Anchor; pattern 2 plays MIDI 60 on steps 5 and 7. Merge strategy is Skip, the default. Channel 2 has no anchor. Merge modes is open for channel 1. Terms used below: Strategy is the choice you make with E3 or grid key (14,8); Active is the strategy that is playing now; Pending is a choice waiting for its boundary and Boundary says when it will apply; Request says whether a choice was accepted, for example NEEDS ANCHOR.

steps.title: Keep the foundation, add the other pattern
steps.caption: Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads FOUNDATION (grid key (14,8) steps through the same choices). Select Active: it reads FOUNDATION. The first pattern stays whole and the second only adds notes.

assertion.characterization: shared effective selector

steps.title: Hear quieter additions
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) for two eight-step loops. The four anchor notes keep their velocities; MIDI 60 is added on steps 5 and 7 at velocity 70.

steps.title: Numeric modes still edit
steps.caption: Under Foundation, Note, Velocity and Length modes still edit. Select each on Merge modes and turn E3 right to read UP, then left to read AVERAGE again.

steps.title: Press the key again
steps.caption: Press (14,8) again: Strategy reads FRAGMENTS.

steps.title: Saved modes are locked
steps.caption: Strategy and Active read FRAGMENTS and (14,8) is at its brightest. The saved Note, Velocity and Length merge settings show AVERAGE SAVED; turning E3 on them changes nothing while Fragments is active.

assertion.characterization: shared effective selector

steps.title: Hear one source fragment
steps.caption: With Size 8 and Seed 0 the loop takes pattern 2 whole: tap Play to hear MIDI 60 on steps 5 and 7 at velocity 100, the source's own velocity.

steps.title: Wrap to Skip
steps.caption: Press (14,8): Strategy wraps from FRAGMENTS round to SKIP and the key dims to its lowest level.

steps.title: Return to the retained modes
steps.caption: Select Note, Velocity and Length mode: the saved settings return as editable AVERAGE. Strategy order: Skip, Only, All, Foundation, Fragments; E3 stops at the ends but the grid key wraps.

assertion.characterization: shared effective selector

steps.title: Hear only the shared attacks
steps.caption: Press (14,8) to choose ONLY. Only steps used by both patterns sound, and these patterns share none, so the grid shows no sounding trigs and Play gives no notes.

steps.title: Compare the original additions
steps.caption: Press (14,8) once more to choose ALL, then press Play (1,8) for two loops and Play again to stop. With ALL, every attack of both patterns sounds: six in all. The added notes at steps 5 and 7 now use their source velocity, 100, not Foundation's 70.

steps.title: Channel two has no anchor
steps.caption: Select channel 2 and open Merge Shape > Rhythm. Anchor reads NONE: this channel has no foundation pattern saved.

steps.title: Read Request - NEEDS ANCHOR
steps.caption: Assign patterns 1 and 2 to channel 2, open Merge modes, set Strategy to ALL and turn E3 right once to request Foundation. Turn E2 down the list to Request: it reads NEEDS ANCHOR, because channel 2 has no anchor pattern saved. Active stays ALL and Pending stays NONE.

steps.title: Recognise a missing anchor
steps.caption: Turn E2 back up to Strategy. It shows FOUNDATION while the footer reads NEEDS ANCHOR and Active is still ALL, so the refused choice stays visible but nothing changes in what plays.

assertion.characterization: shared effective selector

steps.title: The key still moves on
steps.caption: Press (14,8) again: Strategy moves on to FRAGMENTS, so a refused request does not trap the key.

steps.title: Set channel 2 back to ALL
steps.caption: Turn E3 left until Strategy reads ALL again on channel 2.

steps.title: Back to channel one
steps.caption: Tap pattern slots 1 and 2 at (1,2) and (2,2) to take both patterns off channel 2, press Channel (3,8) and select channel 1 at (1,1). Open Channel tasks > Merge Shape > Rhythm: Anchor reads 1.

steps.title: Read Request - NEEDS ANCHOR again
steps.caption: On the Channel editor toggle pattern slot 2 off and on, then remove pattern slot 1, the anchor pattern. Back on Merge modes turn E3 right once and turn E2 down to Request: Foundation is refused in the same way and Request reads NEEDS ANCHOR again. Active stays ALL.

steps.title: Keep the assigned source explicit
steps.caption: Turn E2 back up to Strategy: it shows FOUNDATION and the footer reads NEEDS ANCHOR. Assign the anchor pattern again to recover.

assertion.characterization: shared effective selector

steps.title: Return to ALL with the anchor back
steps.caption: Press (14,8): Strategy moves on to FRAGMENTS. Tap pattern slot 1 at (1,2) to assign the anchor pattern again, then select Strategy and turn E3 left to ALL.

steps.title: Read Pending - FOUNDATION
steps.caption: Check Strategy still reads ALL, press Play (1,8), then turn E3 right once to request Foundation while ALL is playing. Turn E2 down to Pending: it reads FOUNDATION, the choice waiting for its boundary.

steps.title: Request a change during playback
steps.caption: Turn E2 further down to Boundary, which reads NEXT CYCLE. The current loop keeps playing ALL until it ends.

assertion.characterization: shared effective selector

steps.title: Hear the change at the loop boundary
steps.caption: Listen across the loop boundary. The first loop still uses the source velocity 100 on the added notes; the next complete loop plays Foundation's velocity 70. Playback never stops for the change.

steps.title: Find the single Strategy selector
steps.caption: Open Merge Shape from Channel tasks. It shows the accepted Strategy as a read-only summary; turning E3 there does not choose another strategy. Choose strategies with (14,8) or on Merge modes.

assertion.characterization: shared effective selector

steps.title: Edit Add amount without applying
steps.caption: Press E2 to Rhythm, select Add amount and turn E3 left: it reads an unapplied 99.

steps.title: Discard the parameter draft before selecting Strategy
steps.caption: Press K2 to leave without applying, open the Strategy selector and return to Rhythm. The accepted Add amount is still 100: an unapplied draft is discarded.

assertion.characterization: shared effective selector
assertion.label: Add amount

foundation-protected-and-added.title: Keep anchors and accent the additions

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps on the test device with Merge Shape set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, on steps 1 to 4) is saved as the protected Anchor: its steps always play as written. Pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Add amount is how many additions are admitted and Add accent scales their velocity. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

steps.title: Read Add amount and Add accent
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Add amount, which reads 100: every candidate addition is admitted. Turn E2 two detents on to Add accent, which reads 70 and scales the velocity of the added trigs to 70 percent. Both settings are already at these values; you only read them here. The grid shows the anchors on steps 1 to 4 and the additions on steps 5 and 7.

steps.title: Hear anchors and additions
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two eight-step loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays the four anchors, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, then two additions as MIDI 60 at velocity 70, shown in the strip below. Anchor velocities are untouched; only the added notes use Add accent.

steps.title: Lower Add accent to 40
steps.caption: Turn E3 left 30 detents. Add accent reads 40; press K3 to apply it, as the sequencer is stopped.

steps.title: Hear quieter additions
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. The four anchors are exactly as before, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, but the two additions are now MIDI 60 at velocity 40 in the strip below, quieter than the 70 you heard before.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps on the test device with Merge Shape set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, on steps 1 to 4) is the protected Anchor and pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) offers additions; both are assigned. Add amount is 100 and Add accent 70, so all candidate additions are allowed and sound at 70 percent of their velocity. The Phrase settings are still at their defaults, the norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

steps.title: Set Cycles to 2
steps.caption: Press E1 once to the Phrase screen, turn E2 to Phrase and press K3. A cycle is one pass of the eight-step loop. Turn E3 once to set Cycles to 2.

steps.title: Choose the Build shape
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Shape and E3 once to choose BUILD, which reads Cycle 1 50 and Cycle 2 100.

steps.title: Apply the phrase
steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED.

steps.title: Loop 1 adds one note
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen. The first loop plays steps 1 to 4 plus one addition (step 7), five notes in the strip below.

steps.title: Loop 2 adds both
steps.caption: The second loop plays steps 1 to 4 plus both additions (steps 5 and 7), six notes. Keep listening to at least four loops, then tap Stop.

steps.title: Build over two channel loops
steps.caption: The two loops keep alternating: the strip below shows the notes of each pass, loop 1 with step 7 added and loop 2 with steps 5 and 7 added, back to the first anchor at the end.

fragments-seed-source-choice.title: Let each fragment keep its source notes

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays through the test device on an 8-step loop at 90 BPM, rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6. Both patterns are assigned to channel 1 and Strategy is still SKIP. Merge modes is open for channel 1. In this scene a Seed makes a repeatable draw of which pattern each fragment comes from: the same seed always gives the same choice.

steps.title: Choose Fragments
steps.caption: Select Strategy and turn E3 to FRAGMENTS. Strategy and Active both read FRAGMENTS: the loop will be cut into fragments and each fragment will come from one source pattern, chosen by the Seed.

steps.title: Set Size to 4
steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Rhythm. Turn E3 once left so Size reads 4 and press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the eight-step loop is now cut into two four-step fragments, one for steps 1 to 4 and one for steps 5 to 8. On the grid only step 3 is bright: with the starting seed the first fragment comes from pattern 2 (a note on step 3 only) and the second from pattern 1, which has no notes in steps 5 to 8.

steps.title: Seed 0 picks the sparse draw
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays one C (MIDI 60) at velocity 100, a single note in the strip below. Seed 0 gives steps 1 to 4 to pattern 2 and steps 5 to 8 to pattern 1, which has no trigs there, and pattern 1's own E on step 3 is not mixed in.

steps.title: Pick seed 1
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Seed and turn E3 once right so it reads 1. The grid still shows the result of seed 0 until you apply the change.

steps.title: Apply seed 1
steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the grid now lights steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6. Seed 1 gives steps 1 to 4 to pattern 1 and steps 5 to 8 to pattern 2. Try other seeds, 2, 3 and so on, and listen for how each draw reshuffles the fragments.

steps.title: Each fragment keeps its source
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays pattern 1's C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and then pattern 2's C on step 6 at velocity 100. Each fragment keeps the notes and velocities of the pattern it came from.

interlock-leader-window.title: Leave room around a leader’s anchors

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Two 8-step channels play at 90 BPM through the test device. Channel 1 (MIDI channel 1) has pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and pattern 2 (steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has pattern 3, a single trig on step 5, as its Foundation anchor. Channel 1 has no Interlock leader yet. The norns shows channel 1's Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

steps.title: Open Interlock
steps.caption: Select Interlock with E2 and press K3 to open the Interlock page for channel 1. This keeps channel 1's additions out of the way of another channel's anchors.

steps.title: Choose the leader
steps.caption: Select Leader and turn E3 once right to CH02. Channel 2 would lead channel 1; nothing changes until you apply.

steps.title: Apply: channel 2 leads
steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED, Window is 0 and Status reads ON. Step 5 goes dark on the grid because channel 1's addition starts exactly on channel 2's anchor. Steps 1 to 4 and step 7 stay lit.

steps.title: Only the coincidence is removed
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and step 7, and channel 2 plays its anchor on step 5 on MIDI channel 2. Nothing from channel 1 sounds on step 5.

steps.title: Edge case: widen the window while playing
steps.caption: The lesson above is complete; the next four steps are edge cases. Tap Play. While it plays, select Window, turn E3 twice right to 2 and press K3. The footer reads NEXT CYCLE: playback is still running, so Window 2 is queued and starts at the next loop.

steps.title: Edge case: a later draft is discarded
steps.caption: Window 2 is still queued. Turn E3 back to 0 as a new draft and press K2: the draft is discarded and Rhythm returns. Press K3 to reopen Interlock: Window still reads 2, the accepted value, not the discarded 0.

steps.title: Edge case: the window takes over at the loop boundary
steps.caption: After a few loops press Stop. The strip shows every loop played whole: the first loops with step 7, then without it once Window 2 took effect. The grid now shows steps 1 to 4.

steps.title: Select channel 2
steps.caption: Select channel 2 (grid (2,1)). The screen shows channel 2's Merge Shape list, ready to set a leader for it.

steps.title: Open channel 2's Interlock
steps.caption: Open Rhythm and then Interlock for channel 2: turn E2 to the row and press K3 each time. The header reads INTERLOCK CH02.

steps.title: Make channel 1 its leader
steps.caption: Select Leader and turn E3 once right to CH01. Channel 2 already leads channel 1, so this would make a chain.

steps.title: Edge case: a leader chain is refused
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply. The footer reads INVALID CHANNEL IS A LEADER: channel 2 already leads channel 1, so it cannot follow channel 1, and nothing changes.

steps.title: The refusal changes nothing
steps.caption: Press K2 to discard the draft and select channel 1 (grid (1,1)); the screen shows its Merge Shape list. Play two loops: Window 2 still applies, so channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and channel 2 plays step 5.

structure-anchor-chord-and-delete.title: Snap Foundation anchors to a chord

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on the test device, the four-note melody C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) on steps 1 to 4. The additions of the Foundation phrase on steps 5 and 7 do not exist yet; you add them in the next step. No Harmony Ensemble group exists and Structure markers are off, so every note plays as written. The norns shows the Device page and the grid lights steps 1 to 4.

steps.title: Add the additions, open Ensemble
steps.caption: Hold step 1 (1,4) and tap step 8 (8,4) to loop eight steps. Open the pattern page (5,8), choose pattern 2 (2,1), tap trigs on steps 5 and 7, return to Channel (3,8) and assign pattern 2 (2,2). Then open Channel tasks > Harmony and choose Ensemble. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH01.

steps.title: Make the chord three notes
steps.caption: On the Ensemble list choose Create group and press K3 to make group 1. Select Template count with E2 and turn E3 to 3: the group's chord has three tones.

steps.title: Set Tone 2
steps.caption: Select Tone 2 with E2 and turn E3 to 2, two scale degrees above the root, which is E in C major.

steps.title: Set Tone 3
steps.caption: Select Tone 3 with E2 and turn E3 to 4, four scale degrees above the root, which is G. The chord is now C, E and G.

steps.title: Apply the chord
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply: the footer reads APPLIED.

steps.title: Open Members
steps.caption: Press K2 to return to the Ensemble list, select Members and press K3. The header reads MEMBERS CH01: the list of channels that follow the group's chord.

steps.title: Switch the group on
steps.caption: Set Group enabled to On with E3 and press K3. Voice count reads 1: channel 1, the only member, carries the chord on its own. The footer reads APPLIED.

steps.title: Turn Foundation on
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Merge Shape, set Mode to Foundation and press K3 to apply. Open Merge modes: Strategy and Active read FOUNDATION, so the four anchors on steps 1 to 4 plus the additions on steps 5 and 7 now play.

steps.title: Open Structure
steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Pitch, then choose Structure. Structure snaps chosen moments of the Foundation line to a chord while the notes in between keep their own pitch.

steps.title: Markers on anchors
steps.caption: Turn E3 once to set Markers to ANCHORS: every anchor onset now counts as a marker.

steps.title: Chord group one appears
steps.caption: A Chord group row appears showing 1, the Ensemble group you made. Structure needs an enabled group before Apply will accept the markers.

steps.title: Anchors snap to the chord
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then tap Play. Each anchor note snaps to the nearest chord tone, and a note exactly between two chord tones snaps to the lower one. Step 1 stays at 60, step 2 moves from 62 to 60, step 3 stays at 64 and step 4 moves from 65 to 64: the loop plays MIDI 60, 60, 64, 64 in the strip below. The added notes on steps 5 and 7 keep their own pitch and accent. Tap Play to stop.

steps.title: Check who deletion affects
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony > Ensemble and choose Delete group for group 1. A confirmation opens before anything is deleted; its Affected row reads 1, naming channel 1 as the channel that uses the group.

steps.title: Deletion restores authored pitches
steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm. Deleting the group also sets Markers to OFF in the same change. Tap Play: the anchors return to their written pitches, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65, and the added notes on steps 5 and 7 are unchanged. Tap Play to stop.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1 to 4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through the test device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (rate /1). Each step is a single voice: no chord notes are set and Harmony is Off. Playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Add a second voice
steps.caption: Open Masks for channel 1 and turn E3 one detent on Chd1, the first chord note. Chd1 reads 2nd: each step now sounds a second voice one scale step above its note, so the pairs are C+D, D+E, E+F and F+G (60+62, 62+64, 64+65, 65+67).

steps.title: Open Harmony
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony; the header reads VOICE LEADING CH01.

steps.title: Revoice the pairs
steps.caption: Set Mode to REVOICE and press K3 (Preset SMOOTH). Tap Play for two loops. Revoice keeps each pair's two pitch classes but chooses their octaves for the smoothest movement: both notes drop an octave to 48+50, 50+52, 52+53 and 53+55, at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97 in the strip below. Tap Stop.

harmony-ensemble-and-local-bypass.title: Share a voicing while keeping each channel’s rhythm

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Four channels play through the test device, each on its own MIDI channel (1 to 4) with its own sparse rhythm: channel 1 plays the four-step phrase, channel 2 steps 1 and 3, channel 3 steps 2 and 4 and channel 4 step 4. Scale slot 1 (C major) is applied, Harmony is Off on every channel and no scale or octave locks are set, so each channel plays its own written pitches. A Harmony Ensemble group lets several channels share one chord: each member gets a role (Bass, Inner or Top), keeps its own rhythm, and takes its pitch from the group's shared voicing. The norns shows the Device page of channel 4.

steps.title: Create group 1 and open Members
steps.caption: On channel 1 open Channel tasks > Harmony, go to Groups, create group 1 with the Four-part smooth preset and open Members. The header reads MEMBERS CH01: this is where you choose which channels belong to the group.

steps.title: Assign the members, join channel 1
steps.caption: Assign channels 1 to 4 as the members, in order, with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save: the group is complete but still off. Press E1 back to the Harmony list, set Mode to ENSEMBLE with E3, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 1. Then select channel 2 (2,1): its Voice leading page opens.

steps.title: Join channel 2
steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 2. Then select channel 3 (3,1): its Voice leading page opens.

steps.title: Join channel 3
steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 3. Then select channel 4 (4,1): its Voice leading page opens.

steps.title: Join channel 4 and open Ensemble
steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 4. Then turn E2 to Ensemble and press K3. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH04.

steps.title: Switch the group on
steps.caption: On channel 4's Ensemble page select Group enabled and turn E3 to ON. Until now the group existed but did nothing.

steps.title: Four roles, four rhythms, one chord
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then tap Play. Channels 1 to 4 take the roles Bass, Inner, Inner and Top. Each channel keeps its own rhythm and velocities, but all four take their pitch from one shared chord voicing: listen for a single chord spread across the four channels, MIDI 48, 55, 64 and 67 in the strip below. Tap Play to stop.

steps.title: Lock channel 2 to E major
