full-quantisation-precedence.title: Choose which note masks follow the scale

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1; both are already set in the scale editor. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Snap note masks to scale is On, while Quantise note masks (the global full-quantisation option) and Lock merged to pent. are Off. With Snap alone the masks play as written, 60, 64, 69, 71 in the MIDI strip, because Degree and Rotation affect masks only under full quantisation. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. Each step below lists the state as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / X / X.

steps.title: Global: turn full quantisation On
steps.caption: State: On / X / X / X. Press K1, open the Mosaic params and turn Quantise note masks On (the global option). Play, then stop: the same masks now follow Degree II and Rotation 1 and the strip reads 62, 65, 71, 60.

steps.title: Channel: an Off beats the global On
steps.caption: State: On / Off / X / X. Open Channel tasks > Trig params, press K2 and turn E3 to Quantise Note Mask in the parameter list. Press K3 to assign it and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to Off. Play, then stop: the written phrase 60, 64, 69, 71 returns, because the channel setting beats the global On.

steps.title: Step: map just one step
steps.caption: State: On / Off / X / On. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to On to lock that step, then release. Play, then stop: only step 2 changes, to 65. The strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

full-quantisation-inherit-and-step-off.title: Let the channel inherit the global setting

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: On / Off / X / On. The channel Off beats the global On and step 2 has its own On lock, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

steps.title: Channel: X inherits the global On
steps.caption: State: On / X / X / On. With no step held, turn the channel value down to X (unset). The global On applies again: 62, 65, 71, 60. Step 2 keeps its own On lock.

steps.title: Step: switch one step Off
steps.caption: State: On / X / Off / On. Hold step 1, turn E3 one detent up from X to Off and release. Play, then stop: step 1 plays its written note, 60, even though the global option is On. The strip reads 60, 65, 71, 60.

steps.title: Global: turn full quantisation Off
steps.caption: State: Off / X / Off / On. Press K1, open the Mosaic params and turn Quantise note masks Off. The channel value is still X, so it follows the global Off. Play, then stop: steps 3 and 4 play as written and step 2 keeps its On lock, 60, 65, 69, 71.

full-quantisation-channel-beats-global.title: Let the channel beat the global setting

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / Off / On. The global Off is inherited by the channel, step 1 is Off and step 2 is On, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.

steps.title: Channel: On beats the global Off
steps.caption: State: Off / On / Off / On. With no step held, turn E3 two detents up to On. Play, then stop: the channel On beats the global Off, so steps 3 and 4 follow the scale again, 60, 65, 71, 60.

steps.title: Step: clear an Off, then try an explicit X
steps.caption: First hold step 1, press K2 and release: the Off lock clears and the channel On applies. Play, then stop: 62, 65, 71, 60 (state Off / On / X / On). Then hold step 1, turn E3 all the way down to X and release. An explicit step X skips the channel and uses the global option directly, here Off, so step 1 plays its written note: 60, 65, 71, 60.

mask-locks-clear-neighbours.title: Clear a note mask without clearing its neighbour

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. The Masks page (Channel tasks, then Masks) is open on Note. The channel's Note mask default is 67 (G3), step 1 has its own mask 72 and step 2 has 74, so the MIDI strip reads 72, 74, 67, 67.

steps.title: Clear step 1 only
steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), press K2 and release. Step 1 falls back to the channel default, 67, but step 2 keeps its 74. Play, then stop: the strip reads 67, 74, 67, 67.

steps.title: A held step wins over the shift clear
steps.caption: Hold step 1 again, hold K1 and press K2, then release. With a step held, only that step is cleared, even while K1 is down, and step 1 has nothing left to clear. Play, then stop: the strip still reads 67, 74, 67, 67.

steps.title: Clear every step mask on the channel
steps.caption: With no step held, hold K1 and press K2. Every step exception clears but the channel default stays. Play, then stop: the strip reads 67, 67, 67, 67.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: A new project with playback stopped, the default C major scale and Rate /1 (one step is a sixteenth note) on every channel. Channel 1 is set up and its Device page is open: it plays range 1-4, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, to its own MIDI output. Channel 2 is not set up yet.

steps.title: Select channel 2
steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device and press K3. The header reads CH02: this second channel will play a three-step loop.

steps.title: Build channel 2, then play both loops
steps.caption: Give channel 2 its own MIDI output on the Device page. Give it pattern 1 and the range steps 1-3 (hold step 1 and tap step 3), then open Masks and set its values: Note 79, Vel 40 and Len ½ on every step, with step 2 locked to Note 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Select channel 1 and press Play. Both channels start together on step 1. At step 4 channel 1 plays its fourth note, 65, while channel 2, whose three-step loop has wrapped, plays 79 again: look for 65 beside 79 in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step".

steps.title: Both channels keep looping
steps.caption: Keep playing. Channel 1 loops four steps on its own MIDI port and channel 2 loops three on another, so their notes fall out of step and the MIDI strip shows two different phrases running side by side.

steps.title: Both loops restart together at step 13
steps.caption: Keep playing. Hold step 4 and tap step 2 on channel 1: the reversed range (start 4, end 2) is refused and both loops carry on. Twelve steps after the start, the first step count that both 4 and 3 divide into, both phrases begin again from their first notes at the same moment: channel 1 plays 60 as channel 2 plays 79, and the next step plays 62 with 81. Look for that sequence in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", two seconds after the loops started.

steps.title: Both loops stay locked
steps.caption: Press Stop. The refused reversed range changed nothing: both phrases keep the same timing, notes, velocities and lengths. Channel 1 still plays 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97 over steps 1 to 4, and channel 2 plays 79, 81, 79 over steps 1 to 3. Playback is stopped and the Masks screen is showing.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device on OUT 1 and channel 2 to a second output, MIDI port 2 on MIDI channel 2. Each channel has its Masks defaults set so that every step sounds: channel 1 plays a low drum note, C1 (MIDI 36), at velocity 100 and channel 2 plays MIDI 72 at velocity 90, both half a step long. Channel 1's Masks screen is open. The Rate is /1 at 90 BPM, so one step lasts a sixth of a second, and playback is stopped.

steps.title: Enter the drum pattern
steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) for Pattern Trig and choose pattern 1 at (1,1). Tap steps 2, 3 and 4 off at (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4), then tap steps 5, 9 and 13 on at (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4). Pattern 1 now has trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: four hits per bar.

steps.title: Enter the short figure
steps.caption: Choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1, 3 and 4 at (1,4), (3,4) and (4,4): a figure with trigs on steps 1, 3 and 4.

steps.title: Give channel 1 sixteen steps
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8) and channel 1 at (1,1); pattern 1 is already assigned to it. Hold step 1 at (1,4), tap step 16 at (16,4) and release step 1. The footer reads Channel 1 length changed: channel 1 now loops steps 1 to 16, and its four drum steps stay lit.

steps.title: Give channel 2 five steps
steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 at (5,4) and release step 1. The footer reads Channel 2 length changed: channel 2 loops steps 1 to 5, and its three figure steps are lit.

steps.title: Play 80 steps
steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap Play (1,8). The drum channel repeats every 16 steps and the figure every 5, so the figure's three notes slide across the drum hits. Both channels start together on step 1 and only start together again on step 81, 80 steps or 13 and a third seconds later, because 80 is the first step count that both 16 and 5 divide into. Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step": channel 1 plays MIDI 36 four times in every 16 steps and channel 2 plays MIDI 72 three times in every 5. Tap Play again to stop.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Two 8-step channels at 90 BPM. Channel 1 has Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and Pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has Pattern 3, one trig on step 5, as its Foundation anchor, and is channel 1's Interlock leader with Window 0. Interlock ON removes a channel 1 addition that lands on the leader's anchor, so channel 1's grid shows steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 lit. Anchor gap is 0: Gap is a safety distance, 0 to 8 steps, kept clear of additions around an anchor, and 0 turns it off. Every step below is on channel 1 under Channel tasks > Merge Shape (E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Merge Shape, K3); Result, Reason and Rhythm are screens of that list.

steps.title: Open Result for step 7
steps.caption: Open Result and turn E3 to Step 7. Result shows Decision OK: the addition on step 7 is admitted.

steps.title: Inspect an admitted addition
steps.caption: Select Reason and press K3. Merge Reason lists Step 7, Role ADDITION P2 (an addition taken from Pattern 2), Decision OK, Interlock ON, Velocity 70 and Pitch target LEGACY.

assertion.characterisation: characterisation outside legacy README: suppressed Role is EMPTY P2 and Velocity is NONE

steps.title: Open Result for step 5
steps.caption: Return to Result and turn E3 to Step 5. Result shows Decision INTERLOCK CH02: this addition is refused.

steps.title: Inspect an Interlock rejection
steps.caption: Open Reason again. Step 5 sits on the leader's anchor, so Role reads EMPTY P2, Decision reads INTERLOCK CH02 and Velocity reads NONE. The addition was refused and sends no note. EMPTY P2 does not mean Pattern 2 lacks a trig on step 5.

assertion.characterisation: characterisation outside legacy README: suppressed Role is EMPTY P2 and Velocity is NONE

steps.title: Set Anchor gap to 1
steps.caption: Open Rhythm, select Anchor gap, turn E3 once right to 1 and press K3. Anchor gap 1 keeps additions one step clear of an anchor, and step 5 is now next to the anchor on step 4 as well as on the leader's anchor.

steps.title: Read the two reasons in Result
steps.caption: Open Result and select Step 5. Decision now reads GAP, INTERLOCK: two reasons are listed.

steps.title: Inspect two rejection reasons
steps.caption: Open Reason for Step 5: Decision reads GAP, INTERLOCK, with Gap listed first.

assertion.characterisation: characterisation outside legacy README: suppressed Role is EMPTY P2 and Velocity is NONE

steps.title: Play the filtered pattern
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) for two loops, then Stop. Channel 1 plays C D E F on steps 1 to 4 and its addition on step 7. Step 5 stays silent on channel 1 even though Pattern 2 has a trig there.

swing-interlock-pulse-times.title: Swing a merged part: Interlock still removes step 5

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Two 8-step channels at 90 BPM. Channel 1 has Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and Pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has one anchor trig on step 5 and is channel 1's Interlock leader. Interlock removes channel 1's addition on step 5, so channel 1's grid shows steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 lit. Clock Rate is /1 and Swing is not set (X).

steps.title: Set Swing to 25
steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3. Set Feel source to CHANNEL (E3, then K3) so this channel uses its own feel instead of the Song page's. Then select Swing and turn E3 up to 25. Swing runs from -50 to 50 and at 25 every second step is played a quarter of a step late.

steps.title: Interlock is still on
steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Interlock: Status is still ON and step 5 is still removed (step 7 is lit). Swing did not change the merge.

steps.title: Hear the swung notes
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen to a loop or two and tap Play again to stop. Step 5 is still silent. Steps 2 and 4 sound a quarter of a step (about 42 ms) late: in the MIDI strip they sit near 208 ms and 542 ms instead of 167 ms and 500 ms, while steps 1 and 3 stay put (0 and 333 ms) and the added step 7 plays quietly (velocity 70) at 1000 ms. Swing moves the notes but the merge result stays the same.

memory-undo-redo-and-branch.title: Undo, redo and replace a remembered edit

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1. Nothing has been edited yet, so the channel's memory (its list of remembered edits) is empty.

steps.title: Open History
steps.caption: Turn E2 down to History and press K3. The Memory screen shows your position in the channel's remembered edits, as 'position of total'. It reads 0 of 0 because nothing has been edited yet.

steps.title: Hear the original phrase
steps.caption: With nothing remembered, K2, K3 and E3 in History do nothing: the counter stays at 0 of 0. Tap Play (1,8): channel 1 plays C D E F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65. Tap Play again to stop.

steps.title: Record two step edits
steps.caption: Open Masks (E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). Any MIDI keyboard or controller connected to the norns can write onto a held step: hold step 1 and play note 72 at velocity 90, release, then hold step 2 and play note 76 at velocity 80. Each is one edit that Memory keeps. Reopen History: the counter reads 2 of 2, meaning you are at edit 2 of the 2 remembered.

steps.title: Undo the second edit
steps.caption: Tap Play: the phrase is 72, 76, 64, 65 at velocities 90, 80, 107, 97, because steps 1 and 2 carry your edits. Now, in History, turn E3 one detent left. The counter reads 1 of 2: the second edit is undone.

steps.title: Hear the undone state
steps.caption: Tap Play: step 1 keeps your recorded note 72 at velocity 90, and step 2 is back to its original note 62 at velocity 117.

steps.title: Return to the first state
steps.caption: Turn E3 left again: the counter reads 0 of 2, the oldest state, before either edit. (K2 jumps straight here.)

steps.title: Stop at the oldest state
steps.caption: Tap Play: the original four-step phrase 60, 62, 64, 65 is back. Then turn E3 left three more times. The counter stays at 0 of 2: you cannot go further back than the first state.

steps.title: Redo the first edit
steps.caption: Tap Play: still the original phrase. Then turn E3 right once. The counter reads 1 of 2: step 1 has its edit back.

steps.title: Redo both edits
steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 62, 64, 65, so only the first edit is back. Then turn E3 right once more. The counter is back at 2 of 2.

steps.title: Hear both edits again
steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 76, 64, 65, both recorded edits are back.

steps.title: Undo one step again
steps.caption: Turn E3 right three times: the counter stays at 2 of 2, the newest state. Tap Play for 72, 76, 64, 65, press K2 to jump all the way back (0 of 2, the original phrase when you play), then press K3 to jump forward to 2 of 2 (both edits again). Now turn E3 left once: the counter reads 1 of 2 and the second edit is undone, so a new edit will replace it.

steps.title: Replace the undone action
steps.caption: Open Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 79 at velocity 70, release, then reopen History. The counter reads 2 of 2 again, but it is a different second action: the new edit replaced the undone one.

steps.title: Hear the new branch
steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 62, 79, 65. Step 1 keeps its edit, step 2 is back to its original 62 and step 3 plays your new note 79. The old second edit (76) is gone.

output-latest-event.title: Read the latest note on Output

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1 and playback has not started, so no note has played yet.

steps.title: Open Output before anything has played
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Output and press K3. Six rows describe the last note channel 1 played: Note (the note, and any chord voices), Vel / Len (velocity and length), Step (the step it came from), Degree (the pattern degree, and what merging made of it), Pitch (the pitch in the scale, and the harmony's pitch if Harmony moved it) and Sent (the note actually sent, or why none was: MUTED or REST). Nothing has played yet, so every row reads NO EVENT and there is no cursor; this screen only displays.

steps.title: Play, then read the rows
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let the loop run, then tap Play again to stop. Output now shows the last note channel 1 played: Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel / Len 127 / 1.0 (velocity 127, one step long), Step STEP01 (the step it came from), Degree 0 (the first scale degree), Pitch C3 (the pitch in the scale) and Sent C3 (the note actually sent). Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", for the notes behind it.

steps.title: Hold a step to see what it plays
steps.caption: Turn E2 or E3 or press K3: nothing changes, because Output has no cursor. Now hold step 2 at (2,4) without tapping it. Step reads STEP02 HELD and the rows show what step 2 plays: Degree +1, Pitch D3 and Sent D3. Note and Vel / Len still show the last note played. Release the step to return to the latest note.

steps.title: A step with no note shows NO EVENT
steps.caption: Hold step 40 at (8,6), a step with no trig. Every row reads NO EVENT and Step reads STEP40 HELD: a step without a note borrows nothing from the last note played. Release the step to return to the latest note.

note-merge-numeric-output.title: Compare Average and Higher note merging

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are assigned to channel 1, so channel 1 merges them. Pattern 1 plays scale degrees 1, 3, 5, 7 (C E G B) and pattern 2 plays degrees 3, 5, 7, 1 (E G B C). Note merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (15,8). Pentatonic snapping of merged notes is off: before you try this, tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Lock merged to pent. to Off. Left On (the default), merged notes snap to the five-note pentatonic version of the scale and you hear different pitches.

steps.title: Average note merging
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Each note is the mean of the two patterns' degrees (2, 4, 6, 4): D, F, A, F = MIDI 62, 65, 69, 65. Velocity comes from pattern 1.

steps.title: Choose Higher
steps.caption: Tap (15,8) once. The button lights brighter and Note mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Higher: the mean plus the gap between the two degrees.

steps.title: Higher note merging
steps.caption: Tap Play. The notes are F, A, C, E = MIDI 65, 69, 72, 76, wider than either source. Velocity still comes from pattern 1. Use Higher to spread the two lines apart for a wider, brighter contour.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned with different velocities for four notes: 127, 117, 107, 97 and 100, 100, 100, 100. Its notes come from a third pattern, shown on the screen as Note mode PAT 4 (pattern 4 is not assigned to the channel; all its notes are MIDI 67), so only velocity changes. Velocity merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8).

steps.title: Average velocity merging
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Each velocity is the mean of the two sources, for example (127 + 100) / 2 = 114, so the four notes sound at 114, 109, 104 and 99. Read the velocities in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step": every note is MIDI 67 and only the velocity changes.

steps.title: Choose Higher
steps.caption: Tap (16,8) once, without K1 (with K1 held the same button sets length merge instead). The button lights brighter and Velocity mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Higher: the mean plus the gap between the sources.

steps.title: Higher velocity merging
steps.caption: Tap Play. The four velocities in the MIDI strip are 127, 126, 111 and 102. The first is 114 + 27 = 141, limited to 127. Use Higher to accent a step.

steps.title: Choose Lower
steps.caption: Tap (16,8) again. The button changes again and Velocity mode reads DOWN, the manual's Lower: twice the lowest source minus the mean.

steps.title: Lower velocity merging
steps.caption: Tap Play. The four velocities in the MIDI strip are 86, 91, 96 and 95. The first is 2 x 100 - 114 = 86. Use Lower for ghost notes.

steps.title: Return to Average
steps.caption: Tap (16,8) once more. The modes cycle Average, Higher, Lower and back: tap Play and the MIDI strip shows the velocities 114, 109, 104 and 99 again.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are both assigned to channel 1, with the same trigs on the same steps: pattern 1's notes are 2 steps long and pattern 2's are 4 steps long. Length merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8). Length merge is set with K1 (shift) held, which turns the velocity merge button (16,8) into the length button.

steps.title: Average length merging
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Average is the mean of the two lengths, 2 and 4, so each merged note lasts 3 steps (0.5 s).

steps.title: Choose Longer
steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (16,8) once. The button lights brighter and Length mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Longer: the mean plus the gap between the lengths. Without K1 the same button sets the velocity merge instead.

steps.title: Longer length merging
steps.caption: Tap Play. 3 + 2 = 5 steps (0.83 s), longer than either source: overlapping, legato notes. Use Longer for pads that run into each other.

steps.title: Choose Shorter
steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (16,8) again. The button changes again and Length mode reads DOWN, the manual's Shorter: twice the shortest length minus the mean.

steps.title: Shorter length merging
steps.caption: Tap Play. 2 x 2 - 3 = 1 step (0.17 s): short, staccato notes. Use Shorter for tight plucks.

steps.title: Return to Average
steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (16,8) once more: Length mode reads AVERAGE. The modes cycle Average, Longer, Shorter and back: tap Play and the notes last 3 steps again.

shuffle-smooth-amount-boundaries.title: Set Smooth shuffle and change its amount

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale, with Rate /1. Its Clock page is set to Shuffle with Feel Smooth, Basis 9 and Amount 1. Timing is counted in pulses: each step is 24 pulses, so at Amount 1 the notes sit almost exactly on the straight grid, at 0, 24, 48 and 72. Feel and Basis stay the same through this lesson; only Amount changes.

steps.title: Set shuffle amount to 50
steps.caption: Select Amount and turn E3 to 50, then tap Play (1,8). Two of the four notes in each group have moved: the second now lands at 26 pulses instead of 24 and the fourth at 71 instead of 72. Compare the ms offsets in the MIDI strip with the straight grid.

steps.title: Set shuffle amount to 0
steps.caption: Set Amount to 0 and tap Play: shuffle is off and the notes are back on the straight grid at 0, 24, 48, 72 pulses.

steps.title: Set shuffle amount to 100
steps.caption: Set Amount to 100 and tap Play: the fullest shuffle for this feel and basis, with the notes at 0, 26, 48, 69 pulses: the second note is 2 pulses late and the fourth 3 early. The second note was already at 26 at Amount 50 because offsets are whole pulses, so the extra Amount shows in the fourth note (71, then 69). For a stronger groove change Basis; the next steps use Basis 6.

steps.title: Basis 6 at Amount 0
steps.caption: Select Basis and turn E3 to 6, then set Amount to 0 and tap Play. Amount 0 is straight timing whatever the basis: the notes sit on the grid at 0, 24, 48 and 72 pulses.

steps.title: Basis 6 at Amount 50
steps.caption: Set Amount to 50 and tap Play. Basis 6 moves the notes further than Basis 9 did: the second note lands at 28 pulses and the fourth at 68, halfway to the full groove.

steps.title: Basis 6 at Amount 100
steps.caption: Set Amount to 100 and tap Play. The second note is now 8 pulses late, at 32, and the fourth 8 early, at 64: two thirds of the way through each pair. Compare the ms offsets in the MIDI strip with the straight grid, where Basis 9 at Amount 100 moved the notes only 2 or 3 pulses.

algorithm-choose-and-preview.title: Choose a trig algorithm

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Choose Euclidean
steps.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the third algorithm button (14,2). The five algorithm buttons on row 2 are, from the left: Drum (12,2), a library of classic bass, snare and hi-hat patterns; Tresillo (13,2), a 3-3-2 grouping; Euclidean (14,2), trigs spread as evenly as a mathematical rule allows; Numeric (15,2), patterns from Noise Engineering's Numeric Repetitor; and Rhythm Doctor (16,2). The Trig Algorithm screen marks Euclidean as SELECTED and the fader on grid row 2 lights its third position.

steps.title: Browse without applying
steps.caption: Turn E2 left. The screen passes Tresillo and stops on Drum, the first algorithm (a further turn stays on Drum). Drum shows no SELECTED mark and the third fader position stays lit: turning E2 only browses. Euclidean is still the algorithm in use until you press K3.

steps.title: Apply Drum
steps.caption: Press K3. Drum now reads SELECTED and the fader lights its first position. Drum draws on classic drum patterns, so it suits a kick, snare or hi-hat lane, where Euclidean suits an even pulse.

steps.title: Prime with Drum selected
steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8). The Paint Preview screen opens on Algorithm Drum with Shift 0, but no step flashes on the pattern grid: at its default settings Drum previews no steps. Prime previews whichever algorithm is selected.

steps.title: Cancel the empty preview
steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8). The preview closes and nothing was painted.

steps.title: Return to the algorithm list
steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Pattern tasks, turn E2 to Algorithm and press K3. The Trig Algorithm screen returns (a Painting cancelled tip may still show) and Drum is still SELECTED.

steps.title: Browse back to Euclidean
steps.caption: Turn E2 two detents right, past Tresillo. Euclidean is highlighted but carries no SELECTED mark yet, and the fader still shows Drum.

steps.title: Apply Euclidean
steps.caption: Press K3. Euclidean reads SELECTED and the fader lights its third position again.

steps.title: Prime now previews Euclidean
steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8) again. Now every step on the pattern grid flashes and Paint Preview reads 64 trigs: at the default settings Euclidean fills all 64 steps, where Drum previewed none. Prime always previews the algorithm that is selected, so changing the algorithm changes what Prime shows.

steps.title: Prime Tresillo for a 3-3-2 preview
steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8) to close the Euclidean preview and tap Tresillo (13,2), the second algorithm button. Like Drum, Tresillo previews nothing until you choose a pattern: tap drum bank 1 at (12,3), then tap both ends of the first fader on row 2, (2,2) and (10,2), and of the second fader on row 3, (2,3) and (10,3). Tap Prime (16,8). The algorithm fader lights its second position and Paint Preview reads Algorithm Tresillo with 8 trigs. The flashing steps are spaced 9, 9 and 6 steps apart, over and over: the 3-3-2 grouping, scaled up. Nothing is painted yet.

algorithm-choose-and-preview.starting_state: A new empty project, stopped, with Record off. No pattern has trigs, and no trig algorithm has been chosen yet. The first step opens the Pattern editor and picks the algorithm.

paint-shift-and-cancel.title: Move a rhythm before committing

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Choose Numeric
steps.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the fourth algorithm button (15,2) for Numeric. The Trig Algorithm screen marks Numeric as SELECTED. Numeric gives a sparse pattern, which makes shifts easy to see. The controls you will use on grid row 8 are Prime (16,8), Move left (10,8), Reset (11,8), Move right (12,8) and Cancel (14,8).

steps.title: Prime the pattern
steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8). The Numeric pattern flashes on the grid and Paint Preview reads Preview PAINTING, Algorithm Numeric, Shift 0 and 8 trigs, on steps 5, 13, 21, 29 and so on. Nothing is painted yet.

steps.title: Shift right
steps.caption: Tap Move right (12,8). Every flashing step moves one step to the right, from step 5 to step 6 and so on, and the Paint Preview screen reads Shift +1.

steps.title: Two taps left
steps.caption: Tap Move left (10,8) twice. The first tap takes the flashing steps back to where Prime put them (Shift 0); the second moves them one step left of that, from step 5 to step 4 and so on. The screen reads Shift -1.

steps.title: Reset the shift
steps.caption: Tap Reset (11,8). The shift returns to 0 in one tap and the flashing steps are back where Prime put them.

steps.title: Cancel the preview
steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8). Paint Preview reads Preview OFF and Trigs NONE, and no flashing steps remain. Nothing was painted, so the pattern is unchanged. To keep a shifted rhythm instead, tap Prime again while the steps are flashing; the next two steps do that.

steps.title: Prime again
steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8) again. The same Numeric steps flash again at Shift 0. Prime always starts a new preview, so you can try a rhythm, cancel it and come back to it.

steps.title: Press Prime again to paint the shifted rhythm
steps.caption: Tap Move right (12,8) so the preview reads Shift +1, then tap Prime (16,8) while the steps are flashing. Paint Preview now reads Preview OFF and the footer says Pattern painted. The steps stay lit on the pattern grid, one step to the right of where Prime first put them: the shifted rhythm is painted into the pattern.

paint-shift-and-cancel.starting_state: A new empty project, stopped, with Record off. The Pattern editor has not been opened and pattern 1 has no trigs.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned. Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and pattern 2 has trigs on steps 1 and 2 (note C, velocity 100). The Merge modes screen is showing at 90 BPM with every merge mode at its default and playback stopped. The Patterns row reads 01 02: it only shows which patterns the channel plays, and turning E3 on it changes nothing. Assign patterns with the pattern slot buttons on the grid.

steps.title: Skip overlap
steps.caption: Press K2, turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Merge modes and press K3 to return to the Merge modes screen, then turn E2 down to Strategy, the trig merge. It reads SKIP, the default: a step plays only if exactly one pattern has a trig there. Steps 1 and 2 are in both patterns and drop out; only steps 3 and 4 remain.

steps.title: Hear Skip
steps.caption: Press Play at (1,8), then Stop. The loop plays only steps 3 and 4: MIDI 64 (velocity 107) and 65 (velocity 97), over and over.

steps.title: Keep overlap
steps.caption: Turn E3 up once: Strategy reads ONLY, with the footer ONLY APPLIED. (Turning E3 down first does nothing: SKIP is the lowest choice.) Only keeps steps that have a trig in more than one pattern, so steps 1 and 2 play and steps 3 and 4 drop out. The (14,8) button follows the choice.

steps.title: Play the union
steps.caption: Turn E3 up once more: Strategy reads ALL, footer ALL APPLIED. Every trig from either pattern plays. The change applies immediately; there is no K3 apply. The (14,8) button follows the choice.

steps.title: Hear All
steps.caption: Press Play, then Stop. All four steps sound: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 114, 109, 107, 97. Steps 1 and 2 are in both patterns, so their notes and velocities are averaged: C and C stay C, and (127 + 100) / 2 = 114.

steps.title: Open Note mode
steps.caption: Turn E2 down to Note mode, the pitch merge. It reads AVERAGE, the default. The screen's labels map to the manual's modes: UP is Higher, DOWN is Lower, and PAT 1 and PAT 2 take the note from that pattern.

steps.title: Turn through the note modes
steps.caption: Turn E3 up one detent at a time and watch Note mode: AVERAGE, then UP (Higher), DOWN (Lower), PAT 1, and finally PAT 2. At PAT 2 each step takes its note from pattern 2, which is C everywhere. The rhythm still comes from the ALL strategy.

steps.title: Hear Pattern 2 notes
steps.caption: Press Play, then Stop. The four steps still sound, now all at MIDI 60, pattern 2's note, with the same velocities (114, 109, 107, 97).

steps.title: Restore the average and hear it
steps.caption: Turn E3 down four detents: PAT 1, DOWN, UP, then AVERAGE (one more turn down stays on AVERAGE). Press Play, then Stop. The phrase is back to MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops eight steps: pattern 1 plays C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) on steps 1 to 4, and pattern 2 adds trigs on steps 5 and 7. Merge Shape has Foundation on with pattern 1 as the anchor, and Harmony Ensemble has an enabled group holding C, E and G. The Structure screen is open with Markers on Anchors, so each anchor note is a marker. Playback is stopped.

steps.title: Set Markers to Every 4
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent to the right of Anchors and press K3. Markers reads EVERY 4 and the footer says APPLIED: steps 1, 5, 9 and so on are the markers, whatever plays there.

steps.title: Markers 1 and 5 snap to the chord
steps.caption: Press Play, then Stop. Only the marker steps snap to the group, so look at the MIDI strip: step 1 plays 60 and step 5 plays 60 too, because its D snaps to C, while steps 2, 3 and 4 are no longer markers and keep their own notes 62, 64 and 65. Step 7 adds another 60. Each loop sounds 60, 62, 64, 65, 60, 60.

scale-save-d-and-apply.title: Save D major, then apply it

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The Scale editor is open on slot 1, C major, which is the applied scale and is lit brightly on grid row 3. Slots 2 and 3 keep their default settings and are not applied. The sequencer is stopped.

steps.title: Select slot 2 for editing
steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). The title row names slot 2 and its button lights dimly, while slot 1 stays bright: slot 2 is selected for editing but is not applied.

steps.title: Save D as the root
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3 to save. Slot 2 now holds D major, but it is still not applied.

steps.title: Hear that nothing changed
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then Stop. The phrase still plays C, D, E, F, because slot 1 is the applied scale and slot 2 is only being edited.

steps.title: Apply slot 2
steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). Its button lights brightly: it is now the applied scale.

steps.title: Hear D major
steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. The phrase plays D major: D, E, F#, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67), with the same rhythm and velocities.

scale-edit-versus-apply.title: Prepare a scale before applying it

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The Scale editor is open on slot 1, C major, which is the applied scale and is lit brightly on grid row 3. Slots 2 and 3 keep their default settings and are not applied. The sequencer is stopped.

steps.title: Select slot 2 for editing
steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). The title row names slot 2 and its button lights dimly, while slot 1 stays bright: slot 2 is selected for editing but is not applied.

steps.title: Save D as the root
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3 to save. Slot 2 now holds D major, but it is still not applied.

steps.title: Hear that nothing changed
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then Stop. The phrase still plays C, D, E, F, because slot 1 is the applied scale and slot 2 is only being edited.

steps.title: Apply slot 2
steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). Its button lights brightly: it is now the applied scale.

steps.title: Hear D major
steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. The phrase plays D major: D, E, F#, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67), with the same rhythm and velocities.

steps.title: Select slot 3 for editing
steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 at (3,3) for about one second. The editor switches to slot 3, which lights dimly, and slot 2 stays bright.

steps.title: Select the applied scale for editing
steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop: the phrase keeps playing in D major (62, 64, 66, 67), because selecting a slot for editing never changes what you hear. Now hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). Slot 2 is both the applied scale and the one being edited.

steps.title: Saving an applied scale changes the sound
steps.caption: Turn E3 two detents up so the root moves from D to E and press K3. Tap Play, then Stop. Saving a scale that playback is using changes it at once: the phrase now plays E major, MIDI 64, 66, 68, 69.

steps.title: Select slot 3 again
steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 at (3,3) for about one second. The editor moves to slot 3 and slot 2 is still the applied scale.

steps.title: Turn the global scale off
steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 again. A long press on the slot already selected for editing turns the global scale off: no slot button is lit and the editing selection clears. A short press on the applied slot does the same.

steps.title: Hear chromatic notes
steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. With no scale, pattern notes play as semitone steps from the root: C, C#, D, D# (MIDI 60, 61, 62, 63).

steps.title: Apply a scale again
steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). The scale returns with the edits you saved. Tap Play, then Stop: E major, MIDI 64, 66, 68, 69. Recap: a tap applies a slot; K1 plus a tap, or a one-second hold, selects a slot for editing without applying it; a second hold on the slot being edited turns the global scale off; saving with K3 changes the sound only if that slot is the applied one.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-note pattern. The song has one slot, Song 01, at the full global length of 64 steps, with Song mode AUTO, and the sequencer is stopped. The norns is showing the Pattern editor, left over from setup; it is not part of this lesson.

steps.title: Open the Song editor
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8). The Playback screen lists Playing SONG 01, Next SONG 01, Pass 1/1, Global length 64 and Song mode AUTO. The global length fader is on grid row 7: (1,7) subtracts one step, (8,7) adds one, and the buttons between jump to 1, 13, 32, 38, 51 and 64.

steps.title: Shorten by one step
steps.caption: Tap the fader's left end (1,7). It takes one step off the length and the Playback screen shows Global length 63. To loop a short fragment instead, jump with (2,7) to 1 step and add steps with (8,7); see the recipe on this page.

steps.title: Return to 64 steps
steps.caption: Tap the fader's right end (8,7), which adds one step. Global length reads 64 again, so the whole phrase plays.

steps.title: Set the length to 2 steps and play
steps.caption: Tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once to add one. Global length reads 2. Press Play (1,8): the song plays only its first two steps and starts again, so the MIDI sent in this step is C and D (60, 62) over and over, never E or F. Press Play again to stop.

steps.title: Set the length to 4 steps and play
steps.caption: Tap (8,7) twice. Global length reads 4. Press Play: the whole four-note phrase now plays before the song starts again, so the MIDI sent in this step is 60, 62, 64, 65. Press Play again to stop.

steps.title: Return to 64
steps.caption: Tap (7,7), the button that jumps to 64. Global length reads 64 again and the whole phrase is available to the song.

channel-routing-visible-scope.title: Each channel keeps its own device and rate

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Its Device page is open, so the header reads CH01, and Device shows CC Device, Mosaic's built-in generic MIDI device. Channel 2 is not set up yet. Both channels run at the default clock Rate /1 (one step per sixteenth note).

steps.title: An unused channel has no output
steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Device page stays open but now reads CH02 and Device shows None: channel 2 has no output yet, and setting up channel 1 did not change it. The channel buttons choose which channel the screen edits.

steps.title: Return to channel 1
steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). The header returns to CH01 and Device shows CC Device again: each channel keeps its own device.

steps.title: Open the Clock page
steps.caption: Device was the first of a channel's own settings; Rate is the second. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3. The Clock page for CH01 shows Rate /1, the default: one step per sixteenth note. Rate divides the clock, so /2 will run half as fast and make each step twice as long.

steps.title: Select channel 2
steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Clock page stays open and now reads CH02, with its own Rate /1.

steps.title: Give channel 2 a different rate
steps.caption: Turn E3 down two detents to Rate /2 and press K3 to apply. Channel 2 now runs at half the speed of channel 1: each of its steps lasts two sixteenth notes.

steps.title: Channel 1 keeps its rate
steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). Its Clock page still reads Rate /1: changing channel 2's rate left channel 1 alone.

steps.title: Channel 2 remembers its rate
steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1) again. Its Clock page reads Rate /2. Each channel remembers its own settings, so channels can run at different speeds against one tempo.

steps.title: Hear channel 2 at half speed
steps.caption: Open the Device page for channel 2, give it its own MIDI output, give it pattern 1 with the range steps 1-4 and open its Clock page again. Select channel 1 and press Play. Channel 1 plays one note every sixteenth note; channel 2 plays one note every two sixteenth notes, so its notes are twice as far apart. Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", where the second port's notes arrive at half the pace of the first. Press Play again to stop.

pattern-note-range.title: Shape notes across the grid range

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Note the range buttons on row 8 are range-up (14,8), centre (15,8) and range-down (16,8). A press moves the window one degree up or down, a long press jumps to the top or bottom, and the centre button returns to the root page. Pattern Velocity has only two range buttons, (15,8) toward the top page and (16,8) toward the lower page, as the next lesson shows.

steps.title: Choose a scale degree
steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) twice to open Pattern Note for pattern 1. The seven rows are scale degrees, with the root on the bottom row. Tap (4,1), the top row of step 4's column. Press Play at (1,8), then Stop: step 4 now plays degree 6, MIDI 71, while steps 1-3 stay 60, 62, 64.

steps.title: Move the range up twice
steps.caption: Tap range-up (14,8), then tap (4,1): step 4 is now MIDI 72, the next C. Play to check, then Stop. Tap range-up once more, then tap (4,1): step 4 is MIDI 74. Play to check, then Stop.

steps.title: Move the range down twice
steps.caption: Tap range-down (16,8): the window moves down one degree. Tap (4,1): step 4 is MIDI 72 again. Play, then Stop. Tap range-down once more, then tap (4,1): step 4 is back to MIDI 71. Play, then Stop.

steps.title: Jump to the top, which is a limit
steps.caption: Hold range-up (14,8) for about a second: the window jumps to its highest position. Tap (4,1): step 4 plays MIDI 83. Tap range-up again: the window cannot go higher, so (4,1) still plays MIDI 83.

steps.title: Jump to the bottom, which is a limit
steps.caption: Hold range-down (16,8) for about a second: the window jumps to its lowest position. Tap (4,7), the bottom row: step 4 plays MIDI 48. Tap range-down again: the window cannot go lower, so (4,7) still plays MIDI 48.

steps.title: Return to the central range
steps.caption: Tap the centre button at (15,8): the window returns to the root page, with the root on the bottom row. Tap (4,4), degree 3: step 4 plays MIDI 65 and the original phrase 60, 62, 64, 65 is back.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Velocity the range buttons on row 8 differ from Pattern Note, which has three: here there are two, range-up at (15,8), toward the 127-68 page, and range-down at (16,8), toward the 58-0 page.

steps.title: Make a strong accent
steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) three times to open Pattern Velocity. Each row of a step's column is a velocity level, 127 at the top. Tap (4,1). Press Play at (1,8), then Stop: step 4 plays at velocity 127 while steps 1-3 keep 127, 117, 107.

steps.title: Walk down the velocity column
steps.caption: Tap down the column of step 4 and press Play, then Stop, after each tap: (4,2) is 117, (4,3) 107, (4,4) 97, (4,5) 87, (4,6) 78 and (4,7) 68. At (4,7) step 4 plays at 68; the other steps are unchanged.

steps.title: Move the velocity range
steps.caption: Tap range-down (16,8): the window moves down one level. Tap (4,1): step 4 plays at 117, the level that was second from the top. Play, then Stop. Tap range-down again and tap (4,1): 107. Then tap range-up (15,8) to move the window up one level and tap (4,1): 117 again.

steps.title: Jump to the lower page
steps.caption: Hold range-down (16,8) for about a second: the window jumps to the lower page, 58 at the top down to 0 at the bottom. Tap (4,1): step 4 plays at 58.

steps.title: Go quieter
steps.caption: Tap down the column of step 4 to (4,4), playing after each tap: (4,2) is 48, (4,3) 39 and (4,4) 29. At (4,4) step 4 plays at velocity 29.

steps.title: Almost silent
steps.caption: Tap down to (4,5) and (4,6), playing after each tap: (4,5) is 19 and (4,6) is 9. At velocity 9 step 4 still sounds, only very softly: all four notes are in the MIDI strip.

steps.title: Turn an attack into a rest
steps.caption: Tap (4,7), velocity 0, and play. Step 4 is silent: the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", shows only three notes, 60, 62 and 64. A velocity of 0 turns the attack into a rest.

steps.title: Restore full velocity
steps.caption: Tap range-down (16,8) again: the window is already at its lowest page, so (4,7) is still velocity 0 and step 4 stays silent. Then hold range-up (15,8) for about a second: the window jumps back to the top page, 127 down to 68. Tap (4,1): step 4 plays again at velocity 127.

pattern-copy-groups.title: Copy notes and dynamics across the four step pages

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). A pattern has four step pages of 16 steps; here only page 1 has trigs and the Pattern editor has not been opened. Each channel plays a range of steps (start step to end step), which you will set at the end to hear one page at a time.

steps.title: Add trigs on pages 2 to 4
steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) to open Pattern Trig and tap steps 17-20, 33-36 and 49-52 (grid rows 5-7, columns 1-4) so each step page holds four steps. All twelve steps light.

steps.title: Hold K1 and set the first note
steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) again to open Pattern Note. Hold K1 and tap (1,7), the root, C: degree 0 for step 1. The cell lights.

steps.title: Set the other three notes
steps.caption: Keep K1 held and tap (2,6), (3,5) and (4,4): degrees 1, 2 and 3, which are D, E and F. All four notes are lit.

steps.title: Check page 1
steps.caption: Press the first page button (9,8): the four notes are lit on page 1.

steps.title: Check pages 2 to 4
steps.caption: Press the page buttons (10,8), (11,8) and (12,8) in turn. Each page shows the same four notes lit. Holding K1 while you entered them copied each note to all four pages.

steps.title: Copy the dynamics to every page
steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) again to open Pattern Velocity. Hold K1 and tap (1,2), (2,2), (3,2) and (4,2): the second level, velocity 117, on steps 1-4. Press the first page button (9,8): the four cells are lit on page 1.

steps.title: Check velocity pages 2 to 4
steps.caption: Press the page buttons (10,8), (11,8) and (12,8) in turn: the same four cells are lit on every page.

steps.title: Hear page 1
steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8). Hold step 1 and tap step 4 to set the channel range to steps 1-4. Press Play at (1,8), then Stop: C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65), each at velocity 117.

steps.title: Hear pages 2 and 3
steps.caption: Hold step 17 and tap step 20 to move the range to steps 17-20. Play, then Stop. Then hold step 33 and tap step 36, play and stop again. Both pages play the same four notes at velocity 117.

steps.title: Hear page 4
steps.caption: Hold step 49 and tap step 52. Play, then Stop: page 4 plays C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocity 117 too, so every page matches.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major, stopped. Clock Rate is /1 and no Swing or Shuffle is set. Channel 1 is selected and its Clock page is open. Your goal is to give channel 1 its own shuffle feel. Rate is the first row of a vertical list.

steps.title: Read the Clock settings together
steps.caption: Turn E2 left until Rate is selected, the first row (it reads /1, the default). The list shows Rate, Feel source and Swing type together, so you can read the channel's clock and feel settings at a glance.

steps.title: Select Swing type
steps.caption: Tap K1 twice: the first tap opens the norns menu and the second closes it, and the page keeps your place. Turn E2 to Swing type. It reads X: this channel has no feel of its own yet.

steps.title: Follow the global feel
steps.caption: Turn E3 left as far as it goes and press K3. It stays at X. X means this channel follows the global feel set in Song > Tempo and feel.

steps.title: Choose Shuffle
steps.caption: Turn E3 right to Shuffle and press K3. Shuffle adds its own rows below Swing type for setting this channel's feel.

steps.title: Reach the end of the list
steps.caption: Keep turning E2 right. The list stops on its last row, Shuffle amount (0), and does not wrap round however far you turn.

workflow-compose-two-channels.title: Compose two channels and chain song slots

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Nothing else exists yet: no second pattern, no scale change, no second channel and one song slot. Trig merge modes decide what happens when two patterns on one channel both have a trig on a step: Skip (the default) drops those steps, Only keeps only those steps, and All keeps every step.

steps.title: Build pattern 2 and hear Skip
steps.caption: Do these in order. 1) Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1 and 3 on Pattern Trig. 2) Tap Pattern (5,8) again for Pattern Note and raise step 1 to (1,3) and step 3 to (3,1): degrees 4 and 6. 3) Tap Scale (4,8), tap slot 2 at (2,3), turn E2 to Root and E3 two detents up to D, then press K3: D major is applied. 4) Tap Channel (3,8) and tap pattern slot (2,2) to assign pattern 2 to channel 1 beside pattern 1. 5) Press Play, then Stop. Skip drops steps 1 and 3, where both patterns have a trig, so only steps 2 and 4 play: E and G of D major (MIDI 64 and 67) at velocities 117 and 97.

steps.title: Move the trig merge to All
steps.caption: Tap the trig merge button (14,8) twice to move from Skip through Only to All. The button lights at medium brightness.

steps.title: Merge all, with pattern 1 velocities
steps.caption: Hold the velocity merge button (16,8) and tap pattern 1 at (1,2) to take velocities from pattern 1, then press Play and Stop. All four steps play. Steps 2 and 4 come from pattern 1 alone (E and G, 64 and 67). Steps 1 and 3 have a trig in both patterns, so their notes are the average of the two patterns' scale degrees: step 1 averages D (degree 0) and A (degree 4) to F# (66), and step 3 averages F# and C# to A (69). The result is MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97.

steps.title: Select channel 2
steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device and press K3. The Device page now reads CH02.

steps.title: Route channel 2 and open its Masks
steps.caption: On the Device page choose the same device on MIDI port 2 and MIDI channel 2 (turn E3 or E2 to each setting) and press K3 to apply. Tap pattern slot (2,2) for pattern 2, hold step 1 and tap step 4 to give channel 2 the range steps 1-4, then turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Masks and press K3. The screen reads Note Masks for CH02.

steps.title: Add a keyboard note to channel 2
steps.caption: On Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 76 at velocity 90 on a MIDI keyboard or controller to lock it to that step. Tap channel 1 at (1,1) and press Play, then Stop. Both channels sound, each on its own port: channel 1 plays 66, 64, 69, 67 as before, and channel 2 plays pattern 2: MIDI 69 (A) on step 1 and your 76 on step 3.

steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2 an octave up
steps.caption: Do these in order. 1) Tap Song (6,8) and set the global length to 4 steps: tap (2,7), which sets 1, then (8,7) three times. 2) Copy slot 1 to slot 2: hold slot (1,1) and tap (2,1), then tap (2,1) to select slot 2. 3) Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave-up (11,8), so slot 2 plays an octave higher. 4) Tap Song (6,8), select slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play. The four-step phrase plays, then repeats an octave higher in slot 2: MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67, then 78, 76, 81, 79 on channel 1, while channel 2 plays its A and 76 in both slots.

workflow-patterns-and-scale.title: Add a second pattern in D major

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Nothing else exists yet: no second pattern, no scale change and no second channel.

steps.title: Add trigs to pattern 2
steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) to open Pattern Trig, choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1 and 3. Both steps light on the grid.

steps.title: Raise their notes
steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) again for Pattern Note. Raise step 1 to the cell (1,4) and step 3 to (3,6): these are the scale degrees 4 and 6 that pattern 2 plays on those steps. Both cells light.

steps.title: Apply D major
steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) and tap slot 2 at (2,3). Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3. The Scale screen names slot 2 and D major is applied.

steps.title: Give pattern 2 to channel 1
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8) and tap pattern slot (2,2). Pattern 2 now plays on channel 1 beside pattern 1, and both slot buttons are lit.

steps.title: Hear Skip
steps.caption: Press Play, then Stop. By default overlapping trigs are skipped, so steps 1 and 3, where both patterns have a trig, drop out. Only steps 2 and 4 play: look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", for E and G of D major, MIDI 64 and 67, at velocities 117 and 97.

workflow-second-channel.title: Add a second channel with its own output

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 has patterns 1 and 2 merged in All mode with pattern 1's velocities, in D major. All four steps play: MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. Channel 2 is not set up yet.

steps.title: Select channel 2
steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device and press K3. The Device page now reads CH02.

steps.title: Route channel 2
steps.caption: On the Device page choose the same device on MIDI port 2 and MIDI channel 2 (turn E3 or E2 to each setting) and press K3 to apply. Tap pattern slot (2,2) for pattern 2, then hold step 1 and tap step 4 to give channel 2 the range steps 1-4. Assigning the pattern brings up Merge modes for CH02 with Patterns 02, and the pattern slot (2,2) stays lit.

steps.title: Open its Masks
steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. The screen reads Note Masks for CH02.

steps.title: Add a keyboard note to channel 2
steps.caption: On Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 76 at velocity 90 on a MIDI keyboard or controller to lock it to that step. Tap channel 1 at (1,1) and press Play, then Stop. Both channels sound, each on its own port, in the MIDI strip: channel 1 plays 66, 64, 69, 67 as before, and channel 2 plays pattern 2, MIDI 69 (A) on step 1 and your 76 on step 3.

workflow-song-chain.title: Chain song slots an octave apart

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Both channels play four steps. Channel 1 plays 66, 64, 69, 67 and channel 2 plays its A (69) and 76. The song has one slot, Song 01, at the full global length of 64 steps.

steps.title: Set the song length to 4
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8). Tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) three times. The Playback screen reads Global length 4: the song is one four-step phrase.

steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2
steps.caption: Hold slot (1,1) and tap (2,1) to copy slot 1 into slot 2, then tap (2,1) to select slot 2. The Slot setup screen names Song 02 and the footer reads Song sequence 2 selected.

steps.title: Raise slot 2 an octave
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). The octave button lights and the footer reads Ch. 1 octave: 1: channel 1 will play one octave higher in this slot.

steps.title: Hear the chain
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play, then Stop. The four-step phrase plays, then repeats an octave higher in slot 2. The MIDI strip shows 66, 64, 69, 67, then 78, 76, 81, 79 on channel 1, while channel 2 plays its A and 76 in both slots.

song-copy-and-compare.title: Copy a slot, then change the copy

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: A fresh session with Song mode On, its default. Channel 1 plays its default phrase through the test device and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1; nothing is playing. The song has one slot, Song 01.

steps.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2
steps.caption: Open the Song editor with Song (6,8) and set a global length of 2 steps: tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once. Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, then tap slot 2. The Slot setup screen names Song 02 and the footer reads Song sequence 2 selected: slot 2 is selected and holds the same two-note motif as slot 1.

steps.title: Raise the copy an octave
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). The octave button lights and the footer reads Ch. 1 octave: 1. Slot 2 now plays the motif an octave higher than slot 1, and slot 1 is unchanged: each song slot keeps its own octave.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: A fresh session with Song mode On, its default. Channel 1 plays its default phrase through the test device and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1; nothing is playing. You will build a two-note motif (MIDI 60, 62) copied into slots 1, 2, 4 and 5, with slots 3 and 6 left empty.

steps.title: Set the global length to 2
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once. The Playback screen reads Global length 2, so every slot plays a two-note motif, 60 and 62.

steps.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2
steps.caption: Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, then tap slot 2. The Slot setup screen names Song 02 and the footer reads Song sequence 2 selected.

steps.title: Raise slot 2 an octave
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). The footer reads Ch. 1 octave: 1 and slot 2 will sound 72 and 74.

steps.title: Add slots 4 and 5
steps.caption: Repeat for slot 4, leaving slot 3 empty: copy slot 1 into slot 4 and give it octave +2 at (12,8). Then copy slot 1 into slot 5 and give it octave -1 at (9,8). Slots 3 and 6 stay empty, so there are two groups: slots 1 and 2, and slots 4 and 5.

steps.title: Hear the first group loop
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 sounds 60, 62, then slot 2 sounds 72, 74. Slot 3 is empty, so the group ends and playback returns to slot 1: look at the MIDI strip for 60, 62, 72, 74, 60, 62, 72, 74. Press Stop.

course_summary: Keep one project from four notes to a saved two-section arrangement.

project.name: Four notes
project.output: One MIDI instrument or Polyperc1; an independent MIDI channel or Doubledecker for the second part. Polyperc1 is used once.
project.incoming_state: Fresh project. Do not load separate reference-example projects during the course.

learning_path.title: 1. Meet Mosaic
learning_path.goal: Learn what a pattern, a channel and a song slot each do, and how this manual names grid buttons and norns controls, before you change anything.
learning_path.prerequisite: Mosaic is running on norns with a 128 grid connected. Start a new project (PARAMS > MOSAIC > + New) so the course begins from an empty project. Have a MIDI instrument, or a norns voice such as Polyperc 1, ready for chapter 2.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Nothing in the project has changed. You can find a grid button from its (column,row) coordinates, tell the norns keys K1-K3 from the encoders E1-E3, and say what a pattern, a channel and a song slot do.
learning_path.recovery: If a tap opens the wrong page, tap Channel (3,8) to return to the channel page. If the grid does not respond, check the grid connection in the norns menu. If playback later makes no sound, open No Sound.

stages.title: Learn the three objects
stages.goal: Know what a pattern, a channel and a song slot are for before you edit any of them.
stages.action:
Read these three ideas first. Nothing changes until the last line.
1. A pattern holds a rhythm of trigs (steps that play a note) and relative notes. You write patterns on the Pattern page.
2. A channel plays patterns through one sound: a MIDI instrument or a norns voice. Its masks are values that override pitch, velocity and length, for the whole channel or for single steps.
3. A song slot stores one section of the song. You arrange slots in chapter 9.
Then do one thing: tap Channel (3,8) on the grid to open channel 1.
stages.result: The norns screen reads NOTE MASKS with CH01 in the title row. Its eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4) all show X, which means no value is set: the new channel has no pattern, pitch or sound yet. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because channel 1 is the channel you edit, and (3,8) is lit because you are on the Channel page. In chapter 3 you give channel 1 a pattern and a pitch.

stages.title: Read the grid and norns controls
stages.goal: Be able to find any button from its coordinates for the rest of the course.
stages.action:
1. A grid position is written (column,row). Columns count from 1 at the left to 16 at the right; rows count from 1 at the top to 8 at the bottom. (3,8) is column 3 on the bottom row.
2. The bottom-left buttons open the main pages: Play (1,8), Record (2,8), Channel (3,8), Scale (4,8), Pattern (5,8) and Song (6,8). Row 1 selects the channel on the channel page, the pattern on the Pattern page and the song slot on the Song page.
3. On the norns, K1-K3 are the three keys and E1-E3 the three encoders, numbered as printed on the norns. "Tap" means a short press. "Hold K1" means keep K1 down while you act: it is the shift key.
4. Tap Pattern (5,8) on the grid to try a button. Chapter 2 starts by tapping Channel (3,8), so you can leave the Pattern page that way.
stages.result: The screen changes to PATTERN TRIG with PAT01 CH01 in the title row. No trigs are set yet, so the steps are dim. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because pattern 1 is the pattern you edit, and (5,8) is lit because you are on the Pattern page.

learning_path.title: 2. Choose one sound
learning_path.goal: Send channel 1 to one instrument you can hear, and set a known tempo of 90 BPM.
learning_path.prerequisite: New project, transport stopped, Record off. A MIDI instrument is connected and set to receive on a MIDI channel you know, or Polyperc 1 is enabled for norns. Switch it on and set its volume before you start.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Channel 1 routes to your instrument or to Polyperc 1; the tempo is 90 BPM; no pattern is assigned yet, so nothing plays.
learning_path.recovery: If the Device page does not offer your instrument, check the connection, the MIDI port and the enabled norns voices before changing notes. K2, or E1, cancels a draft without changing the active output.

stages.title: Open the Device page
stages.goal: Reach the page where a channel is given its sound.
stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8). Channel 1 is selected (CH01 in the title row).
2. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens. This list holds everything you can do with the channel: Masks, Trig params, Output, Clock, Merge modes, Merge Shape, Harmony, Device and History.
3. Turn E2 until Device is highlighted.
4. Press K3 to open it.
stages.result: The title row reads DEVICE with CH01. Only the Device row is listed, set to None: the MIDI channel and MIDI port rows appear once you choose a device. What you change here is only a draft until you press K3.

stages.title: Choose the output and apply it
stages.goal: Make channel 1 play your instrument.
stages.action:
1. Turn E3 one detent to choose a Device. The first entry after None is CC Device, a generic MIDI device that suits any MIDI instrument. If your instrument has its own entry, choose that instead. With no external instrument, choose Polyperc 1, the norns voice.
2. The MIDI channel and MIDI port rows now appear. CC Device reads CC1 and OUT 1, so notes leave on port 1, MIDI channel 1. If your instrument listens elsewhere, turn E2 to a row and E3 to the value it needs. A device entry that fixes a value does not let you change it, and Polyperc 1 needs neither row.
3. Press K3 to apply. Until K3 the page only shows a draft and the channel keeps its old routing; K2 cancels the draft.
stages.result: The DEVICE page lists Device CC Device, MIDI channel CC1 and MIDI port OUT 1 (or your own choices), and the routing is now active for channel 1. You hear it in chapter 3 when the first notes play. If it stays silent, open No Sound.

stages.title: Set the tempo to 90 BPM
stages.goal: Fix a known tempo so every timing in later chapters is exact: at 90 BPM a beat is 2/3 s. If you prefer another tempo, keep it and scale the times.
stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8).
2. Turn E1 right one detent to open Song tasks, turn E2 to Tempo & feel and press K3. GLOBAL FEEL opens.
3. Turn E2 up to Tempo, the top row. Turn E3 left until Tempo reads 90. Tempo follows the norns clock, so it shows whatever your norns is set to (often 120 on a fresh norns; this walkthrough's recording opens at 90). It moves one BPM per detent with no coarse step: keep turning E3 until the screen reads 90.
4. Press K3 to apply.
stages.result: The GLOBAL FEEL page for SONG 01 shows Tempo 90. At 90 BPM a beat lasts 2/3 s. A channel's default Rate, /1, makes each step a sixteenth note, so each step lasts 1/6 s; four steps make one beat.

learning_path.title: 3. Make four equal notes
learning_path.goal: Write four trigs, give them a pitch and hear them repeat as a very fast four-note loop.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue with the routed project from chapter 2: tempo 90, channel 1 routed to your instrument, transport stopped.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1-4; channel 1 plays pattern 1 over steps 1-4; its masks are Note 60 (C3), Vel 80 and Len 1/2; no step has its own mask; playback is stopped.
learning_path.recovery: If you hear nothing, check in this order: Play (1,8) was tapped; pattern 1 is lit on row 2 of the channel page; steps 1-4 are lit on row 4; Note, Vel and Len are set in Masks; the Device page from chapter 2 was applied with K3. If Play will not stop because Shift press stop is on (PARAMS > MOSAIC > sequencer options), hold K1 while you tap Play.

stages.title: Enter four trigs
stages.goal: Write a first rhythm. A trig is a step that will play a note. Four neighbouring trigs are deliberately plain; chapter 4 reshapes them.
stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8). The screen reads PATTERN TRIG.
2. Tap (1,1) on the top row to choose pattern 1. PAT01 appears in the title row.
3. Tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Row 4 holds steps 1 to 16 of the pattern. Each tap switches one step on; tap a lit step again to remove it.
stages.result: Four bright buttons light at (1,4) to (4,4), and PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows four bright trigs. Nothing sounds yet: the pattern is not assigned to a channel and no pitch is set.

stages.title: Assign pattern 1 and loop four steps
stages.goal: Connect the pattern to channel 1 and make the channel repeat steps 1 to 4 only.
stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8). Channel 1 is selected on row 1.
2. Tap (1,2), the first pattern slot on row 2. It lights: channel 1 now plays pattern 1. The screen opens MERGE MODES for CH01 because assigning a pattern always shows it; Patterns reads 01. You do not need the other rows yet.
3. Row 4 of the channel page is the range row: it sets which steps the channel loops. Hold (1,4), tap (4,4), then release (1,4). Steps 1 to 4 stay bright and the other steps go dark, so the channel loops four steps. A short loop keeps the first sound easy to hear; chapter 4 widens it.
stages.result: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 and repeats steps 1 to 4. The grid shows (1,2) lit and steps 1 to 4 bright on row 4, and the tooltip reads Channel 1 length changed.

stages.title: Open the Masks page
stages.goal: Find where a channel's pitch, velocity and length are set.
stages.action:
1. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens.
2. Turn E2 to Masks and press K3. The title reads NOTE MASKS with CH01.
3. A mask is a value that overrides what the pattern would use. With no step held, E2 chooses a cell and E3 sets that cell for every step of the channel.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 lists eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4). They all read X, which means no mask is set, so the channel has no pitch, velocity or length yet.

stages.title: Set pitch, velocity and length
stages.goal: Give all four trigs the same note, loudness and duration with the channel's mask defaults.
stages.action:
1. With no step held, turn E2 to Note and turn E3 right until Note reads C3 (MIDI 60; norns labels MIDI note 60 as C3). It starts at X, so expect about 60 detents; turn until the screen shows C3.
2. Turn E2 to Vel and turn E3 right until Vel reads 80 (about 80 detents from X).
3. Turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until Len reads 1/2, a note half a step long (8 detents).
stages.result: NOTE MASKS shows Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2. All four trigs use these values: a medium-loud, short note. You do not need to count detents; turn until the screen shows the value.

stages.title: Play the loop
stages.goal: Hear the four trigs repeat.
stages.action:
1. Tap Play (1,8).
2. Listen for about two repeats. Four identical notes, C3 at velocity 80, follow each other 1/6 s apart and the pattern restarts every 2/3 s, so you hear a fast stutter rather than a tune. The MIDI strip under the step lists the notes.
3. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.result: Four equal C notes repeat, then stop with no note left sounding. The strip shows note 60 at velocity 80, about 167 ms apart. The stutter confirms that pattern, channel, masks and output all work. Chapter 4 spreads these four trigs out so each one lands on a beat.

learning_path.title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar
learning_path.goal: Turn the four fast trigs into four evenly spaced beats by stretching the loop to 16 steps.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 3, stopped. Note 60, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 stay set.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13; channel 1 plays steps 1-16; Rate is /1, the default sixteenth-note rate (1/6 s per step at 90 BPM); Note 60, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 are unchanged; playback is stopped.
learning_path.recovery: Remove an accidental trig by tapping it again in Pattern Trig. If the loop still repeats after four steps, hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4) again on the channel page.

stages.title: Loop all 16 steps
stages.goal: Make the channel play a whole bar before it repeats.
stages.action:
1. If you are not on the channel page, tap Channel (3,8).
2. Set the range, the loop length, on row 4: hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4). This is a range gesture, not a trig tap. The range is now steps 1 to 16: one bar of sixteenth notes, 16 x 1/6 s = 2.7 s. Steps 5 to 16 now glow dimly because they are inside the loop.
3. Open the Clock page: turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Clock and press K3.
stages.result: The grid shows the 16-step range on row 4 (dim pads inside the loop, bright trigs on steps 1 to 4) and the screen opens CLOCK for CH01. The trigs stay on steps 1 to 4 until the stage after next.

stages.title: Check the clock rate
stages.goal: Confirm that a step is a sixteenth note, so the timings in this course hold.
stages.action:
1. Turn E2 up to Rate, the top row, if it is not highlighted.
2. Check that it reads /1, the default rate (one step per sixteenth note). If it shows something else, turn E3 to /1.
3. Press K3 to apply.
stages.result: The CLOCK page shows Rate /1 for CH01, so a step lasts 1/6 s at 90 BPM and the channel plays 16 steps before it repeats. This check changes nothing when the rate is already /1.

stages.title: Move the trigs onto the beats
stages.goal: Space the four trigs one beat apart.
stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8). The screen reads PATTERN TRIG and pattern 1 is still chosen.
2. Tap (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4) to remove those trigs. Step n is column n of row 4.
3. Tap (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4) to add trigs. Keep (1,4).
stages.result: Row 4 shows trigs at (1,4), (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4). Four steps lie between trigs, which is one beat at 90 BPM, so the trigs fall on beats 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the bar.

stages.title: Open Masks for chapter 5
stages.goal: Leave the Masks page open, so the next chapter starts where it needs to.
stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8).
