2. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Masks and press K3.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 as before, and row 4 of the grid shows the four trigs one beat apart inside the 16-step range.

stages.title: Hear the wider phrase
stages.goal: Hear the same note spread across a bar.
stages.action:
1. Tap Play (1,8) and listen for two passes of the 16-step phrase, about 5.3 s.
2. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.result: C3 sounds once per beat, 2/3 s apart, over four beats and then repeats; the MIDI strip lists the note-ons about 667 ms apart. Compare it with the stutter of chapter 3: the pitch is the same, only the spacing changed.

learning_path.title: 5. Give the phrase an ending
learning_path.goal: Change only the last note of the phrase, without rewriting the rhythm, by giving step 13 its own mask. Chapter 7 removes the channel Note mask again so the scale can move the pitch; this chapter shows how masks override the pattern and how to undo them.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 4: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13, range 16; Note 60, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 are the channel defaults; stopped.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Same rhythm. Step 13 has Note 62 (D3) and Vel 50; the channel defaults are still Note 60, Vel 80 and Len 1/2; no other step has a mask; stopped.
learning_path.recovery: If every note changes, you edited the channel default: release all steps and check that the title row shows ST13 while you edit. To remove a step's masks, hold the step and press K2; this clears Note and Vel together, so set them again.

stages.title: Find the channel default
stages.goal: See the value every step uses before any step has an exception, so you can tell later what an exception changes.
stages.action:
1. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Masks and press K3 if you are not already on this page from chapter 4.
2. With no step held, turn E2 to Note.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3 (MIDI 60) in the highlighted cell. The title row has no step number, so C3 is the default for the whole channel. A step mask will override it for one step only.

stages.title: Select the last beat
stages.goal: Choose the one step you will change.
stages.action: Hold (13,4), the fourth trig, and keep holding it for the next stage.
stages.result: The title row now reads CH01 ST13: the screen edits step 13 only. Note still reads C3 because step 13 has no exception yet.

stages.title: Raise the last note
stages.goal: Give step 13 a pitch of its own.
stages.action: While you hold (13,4), turn E3 right two detents. Note moves by one semitone per detent, 60 to 61 to 62, and reads D3 (MIDI 62).
stages.result: Only step 13 now has a Note exception, D3. Steps 1, 5 and 9 still use the channel default C3.

stages.title: Return to the default view
stages.goal: Leave step 13 and see that its exception is kept.
stages.action:
Release (13,4).
To check that the exception is still there, hold (13,4) again: the title row shows ST13 and Note reads D3. Release it again.
stages.result: The title row loses ST13 and Note shows the channel default, C3, again. Step 13 still holds D3; you hear it in the next stage.

stages.title: Hear the new ending
stages.goal: Hear the exception on the beat it belongs to.
stages.action:
1. Tap Play (1,8) and listen for two passes, about 5.3 s.
2. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.result: You hear C, C, C, D: three beats of C3, then the fourth beat a whole tone higher. The MIDI strip shows notes 60, 60, 60 and 62, all at velocity 80, one beat apart. The rhythm and the other notes are unchanged.

stages.title: Make the ending softer
stages.goal: Give step 13 its own velocity as well.
stages.action:
1. With no step held, turn E2 to Vel. It reads 80, the default.
2. Hold (13,4). The title row shows ST13, and Vel reads 80 because step 13 has no velocity exception yet. Turn E3 left 30 detents until Vel reads 50, then release (13,4).
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.result: While you hold step 13 the screen shows its own Vel 50; after you release it shows the channel default Vel 80 again. The last D sounds quieter: the MIDI strip shows velocity 50 for note 62 against 80 for the others. The pitches and the timing do not change.

stages.title: Change the default, not the exception
stages.goal: See what a step mask protects.
stages.action:
1. With no step held, turn E2 to Note. Turn E3 right seven detents to G3 (MIDI 67).
2. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop. You hear G, G, G, D: the three steps without a Note mask follow the new default and step 13 keeps its own D.
stages.result: The ending note stayed D while the other three moved to G, so a step mask overrides the channel default. The MIDI strip shows 67, 67, 67 and 62 (velocity 50).

stages.title: Restore the default
stages.goal: Put the channel default back to C3.
stages.action:
1. Turn E3 left seven detents to return Note to C3 (MIDI 60).
2. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.result: With the default back at C3, the phrase is C, C, C, D again, with step 13 still at velocity 50.

stages.title: Clear a step's masks with K2
stages.goal: Learn the undo for step masks, using the ending you just built. The next stage rebuilds it.
stages.action:
K2 on a held step clears every mask on that step, Note and Vel together; the channel defaults are not touched.
1. Hold (13,4).
2. Press K2.
3. Release (13,4).
4. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.result: You hear C, C, C, C, all at velocity 80: step 13 uses the channel defaults again, so K2 removed both the Note and the Vel exception. The screen still shows Note C3 and Vel 80, because K2 left the defaults alone.

stages.title: Rebuild the ending
stages.goal: Put back D3 at velocity 50 for the rest of the course, using the two edits you already know.
stages.action:
1. With no step held, turn E2 to Note. Hold (13,4), turn E3 right two detents to D3 and release (13,4).
2. Turn E2 to Vel. Hold (13,4), turn E3 left 30 detents to 50 and release (13,4).
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.result: The phrase is C, C, C, D again with a softer last note (62 at velocity 50 in the MIDI strip). This is the phrase the next chapters build on.

learning_path.title: 6. Add a second part
learning_path.goal: Add a second channel that plays a root-and-fifth bass beneath the phrase.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 5, stopped. You need a second output: another MIDI port or MIDI channel, or Doubledecker. Do not give Polyperc 1 to both channels.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Channel 1 still plays C, C, C, D. Channel 2 plays pattern 2 (trigs on steps 1 and 9, degrees 0 and 4) over 16 steps at octave -1, with no masks, so it sounds MIDI 48 and 55 at velocity 100 and length 1. If you tried the optional merge detour, channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone again and its merge Strategy is left on All.
learning_path.recovery: If the first part changes, select channel 1 and check its Device page and masks: selecting channel 2 does not change channel 1. If channel 2 repeats too fast, set its range to 16 steps again.

stages.title: Write a root-and-fifth bass pattern
stages.goal: Write pattern 2: two trigs, one on the root of the scale and one on the fifth.
stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8) until the screen reads PATTERN TRIG. Tap (2,1) on the top row to choose pattern 2 (PAT02). It starts empty.
2. Tap (1,4) and (9,4): two trigs, half a bar apart.
3. Tap Pattern (5,8) once more. The screen reads PATTERN NOTE. Here row 7, the bottom row of notes, is degree 0, the root of the scale, and each row above it is one scale step higher. The bright band along row 7 is the degree 0 baseline every step starts on.
4. Tap (1,7) for degree 0 at step 1 and (9,3) for degree 4, the fifth, at step 9.
Pattern notes are relative: the scale decides the real pitch. The title still says CH01 because channel 1 is selected; pattern 2 is not assigned to anything yet.
stages.result: PATTERN NOTE PAT02 shows the tooltip Step 9 note set to 4, with a pad at (9,3); the root stays on the row 7 baseline at step 1. The extra pad at (13,6) is not one of yours and does not play, because pattern 2 has no trig on step 13. In C major your two notes will sound as C and G.

stages.title: Open channel 2's Device page
stages.goal: Reach the page where channel 2 is given its own sound.
stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8), then tap (2,1) to select channel 2 (CH02).
2. As in chapter 2: turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Device and press K3.
stages.result: The title row reads DEVICE with CH02. Channel 2 has its own Device row: choose an output that differs from channel 1's in the next stage.

stages.title: Route channel 2 and set its octave
stages.goal: Give the bass its own sound, pattern, loop length and register.
stages.action:
1. Choose a second output that differs from channel 1's. Turn E3 one detent to choose CC Device, turn E2 down to MIDI channel and E3 one detent to CC2, turn E2 down to MIDI port and E3 one detent to OUT 2. Any other port or MIDI channel works for your own instrument, and Doubledecker is another choice. Do not give Polyperc 1 to both channels. Press K3 to apply.
2. Tap (2,2) to assign pattern 2 to channel 2. Row 2 should show only (2,2) lit for CH02; if another pattern slot is lit, tap it to remove it.
3. Set the range so channel 2 loops the same 16 steps as channel 1: hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4). This is a range gesture on row 4, not a trig tap.
4. Tap (9,8) to set the channel octave to -1. The octave buttons run from -2 at (8,8) to +2 at (12,8); (10,8) is 0.
stages.result: The screen reads NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and shows Ch. 2 octave: -1. On the grid, (2,2) is lit on row 2 and (9,8) is lit on the bottom row. Channel 2 now plays pattern 2 an octave down, as MIDI 48 (C2) and 55 (G2) in the default C-major scale, and repeats every 16 steps like channel 1. The output you chose is on its Device page.

stages.title: Hear the two parts
stages.goal: Hear the bass under the phrase.
stages.action:
1. Tap Play (1,8).
2. Listen for two passes of 16 steps, about 5.3 s. Channel 1 plays C, C, C, D on beats 1 to 4. Channel 2 plays a low C on beat 1 and a low G on beat 3. The MIDI strip lists both channels' notes.
3. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.result: You hear the phrase above a two-note bass: C on beat 1 and G on beat 3. The strip shows channel 1 on port 1 (60, 60, 60 at velocity 80, 62 at 50) and channel 2 on port 2 (48 and 55 at velocity 100). Each channel keeps its own output, pattern and settings.

stages.title: Detour: add pattern 2 to channel 1
stages.goal: Hear why assigning a second pattern to a channel can remove a trig. This detour is optional and you undo it at the end. It edits channel 1 temporarily, so skip it if you would rather not touch the phrase. Merge modes has the full reference.
stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8), then (1,1) to select channel 1.
2. Tap (2,2) to assign pattern 2 as well as pattern 1. MERGE MODES shows Patterns 01 02 and the trig merge button (14,8) is on Skip, the default. Skip plays a step only if exactly one assigned pattern has a trig there. Patterns 1 and 2 both have trigs on steps 1 and 9, so those two go silent: on row 4 only steps 5 and 13 stay bright.
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop. Channel 1 plays only steps 5 and 13: one C and the D. The bass is unchanged.
stages.result: With Skip, channel 1 drops the overlapping steps 1 and 9 and plays only steps 5 and 13 (60 and 62 at velocity 50 in the MIDI strip).

stages.title: Press the merge button once
stages.goal: See the middle merge mode.
stages.action: Tap (14,8) once. The button cycles Skip, Only, All.
stages.result: MERGE MODES shows Strategy ONLY with the tooltip ONLY APPLIED, and the (14,8) button changes brightness. Only plays a step only when more than one assigned pattern has a trig there, so on row 4 just steps 1 and 9 stay bright. This example does not play it.

stages.title: Merge mode All
stages.goal: Hear that All keeps every trig.
stages.action:
1. Tap (14,8) once more: Strategy reads ALL. All plays a step if any assigned pattern has a trig there.
2. Tap Play, listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.result: All four trigs light on row 4 and return in the sound: C, C, C, D. The pitches and velocities come from channel 1's Note and Vel masks, whichever pattern's trig fires.

stages.title: Undo the detour
stages.goal: Take pattern 2 off channel 1 again.
stages.action:
1. Tap (2,2) to remove pattern 2 from channel 1.
2. Tap Play, listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
3. Optional: tap (14,8) until Strategy reads SKIP again. With one pattern the mode makes no difference, and chapter 7 works with either.
stages.result: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, C, C, C, D, and channel 2 keeps its bass (48 and 55). The merge Strategy stays on All until you tap (14,8) back to Skip.

learning_path.title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm
learning_path.goal: Move the whole piece from C major to D major by changing the scale, not the notes or the rhythm. A Note mask fixes a pitch whatever the scale says, so this chapter first removes the one you made in chapter 5.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 6, stopped, with the detour undone (channel 1 plays pattern 1 only; its merge Strategy may still read All, which changes nothing with one pattern). Masks override pattern notes, so channel 1's Note mask must be removed before the scale can change its pitch.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Channel 1's pattern 1 has degrees 0, 0, 0, 1 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13; its channel Note is X (no mask); step 13 keeps Vel 50; the defaults Vel 80 and Len 1/2 are kept. Channel 2 is unchanged. Scale slot 1, C major, is applied again.
learning_path.recovery: If the pitch does not follow the pattern, check that channel 1's Note is X and that step 13 has no Note mask before editing the pattern again. If the scale looks wrong, tap scale slot 1 at (1,3) and press K3 to return to C major.

stages.title: Let the pattern notes through
stages.goal: Remove the Note masks so the pattern and the scale decide the pitch.
stages.action:
1. On channel 1, open Masks (E1, E2, K3) if the NOTE MASKS page is not already open.
2. With no step held, turn E2 to Note and turn E3 left until it reads X. X means no mask: steps use the pattern's note through the scale.
3. Hold (13,4) and press K2. K2 clears every mask on the held step, Note and Vel together, so the Note 62 and the Vel 50 both go. Release (13,4).
4. Bring the quiet ending back, because K2 cannot clear the Note alone: turn E2 to Vel, hold (13,4), turn E3 left 30 detents until Vel reads 50 and release (13,4).
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X and Vel 80, the channel defaults. Step 13's own Vel 50 is not shown until you hold (13,4). No step has a Note mask now, so the next stage writes the melody into the pattern.

stages.title: Write the melody into the pattern
stages.goal: Make pattern 1 carry C, C, C, D as relative notes.
stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8) until the screen reads PATTERN NOTE and tap (1,1) to choose pattern 1. Row 7 is degree 0, the scale root; each row above is the next scale degree.
2. Tap (1,7), (5,7) and (9,7): degree 0 on steps 1, 5 and 9.
3. Tap (13,6): one row up is degree 1, the second scale note (D in C major), on step 13.
4. Tap Channel (3,8), tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.result: You hear C, C, C, D again, now from pattern notes read through the C-major scale: the MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62. The softer last note still comes from step 13's Vel mask on the channel.

stages.title: Add a second scale slot
stages.goal: Prepare a second scale without changing what plays.
stages.action:
1. Tap Scale (4,8) to open the scale page.
2. Tap (2,3), scale slot 2. A slot stores one scale; slot 2 holds C major, like slot 1, so nothing changes. Ignore the Degree and Transpose rows: they stay at I and 0 in this chapter.
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop. The phrase and bass sound as before: C, C, C, D above C, G.
stages.result: SCALE SLOT 02 opens with Scale Major. The MIDI strip still shows 60, 60, 60, 62 and 48, 55: still C major.

stages.title: Draft D major
stages.goal: Change the root of slot 2 without applying it yet.
stages.action:
1. Turn E2 to Root and turn E3 right two detents to D.
2. Turn E2 down to Scale and check that it reads Major.
The page shows the change as a draft with Press K3 to confirm. Until K3, playback keeps using the applied scale.
stages.result: SCALE SLOT 02 shows Root D and Scale Major as a draft, with Press K3 to confirm on screen. You still hear C major until you press K3.

stages.title: Apply D major
stages.goal: Hear the same rhythm transposed.
stages.action:
1. Press K3 to apply D major. The Press K3 to confirm line disappears: that is how you tell applied from draft.
2. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop. Channel 1 now plays D, D, D, E (MIDI 62, 62, 62, 64) and channel 2 plays D and A (MIDI 50 and 57). Rhythm and velocities are unchanged.
stages.result: The same rhythm sounds a whole tone higher in D major; the MIDI strip lists 62, 62, 62, 64 and 50, 57.

stages.title: Return to C major
stages.goal: Restore the arrangement scale so the next chapters match chapter 5.
stages.action:
1. Tap (1,3), scale slot 1, and press K3 to apply C major again.
2. Tap Play, listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop: C, C, C, D over C, G.
stages.result: SCALE SLOT 01 shows Root C and the MIDI strip is back on 60, 60, 60, 62 and 48, 55.

learning_path.title: 8. Add a pickup
learning_path.goal: Extend the phrase with a quiet extra note just before the loop restarts.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 7 in C major, stopped.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15; step 15 is degree 0; velocities are 80 on steps 1, 5 and 9, 50 on step 13 and 35 on step 15; channel 2 is unchanged; stopped.
learning_path.recovery: To go back to the four-beat phrase, tap (15,4) again in Pattern Trig to remove step 15.

stages.title: Add a late trig
stages.goal: Place a pickup note between the last beat and the next bar.
stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8) until the screen reads PATTERN TRIG and tap (1,1) for pattern 1.
2. Tap (15,4) to add a trig on step 15.
3. Tap Pattern (5,8) once to open PATTERN NOTE, then tap (15,7): degree 0, the root.
stages.result: PATTERN NOTE PAT01 shows the tooltip Step 15 note set to 0 and trig stripes on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15. A C pickup now sounds 1/3 s after beat 4 and 1/3 s before the bar restarts, halfway between the last beat and the next bar.

stages.title: Open Masks
stages.goal: Reach the Masks page, where a step can get its own velocity.
stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Masks and press K3.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X (the pattern notes decide pitch), Vel 80 and Len 1/2: the channel defaults the new trig uses until you give step 15 its own velocity.

stages.title: Make the pickup quiet
stages.goal: Shape the dynamics: main beats 80, ending 50, pickup 35.
stages.action:
1. Turn E2 to Vel.
2. Hold (15,4), the step you just added. While a step is held, the screen shows that step's own value. Turn E3 left 45 detents until Vel reads 35 (from 80), then release (15,4).
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.result: You hear three beats of C at velocity 80, the D at 50, and a very quiet C pickup at 35 just before the bar restarts; the MIDI strip lists velocity 35 for the step 15 note. After release the screen shows the channel default Vel 80 again. This version stays deterministic; probability and parameter slides are optional follow-up guides.

learning_path.title: 9. Arrange two sections
learning_path.goal: Alternate a bass-only section and the full two-part phrase.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 8 on slot 1, stopped. Song slots 2 and 3 are empty.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Slot 1 has channel 1 muted and channel 2 audible; slot 2 has both channels audible. Global length is 16 and Repeats is 1 on both slots; Song mode is On; slot 3 is empty; slot 1 is selected; stopped.
learning_path.recovery: Stop playback before you edit. Check the title row to see which slot you are editing: it reads SONG 01 or SONG 02. Copying a slot overwrites the target slot, and there is no undo.

stages.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2
stages.goal: Make a second section from the complete first section.
stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8). Slot 1 at (1,1) is the selected slot.
2. Hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1), then release slot 1. This copies the whole section (patterns, channel settings, masks and mutes) into slot 2 and overwrites what was there.
3. Tap (2,1) to select slot 2. The title row reads SONG 02.
stages.result: Slot 2 holds the same phrase, bass and settings as slot 1. The screen reads SLOT SETUP, SONG 02, the tooltip says Song sequence 2 selected, and (2,1) is the bright slot button.

stages.title: Mute channel 1 in slot 1
stages.goal: Make slot 1 a bass-only section.
stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8) and tap (1,1) to select slot 1.
2. Tap Channel (3,8). Hold K1, the shift key from chapter 1, tap (1,1), then release K1. K1 plus a channel button mutes that channel in the selected slot only.
stages.result: The title row shows CH01 MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 muted. Slot 1 will play the bass alone.

stages.title: Check that slot 2 stays full
stages.goal: Confirm slot 2 keeps the full phrase.
stages.action: Tap Song (6,8), tap (2,1) to select slot 2, then tap Channel (3,8).
stages.result: The title reads CH01 S02 with no MUTE: channel 1 is audible in slot 2. Slot 1 plays the bass alone; slot 2 plays the bass, the phrase and the pickup.

stages.title: Set slot 1 to one 16-step bar
stages.goal: Make slot 1 one bar long. Global length is how many steps a section lasts before the song moves on; a slot starts at 64.
stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8) and tap (1,1) to select slot 1. Playback is stopped.
2. The length fader is row 7, columns 1 to 8. (1,7) subtracts one step and (8,7) adds one. The inner buttons jump to coarse values: (2,7) 1, (3,7) 13, (4,7) 32, (5,7) 38, (6,7) 51 and (7,7) 64. Tap (3,7) to jump to 13.
3. Tap (8,7) three times: 13 + 3 = 16.
stages.result: SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 01 shows Global length 16. Song mode reads AUTO there, which means Song mode is on and advancing.

stages.title: Set slot 2 to one 16-step bar
stages.goal: Make slot 2 one bar long too, so the song alternates every 2.7 s.
stages.action: Tap (2,1) for slot 2 and repeat the fader taps: (3,7), then (8,7) three times.
stages.result: SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 02 shows Global length 16.

stages.title: Optional: check Repeats and Song mode
stages.goal: Confirm two settings that are already right by default. Skip this stage if you like.
stages.action:
1. Turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Slot setup and press K3. With slot 1 selected, check that Repeats reads 1; with slot 2 selected, check it again.
2. For slot 2, turn E2 to Song mode. It should read On, the default. If it reads Off, turn E3 to On and press K3.
3. Leave slot 3 empty and select slot 1.
stages.result: Slots 1 and 2 form one chain: each plays 16 steps once. After slot 2 the song wraps to slot 1, because slot 3 is empty. The Slot setup screen shows Repeats 1 and Song mode On for SONG 02.

stages.title: Hear the arrangement
stages.goal: Hear the two sections alternate.
stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8) and tap (1,1) to select slot 1.
2. Tap Play (1,8). Listen for four sections of 16 steps, about 10.7 s. The MIDI strip lists the notes: the bass (port 2) in every section and the phrase (port 1) only in the slot 2 sections.
3. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.result: You hear the bass alone, then the bass with the phrase and pickup, then the bass alone, then the bass with the phrase. The screen returns to SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 once you stop.

learning_path.title: 10. Save, reload and perform
learning_path.goal: Save the arrangement under a name, reload it and play it back.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 9, stopped, with slot 1 selected.
learning_path.outgoing_state: The saved project Four notes contains both sections and restores their playback exactly. Playback is stopped and no note is held.
learning_path.recovery: K2 cancels the Load dialog without replacing the current project. Keep the saved name Four notes until you have finished the optional follow-ups.

stages.title: Open Save project
stages.goal: Reach the save command in the norns menu.
stages.action:
1. Stop playback. Tap K1 briefly to open the norns system menu.
2. Turn E1 to PARAMS and press K3, open MOSAIC and turn E2 to < Save project.
stages.result: The norns menu shows Pattern project management with Save project selected.

stages.title: Save the arrangement
stages.goal: Store the project under a name so autosave cannot replace it.
stages.action:
1. Press K3 on < Save project. The norns text entry screen opens with the suggested name new.
2. Press K3 on DEL to delete the old name, then turn E2 to each character of Four notes and press K3 to enter it. Confirm the name when it is complete.
3. Tap K1 to return to Mosaic.
stages.result: Saving writes the project files Four notes.ptn and Four notes.pset. Mosaic's own screen does not change; it still shows SLOT SETUP, SONG 01.

stages.title: Make an unsaved change
stages.goal: Change something you will not save, so the reload has something to undo.
stages.action: Tap Channel (3,8). Hold K1, tap (1,1) and release K1. This unmutes channel 1 in slot 1: a deliberate change you have not saved.
stages.result: The title row reads CH01 with no MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 unmuted.

stages.title: Open Load project
stages.goal: Reach the load command.
stages.action: With playback stopped, tap K1, open PARAMS, then MOSAIC, and turn E2 to > Load project. K2 cancels the dialog.
stages.result: The norns menu shows Load project selected.

stages.title: Reload to check the saved version
stages.goal: See that loading brings back the saved arrangement.
stages.action:
1. Press K3 on > Load project, turn E2 to Four notes in the file list and press K3.
2. Tap K1 to return to Mosaic and tap Channel (3,8).
stages.result: Slot 1 is bass alone again: the title row shows CH01 MUTE and the unsaved change is gone.

stages.title: Replay the restored sections
stages.goal: Hear that the loaded project plays the same arrangement.
stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8) and tap (1,1) to select slot 1.
2. Tap Play (1,8), listen for four sections (about 10.7 s), then tap Play to stop.
stages.result: You hear bass alone, bass with the phrase, bass alone, bass with the phrase, as before the save; the MIDI strip lists the same notes as chapter 9. Next you can follow the merge, recording or modulation task guides; keep the saved Four notes project unchanged while you try them.
